They will also play an active role in developing and improving healthcare services for a diverse patient population, including practice-based commissioning, patient participation and health promotion initiatives.

The postholder will be closely supported by both the clinical and management teams within the practice and will be part of a wider multi-site clinical team. While the main base will be at Esher Green Surgery, there may be opportunities to deliver triage and on-site clinical sessions at other Bourne Health GP Practices.

We appreciate the interest of all applicants in this opportunity. Please note that we may close this vacancy early if we identify a suitable candidate before the advertised closing date. We encourage interested applicants to submit their applications as soon as possible.

In accordance with the practice timetable, as agreed, the post-holder will make themselves available to undertake clinical sessions. A clinical session is normally composed of face-to-face appointments together with telephone appointments, followed by a variety of duties including queries, visiting patients at home, checking and signing repeat prescriptions, actioning test results, medical reports, and examinations (e.g. Insurance Companies) on behalf of the Practice. The above duties should be performed in a timely manner. Appointments will be 10 minutes duration.

Bourne Health is the largest primary care provider in South West London, serving diverse communities across multiple GP surgeries. We are committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care, underpinned by innovation, community engagement, and operational excellence.

title: Salaried General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a friendly enthusiastic salaried GP to join our friendly practice. This position is available due to the reduction in sessions of our long standing senior partner in July 2027 and we wish to give ourselves plenty of time to find the right candidate.

We have a patient list size of 8100 in rural Oxfordshire, Main site at Bloxham with branch surgery at Hook Norton.

We have a full compliment of clinical staff who work closely together to support the practice needs.

We do not operate total triage at the practice. Our focus is to accommodate our patients on a daily basis with the options of either a face to face appointment or a telephone consultation depending on which option a patient has chosen.

We have open sessions in the morning with pre-booked appointments in the afternoon.

We have 15 slots in the morning and 12 slots in the afternoon.

You will be supported by a full compliment of nursing to support GP's over both sites. The team consists of 3 nurses, 2 health care assistants and 1 phlebotomist who is trained to do paediatric bloods.

You will be required to work at our branch surgery which is approximately 5 miles away from our main surgery site.

We have 1 private nursing home situated at the end of our driveway for which we cover 1 clinic session per week for their registered clients.

Your contract will be based on the BMA standard contract.

We are a traditional practice with a strong team work ethic to provide a highest possible standard of care for our patients.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
An opportunity has arisen for a Salaried GP or Partner position at The Denmead Practice. We are looking for an enthusiastic, committed GP to join our experienced and dedicated team.

We are a well-established Practice situated in Denmead, Hampshire with easy access to the motorway and the South Downs National Park. The team has an excellent skill mix whereby the GPs and Nursing team work closely together to provide first-rate patient access.

The role consists of 4 sessions worked over 3 day; Tuesday AM, Wednesday all day and Friday PM.

The salary is competetive, and dependent on experience. Informal visits to the Practice are welcome

The ideal candidate will have experience in General Practice and will work collaboratively with the whole practice team to deliver an excellent experience that meets the needs of the patients.

You will hold your own patient list as we believe that continuity of care is important for both the patient and the doctor,

You will be responsible for the complete patient journey, from consultation through to all the associated admin that accompanies them. You will apply critical thinking and practices within professional boundaries, be proactive and a driver for change, assist in the training, development and clinical supervision of practice personnel and medical students.

Youbwill be required to undertake one duty session per week.

A buddy system applies and you will cover a nominated GP's pathology and urgent admin when on leave, and vice versa.

We are part of Havant and Waterlooville PCN, our Home visiting team will ensure most home visits are covered, however where not applicable or there is no capcaity, you will be responsible for visiting your housebound patients when required.

Adhere to policies and procedures and provide guidance to the practice team as required.

4 GP partners 10,500 patients 2 part-time Salaried GPs 1 Advanced Nurse Practitioners 3 Practice Nurses 3 Health Care Assistants

1 Phlebotomist Excellent Administration and Reception Team

Various attached staff employed through the PCN including Clinical Pharmacists, Dementia advisors, Health and well being coaches, Social Prescribers, First Contact Practitioners, Mental Health Advisors and a newly established Aging Well team.

We are an EMIS Web practice, using various IT software including eConsult, Accurx, Anima and Medlink and run personal GP lists to enable continuity of care.

Our reputation is very important to us. We pride ourselves on our consistent posisitve feedback from our patients and peers working as a team to deliver the best care possible within the resources we have.

employer: North Cumbria Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Gastroenterologist
descriptionHtml:
North Cumbria Integrated Care is looking for a dynamic and motivated Consultant gastroenterologist to join our team of consultant gastroenterologists and gastrointestinal surgeons to provide an integrated digestive diseases service across north Cumbria. The North Cumbria GI Service is a new, cohesive and integrated department, combining the services of gastroenterology and endoscopy, upper gastrointestinal, hepatobiliary, colorectal, emergency GI surgery.

The successful candidate will join a team of gastroenterologists supported by nurse specialists in IBD & hepatology across the Trust. Associated with the transformation of all our services across the Trust, and in conjunction with the introduction of our model for acute medical care, it is envisaged that future configurations will focus complex in patient work at the Carlisle site, and elective outpatient services (endoscopy and outpatient clinics) will be provided by all of the team across the Trust. Sub specialty interest will be encouraged where this contributes to and complements the department and Trusts' service needs.

Please note: You must be on the Specialist Register in order to be eligible for appointment to this level of post.

The department has two dedicated GI wards within the Cumberland Infirmary at Carlisle for the treatment of inpatients. The plan in the near future is to have all GI areas co-located. There is a dedicated 4-room endoscopy unit at The Cumberland Infirmary and the new endoscopy unit at West Cumberland Hospital, Whitehaven has 2 dedicated rooms in a new, state of the art facility. There is a specialist GI physiology lab on both sites.

We currently provide a consultant of the week service for our in patients, a 24/7 GI bleed rota as well as specialist services in IBD, Hepatology, HPB, Bowel Cancer screening and complex polypectomy. Endoscopy services, are provided across our two acute sites in Carlisle and Whitehaven. A full range of diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, including ERCP, are available. Our new £15M, 5 room, State of the Art, JAG accredited Endoscopy Suite opened in March 2025.

At NCIC, we have an ambition to deliver outstanding healthcare services to the population of North Cumbria. The Trust is committed to creating a centre of excellence in providing rural and remote healthcare and provides a wide range of community and acute services throughout our county.

Our 5 key principles demonstrate our belief in the delivery of 'safe, high quality care every time':

Being a clinically led organisation

Quality and safety at the heart of our Trust

A positive patient experience every time

A great place to work

Managing our money well

As an organisation we are serious about supporting a diverse workforce that reflects our local community and are very much focused on being an inclusive and compassionate place to work.

Across the North East and North Cumbria we are working together to deliver our ambition to be the greenest region in England by 2030. All staff are expected to support sustainability.

title: Consultant in Rehabilitation Medicine (Neuro & Spinal Rehab)
descriptionHtml:
Akessa Healthcare is seeking to appoint a Consultant Neurologist to lead the development of outpatient Neurological services, as well as support the ongoing treatment and rehabilitation of our neuro and spinal patients.

In this role the appointee is expected to provide comprehensive care for private patients. The appointment is based at two sites, The main base, with both outpatient and inpatient care, is based at the Royal Buckinghamshire Hospital in Aylesbury . Outpatient clinics will also be provided at The New Foscote Hospital in Banbury.

The appointee will be provided with luxurious facility, caring environment, ample time and administrative support to deliver world class care.

As a senior colleague, the post-holder will work in close co-operation with, and support, other clinical, medical professional and managerial colleagues in providing high quality healthcare to our patients.

The successful candidate will be assigned appropriate secretarial support to clinical work and diary management.

Duties and responsibilities:

  • Lead on the development of Neuro-Spinal services.
  • Deliver high-quality care for all patients and support the smooth running of the service.
  • Support efficient management of resources and maintenance of our short waiting lists for private and insured patients.
  • Take ownership in the successful performance against key performance indicators, ensuring zero compromise to the quality of care or clinical excellence for patients.
  • In collaboration with department leads, maintain and develop quality standards and improvement throughout the department and in line with any relevant accreditation requirements.
  • Provide on-site clinical expertise as and when needed, supporting MDTs as required.
  • Essential requirements:
  • CCT in Neurology or Rehabilitation Medicine
  • Full GMC Registration.
  • Inclusion in the GMC Specialist Register in Neurology or Rehabilitation Medicine.
  • Currently employed, or has previously held substantive NHS consultant post.
  • Eligible to register with private medical insurance companies (BUPA, AXA-PPP etc).
  • Able to take responsibility for delivering the service without direct supervision.

The Akessa Healthcare Group is managed and run by clinicians. We are proud to be part of a highly skilled, diverse team.

The New Foscote Hospital was established in Banbury over 40 years ago and has provided services and treatments to thousands of people from across the region. We have over 50 consultants, all of whom are leaders in their specialist fields and choose to hold their private practices here, working alongside our friendly, highly qualified and experienced nursing and support teams.

The Royal Buckinghamshire Hospital was established in Aylesbury in 1832 and has provided services and treatments to thousands of people from across the region. The ownership of the hospital was transferred to our new management team in January 2023. By joining our existing portfolio, the hospital is now run professionally and provides clinical care to private, insured and NHS patients, with a strong ethos on caring for our staff.

Significant ongoing investment into both hospitals includes complete refurbishment of the wards, the outpatient area, reception, staff facilities, radiology and the construction of additional state-of-the-art operating theatres and endoscopy suites.

With the expansion of the Group this is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Consultant Neurologist to join our growing team to provide clinical excellence for our patients at both hospitals.

title: General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
Irchester Surgery is a friendly, community-focused GP practice based in Irchester, Wellingborough, working in close partnership with Summerlee Medical Centre in Finedon.

We are seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Salaried GP to join our team for 4-6 sessions per week. This is an excellent opportunity to work across both practice sites within a well-established and supportive environment where continuity of care, teamwork and high clinical standards are at the heart of everything we do.

Irchester Surgery has a registered patient population of approximately 4,100. The practice is supported by a small, friendly team comprising two GPs and four experienced members of the nursing team, alongside our administrative staff.

title: Locum Consultant in Clinical Immunology and Allergy
descriptionHtml:
This advert is for a 1.0WTE Consultant in Allergy based at Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust (QMC Campus).

This appointment will be on the terms and conditions of the extant NHS Consultant contract. The contract is for a fixed 12 month period.

The successful candidate will be on the Full and Specialist Register of the GMC or be eligible for registration within six months of interview. It is expected that the appointee will hold Fellowship of the Royal College of Physicians (FRCP) or Pathologists (FRCPath).

The appointee, in collaboration with the other consultants, will be expected to fulfil the duties within the agreed Job Plan.

Summary of Duties:

  1. participation in the provision of a clinical service in the diagnosis and management of patients with allergic disease. This may occasionally require review of individual patients on the wards or discussion with colleagues outside NUH, for example in other Trusts or in primary care.
  2. cover for colleagues' annual leave and other authorised absences.
  3. professional supervision and management of junior medical staff, nursing staff, specialist pharmacist, dietitian, STPs and clinical scientists where required
  4. responsibility for carrying out teaching, examination and accreditation duties as required and for contributing to undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing medical education activity locally and nationally.
  5. participating in medical audit, the Trust's Clinical Governance processes and in CPD.
  6. involvement in research, as appropriate to job plan
  7. a willingness to undertake additional professional responsibilities at local, regional, or national levels.
  8. the post holder must at all times carry out their duties with due regard to the Trust's Equal Opportunities Policy.

Every day, our teams at Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust (NUH) make a difference. We save lives, we improve lives, and we usher in new life. We are proud to play a central role in supporting the health and wellbeing of people in Nottingham, Nottinghamshire and our surrounding communities.

With more than 20,000 colleagues, we are the largest employer in Nottinghamshire and one of the biggest and busiest NHS Trusts in the country, serving more than 2.5m residents of Nottingham and Nottinghamshire and a further four million people across the East Midlands and beyond. Our Trust spans over three sites including Queen's Medical Centre (QMC), Nottingham City Hospital and Ropewalk House.

We provide a range of national and internationally renowned specialist services, and we are at the forefront of new surgical procedures and research programmes.

We are home to the East Midlands Major Trauma Centre, the Nottingham Children's Hospital and in partnership with the University of Nottingham we host a Biomedical Research Centre carrying out vital research into hearing, digestive diseases, respiratory, musculoskeletal disease, mental health and imaging.

As a teaching hospital, we are instrumental in the education and training of doctors, nurses and other healthcare professionals. We are proud of our strong relationships with universities across the East Midlands, including the University of Nottingham, Nottingham Trent University and Loughborough University.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Salaried GP up to 8 sessions - Full-time or Part-time (up to 8 sessions per week but must be available to work Fridays)

We are a thriving; innovative and passionate training practice and an opportunity has arisen for a like minded individual to join our friendly team. We boast a plethora of experience within the extensive clinical team including GPs, Nurses, allied health professionals and trainees. Every salaried GP is paired with a dedicated GP Partner mentor. We place a strong emphasis on mutual support and professional growth. We are proud to lead on several pioneering projects, such as our nationally recognised Dermatology Drive Through Service and the Cancer Quality Care Project.

Whether you're newly qualified or an experience GP, we offer a supportive, collaborative, and inspiring environment to thrive in. We would like to invite you to be part of the Ringmead Team and share our attitude of enjoying our work and maintaining a work life balance whilst providing high quality care to our community.

Key Benefits

  • Training practice with lots of opportunity for professional growth
  • Private Healthcare provided for all clinicians
  • 7 weeks leave (6 annual and 1 study leave)
  • Birthday day off in addition to annual leave
  • Protected daily Clinician coffee break
  • Weekly in-house training and education sessions
  • Support for GP Fellowship via Frimley Training Hub
  • GP Partner mentor provided
  • Indemnity cover funded
  • Low home visit rate, as in house paramedics and community home visiting service
  • Provider of community clinics for Dermatology, minor surgery and joint injections
  • Community Women's health service with LARC, polyp removal
  • Innovative use of technology with AI triage and Robot automation of results and prescriptions

Ringmead is a 5-site training practice looking after approximately 40,000 patients across Bracknell, Crowthorne, Sandhurst and Owlsmoor. As well as delivering excellent primary care, we are fortunate in having clinicians with expertise in cardiology, haematology, palliative care, immunology, dermatology, minor surgery, joint injections, LARCs and frailty. There is a strong ethos on supporting one another, as well as on education. We offer protected educational and clinical meetings several times a month and mentor ST and FY doctors, medical students, nursing students and pharmacy students. We are also highly active within our ICB, Federation and PCN (The Health Triangle) with 2 of our Partners being the Clinical Directors.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Windrush Medical Practice is seeking a Salaried GP to join our established and highly regarded team.

We are a large, GP-owned practice serving over 21,000 patients in West Oxfordshire, with a longstanding commitment to high-quality, patient-centred care. Our model is built around continuity, collaboration and providing clinicians with the time and support needed to practise medicine to a high standard.

We are looking for an enthusiastic salaried GP to work 4 - 6who shares our commitment to delivering excellent patient care and values working as part of a supportive and engaged clinical team.

Whether you are an experienced GP or looking for your next long-term post, we offer an environment where clinicians can develop professionally while maintaining a sustainable and rewarding career in general practice.

The duties of the post are to provide a full range of general medical services as contained in accordance with the associated job plan.

The post holder is expected to support the partners in providing all services outlined in the GMS contract and also in the aims and objectives of the practice.

You will be expected to support and input into the aims of the practice in areas of clinical governance, good practice, QOF, Enhanced Services, Practice Audit, referral review and any other improvement areas as determined by the practice.

You will be encouraged to utilise and develop any skills for improvement of services to patients.

You are expected to maintain and keep good standards of good clinical records at all times.

Full involvement in any practice training and on-going requirements.

You are expected to maintain and keep good standards of paperwork.

You will be required to attend and participate in Practice Meetings.

Practitioners will be required to comply with the requirement of NHS Appraisal and re validation as may from time to time apply. You will have a personal appraisal with the practice manager at least on an annual basis which will provide the opportunity to review your job plan.

Confidentiality - you must strictly adhere to the applicable GMS Guidance on Patient Confidentiality

Windrush is an Outstanding-rated practice with a strong reputation for clinical quality, education and innovation. We are a training practice with undergraduate teaching, active involvement in primary care research, and well-established multidisciplinary services including pharmacists, prescribing nurses and ECP-led clinics.

Located on the edge of the Cotswolds and just 13 miles from Oxford, the practice benefits from close links with adjacent community services, diagnostics and secondary care facilities.

We are proud to offer:

  • 15-minute GP appointments
  • Allocated daily administration time
  • First-line document management by trained Practice Assistants
  • An experienced and supportive multidisciplinary team
  • Regular clinical meetings and peer support
  • Mentoring for clinicians new to the practice
  • Opportunities to contribute to teaching and research
  • A collaborative and forward-thinking practice culture

title: GP Maternity Locum
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a fixed term GP at any stage of their career to join our team at Bersted Green Surgery covering maternity leave starting December 2026.

5 - 7 sessions per week , Tuesday - Friday.

15 minute appointments . Standard clinic is 13 patients per session , with a mix of telephone and face to face appointments.

4 GP Partners, 5 salaried GPs . Supported by a friendly team of Paramedics, Practice Nurses, Pharmacy Team, Care coordinators , Mental Health Social Prescriber, First Contact Physiotherapist, Youth Emotional Support Workers.

Majority of home visits covered by the Paramedic Team.

You will be expected to undertake all the normal duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care.

Duty sessions shared out between all Doctors .

Bersted Green Surgery is a dedicated, forward-thinking and busy Teaching Practice, looking after over 13,000 patients.

We are located in the delightful seaside town of Bognor Regis, renowned for its sunny climate on the south-coast, near Chichester and at the foot of the South Downs National Park.

We pride ourselves on being an exceptionally friendly place to work with an emphasis on team-working in a supportive environment, with a true focus on work life balance and wellbeing.

As a training practice and a hub for research we are committed to fostering the next generation of healthcare professionals , hosting medical students, FY2 and ST1 , ST2 , ST3 Trainees.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a caring, motivated and team-minded salaried GP to join our friendly, well-established training practice. The post is for 4 sessions per week, available from November 2026. The role is a replacement for a colleague who is emigrating, so you would be joining a stable and supportive team.

Clinical work

Contributing to clinical audit quality improvement significant event analysis and complaint review

Maintaining your own continuing professional development annual appraisal and revalidation

About the Practice

List size of approximately eight thousand five hundred patients situated in centre of Warrington

Care quality commission rating Good

Training practice with general practice registrars vocational training scheme and foundation year doctors

Member of our primary care network and participating in the primary care network directed enhanced service and additional roles reimbursement scheme staff

Clinical team of four general practice partners three salaried general practitioners and two practice nurses

Access to an acute visiting service for some home visits

Practice offers womens health including coils and implants

Enhanced Access sessions on Tuesdays participation may be required and this is open to negotiation

Participates in research projects

employer: Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board
title: Consultant Haematologist
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Consultant Haematologist to join a friendly and enthusiastic team at Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board. Whilst this appointment is a Health Board wide appointment, this post will be based at Prince Charles Hospital.

Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board is one of the largest Health Boards in Wales and was formed in 2019. It is situated near of the vibrant cities of Cardiff, Swansea and Bristol and is enriched with magnificent scenery including beautiful beaches and the stunning Brecon Beacons national park. Welsh history, culture, music and of course rugby lie at the heart of the Health Board.

Proposed Interview date: September 9th 2026

Welsh and/or English speakers are equally welcome to apply.

The post requires malignant and general haematological work. Candidates with any field of interest are encouraged to apply. However, it is desirable to have an interest and experience in haematological malignancy and chemotherapy. The work will be shared equally with the other consultants to provide clinical, laboratory, liaison haematology service and on call. The development of a special interest by the appointee is encouraged and would be in line with the clinical interest of the Health Board.

The haematology department at Cwm Taf Morgannwg UHB is also undergoing an exciting piece oftransformation work. This will lend itself to sub-specialisation and expansion and further development of all levels of the medical and nursing structure within the haematology service. Development and expansion of Advanced Nurse Practitioner, Clinical Nurse Specialist, Consultant Nurse, and Clinical Scientist posts are all being explored as a part of this on-going and dynamic work. Collaborative work with neighbouring health boards and trusts is also being explored.

The Cwm Taf Morgannwg UHB Haematology service, whilst performing BCSH level 2 Haematology, has close links with the regional Haematology and BMT centre based in the University Hospital of Wales, Cardiff,

Potential applicants are encouraged to visit and to meet the current team and consultants.

Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board is part of the NHS Wales family. Our Health Board provides primary, secondary and community health and wellbeing services to around 450,000 people living in three County Boroughs: Bridgend Merthyr Tydfil, and Rhondda Cynon Taf.

We live by our core values:

  • We listen, learn and improve
  • We treat everyone with respect
  • We all work together as one team

We are a proud local employer; around 80% of our 15000 workforce live within our region, making our staff not only our lifeblood of our organisation but of the diverse communities that we serve.

title: Salaried GP - Stourport Medical Centre
descriptionHtml:
Salaried GP Up to 6 Sessions

Stourport Medical Centre | Wyre Forest Health Partnership

Looking for a General Practice role where you can enjoy medicine, develop your career and achieve a healthy work-life balance? We'd love to welcome you to the Stourport Medical Centre.

As one of five practices within one of Worcestershire's largest GP partnerships, at Stourport Medical Centre we provide care to approximately 22,000 patients. We combine the stability, opportunities, and support of a large organisation with the welcoming, friendly atmosphere of small local practice.

When you join us, you'll benefit from:

  • Modern, purpose-built, air-conditioned practice
  • Supportive and experienced GP and multidisciplinary team
  • Flexible working opportunities
  • Excellent work-life balance
  • Opportunities to develop clinical, educational and leadership interests
  • A welcoming culture where your ideas and well being matter
  • The chance to help shape the future of primary care

Whether you're newly qualified or an experienced GP, we'll support you to build a rewarding and enjoyable career.

You'll provide high-quality, patient-centred care within a well-supported clinical environment, allowing you to focus on delivering excellent General Practice.

We offer:

  • Routine sessions capped at 14 patient contacts
  • GP home visits by clinical exception only. Our dedicated Visiting ANP team undertakes the majority of home visits, with any GP visits scheduled within protected visiting appointment slots during the working day.
  • Experienced Triage GPs ensuring booked appointments are GP appropriate
  • Innovative back-office support reducing routine administrative workload
  • Multidisciplinary team including Pharmacists, First Contact Physiotherapists and Care Coordinators
  • Structured induction tailored to your experience
  • Regular educational meetings and clinical supervision
  • Partnership-funded salaried GP educational away days
  • Six weeks' annual leave plus bank holidays
  • One week's paid study leave each year
  • Salary from £10,500 per session, depending on experience
  • MDU indemnity reimbursement
  • Laptop provided
  • Funded appraisal and revalidation portfolio
  • Opportunities for teaching, research, quality improvement and leadership

Our experienced practice management and Head Office teams work alongside clinicians to provide the support you need to thrive professionally and personally.

Wyre Forest Health Partnership is one of Worcestershire's largest GP partnerships, caring for approximately 73,000 patients across five practices with a team of around 360 colleagues, including more than 50 GPs. By working at scale, we've created the opportunities and support of a larger organisation while keeping the friendly, collaborative feel of local General Practice.

We're proud to invest in our people. You'll be joining a supportive multidisciplinary team, backed by experienced practice managers, a dedicated Head Office and wellbeing team, and colleagues who genuinely enjoy working together. Whether you're interested in developing a specialist clinical interest, teaching, research, leadership or a portfolio career, we'll help you achieve your ambitions.

Stourport Medical Centre is modern, purpose-built and air-conditioned, with free on-site parking, secure cycle storage, shower facilities, complimentary tea and coffee, and regular social events that help build strong relationships across the Partnership.

Above all, we're committed to creating an environment where GPs can thrive. We continually invest in innovation, education and service improvement, while supporting flexible ways of working that enable our colleagues to provide outstanding care and enjoy a rewarding career. We're also proud to support the NHS ambition to achieve net zero and encourage colleagues to contribute to sustainable healthcare.

employer: The Hillingdon Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Neurological Rehabilitation
descriptionHtml:
This post consists of 10 Programmed Activities (PAs), annualized as 8.5 Direct Clinical Care (DCC) and 1.5 Supporting Clinical Activities (SPA). This is an appointment by the Hillingdon Hospital NHS Foundation Trust with license to attend at Imperial College NHS Trust. The post holder must hold full MRCP and a certificate of completion of training (CCT) in Rehabilitation Medicine. We welcome application from trainees in Rehabilitation Medicine who are approximately 6 months from CCT.

The appointee will join two consultants in Rehabilitation Medicine and a team of neurologists as part of a friendly and reputable service that works across Hillingdon Hospital and Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust to provide seamless transition for patients from tertiary care into secondary care and community services. This post provides an excellent opportunity to provide high quality neurological rehabilitation care for patients with spinal cord injury, in a busy District General Hospital or in a tertiary setting at Imperial. 6 of the DCC PA's will be based at the Hillingdon site and 4 PA's will be based primarily at Imperial.

The post holder will provide consultant input to the London Spinal Cord Injury Network and the Major Trauma Network in North West London. The post holder will be responsible for improving the care of spinal cord injury patients needing rehabilitation in the North West London sector. There is scope to develop integrated care across secondary and community services in partnership NW London ICB. This will involve linking with community teams and outreach visits to community settings.

The Hillingdon Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is the only acute Hospital in the London Borough of Hillingdon and offers a wide range of services including accident and emergency, inpatient care, day surgery, outpatient clinics and maternity services. The Trust's services at Mount Vernon Hospital include routine day surgery, delivered at a modern treatment centre, a minor injuries unit and outpatient clinics.

The safety and well-being of our patients and of our staff is paramount and we are making urgent improvements to address this - particularly in infection prevention and control. We are making progress and going forward by working in partnership with local GPs, charities,community services, academic partners, our local authority, neighbouring hospitals and the wider North West London Integrated care system, and ensuring that we listen and work in partnership with our local population. We are absolutely focused on ensuring that our hospitalsprovide high quality, safe and compassionate care, while drive forward the building of the new Hillingdon Hospital.

We have over 3,500 members of staff that are proud to care for nearly half a million people, with a vision to be an outstanding provider of healthcare through leading health and academic partnerships, transforming services, to provide the best care where needed.

title: General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
Join a progressive Brighton & Hove practice as we prepare to launch a new organisation in January 2027, with a rebrand & new management.

Bring your ideas. Develop your interests. Help build a modern, supportive approach to general practice, with compassionate care & staff wellbeing at its heart.

THE PRACTICAL BITS

Designed around you.

15-minute routine appointments: time to consult properly.

Non-duty clinical sessions: 12 appointments, plus 10 minutes for admin.

One paid admin session weekly, with the option to work from home.

Pro-rata duty rota managing online requests; infrequent home visits.

SystmOne and Accurx Triage, supported by pharmacy and multidisciplinary teams.

BMA contract on GMS terms.

SUPPORT TO DEVELOP

Mentoring, CPD and opportunities to develop clinical interests or contribute to education, service development and leadership.

A DIVERSE COMMUNITY. A STRONG TEAM.

Around 25,500 patients across three sites in Brighton, Hove and Portslade.

Pharmacy, paramedic and nursing colleagues support our work. Training is provided for working with neurodiverse, trans, non-binary and intersex patients.

WHO WERE LOOKING FOR

Full GMC registration; MRCGP or equivalent; general practice experience; safe clinical judgement; a collaborative, inclusive approach; and commitment to CPD, safeguarding and clinical governance. UK work eligibility and ability to work across all three sites are essential.

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and can discuss reasonable adjustments during recruitment.

As a GP, your clinical responsibilities include conducting surgery and telephone consultations, managing queries, home visits, repeat prescriptions, and timely correspondence. You will make autonomous decisions for self-referred and referred patients, assess undiagnosed health concerns, screen for disease risks, provide counselling, and deliver health education. You will admit or discharge patients, refer to other care providers, and ensure consultation notes and data meet agreed standards. Responsibilities include issuing computer-generated prescriptions, adhering to the Practice prescribing formulary, and fulfilling duties expected of a GP in primary care.

Organisational responsibilities involve participating in developing and delivering new services and care models, adhering to Practice policies (e.g., prescribing, confidentiality, data protection), and committing to ongoing learning and evidence-based best practices. You will contribute to Enhanced Services, QOF/IIF initiatives, audits, and clinical standard setting. title: Medical Examiner
descriptionHtml:
This post has been created by the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) in response to observations made in the Third Report of the Shipman Inquiry. The introduction of the Medical Examiner system will promote robust, transparent and independent scrutiny of death certification processes.

Medical Examiners are appropriately trained doctors who will verify clinical information on Medical Certificates of Cause of Death (MCCDs) and ensure that the right referrals are made to the Coroner for further investigation. MEs will take a consistent approach to the formulation of MCCD content, which must be clinically accurate and reflect any discussions with the next of kin / informant. MEs must not have been involved in the care of the deceased patients for deaths they scrutinise.

The Rotherham NHS Foundation Trusts Medical Examiner should be a practising medical practitioner who has been on the General Medical Council register for a minimum of 5 years post-registration. The Medical Examiner will be appointed by the Executive Medical Director and the Trusts Lead Medical Examiner, supported by HM Coroner.

The Rotherham NHS Foundation Trust (TRFT) is a combined acute and community Trust serving our local population of around 270,000 people. Our vision is to always act the right way and be proud to provide exceptional healthcare to the communities of Rotherham.

title: Care Coordinator (PCN)
descriptionHtml:
At North Liverpool Primary Care Network, we pride ourselves on being a forward-thinking organisation that embraces innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement. Working within our Care Coordinator team, you will thrive in a fast-paced environment where no two days are the same. You will play a pivotal role in supporting patients to access the right services at the right time, helping to improve outcomes and patient experience across our network.

As a key member of the team, you will also act as an ambassador for the work of the PCN, helping to showcase our services, successes and community impact through social media and digital engagement. You will be the link between our teams, patients and wider stakeholders, promoting the valuable work taking place across the network and ensuring our achievements are shared with the communities we serve.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is proactive, organised and passionate about making a difference, with the ability to build strong relationships, adapt to changing priorities and contribute to the continued development of innovative primary care services.

Why join us?

Be part of a progressive and supportive PCN focused on improving patient care.

Work in a varied and dynamic role with opportunities to develop new skills.

Help shape and promote innovative services that make a real difference to local communities.

Join a team that values collaboration, creativity and continuous improvement.

This role offers the opportunity to be at the heart of Primary Care Network development, supporting projects that make a real difference to patients, practices and the wider community. With a varied workload and no two days the same, it is ideal for someone who enjoys building relationships and contributing to innovative healthcare services.

As a Care Coordinator, you will work with PCN leaders, practice teams and partner organisations to improve patient care and access to services. You will support patients with personalised care needs, helping them navigate health and community services and access the right support at the right time.

You will help promote the work of the PCN through social media, patient engagement activities and health campaigns, raising awareness of local services, screening programmes, immunisations and wellbeing initiatives. You will also support the Patient Participation Group, gather patient feedback and contribute to service improvements.

Working closely with the PCN Manager, Clinical Director and partner organisations, you will support quality improvement projects, audits and healthcare programmes while developing partnerships that enhance integrated patient care.

This is an exciting opportunity for a proactive and organised individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and wants to play a key role in improving health outcomes across North Liverpool.

North Liverpool is the largest Primary Care Network (PCN) in Liverpool, comprising 21 aligned GP practices serving a weighted population of approximately 150,000 patients. Our network brings together forward-thinking GP practices and multidisciplinary healthcare professionals who are dedicated to delivering high-quality, patient-centred, and integrated care. Through collaboration and innovation, we strive to improve health outcomes and meet the evolving needs of our diverse local communities.

employer: Lancashire & South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist, General Adult Psychiatry - Nelson
descriptionHtml:
Consultant Psychiatrist - General Adult Psychiatry, Pendle CMHT (10PA)

We are seeking to recruit a substantive Consultant Psychiatrist in General Adult Psychiatry to work as part of the Pendle Community Mental Health Team. The Pendle CMHT is one of six in Pennine Lancashire. You will be working as part of an MDT and would carry a compact caseload of the most complex and unstable cases, as well as supporting and advising other team members.

Applicants should hold full GMC registration and be included on the Specialist register of the GMC or they should be eligible for entry to the Specialist Register within 6 months of the interview date.

It is a requirement that applicants are Section 12 Approved at the time of commencing employment and have or are eligible to have Approved Clinician Status. Remuneration will be as set out in the terms of the New Consultant Contract according to previous experience.

The role:

At least 2.5 SPAs as standard for a full time post (we would be flexible in looking at enhancements to support other activities that support the wider ambitions of the Trust).

Excellent peer support group

Study leave budget of £3000 over 3 years or up to £5000 over 3 years for newly qualified Consultants

Opportunities to be a clinical supervisor

Relocation package available.

At our Trust, we're really keen to develop our Consultant workforce and nurture their areas of interest in a flexible way where possible. Come and have a chat with us about what your special interest or development area and build a suitable job plan with us.

We also have an extremely active Medical Education department and support our Consultants in becoming Clinical & Educational Supervisors and nurturing their interests in this area. There are also opportunities to have a role in Digital Leadership if this is a passion for any of our Consultants.

title: Maternity Cover Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Maternity Cover Salaried GP Opportunity at Severnside Medical Practice for 4-6 months.4 sessions per week on Tuesday and Fridays. Immediate Start, with option to become a permanent member of the team.

Who were looking for

  • A GP at any stage of their career, including newly qualified
  • Will consider GPs looking to join the retainer scheme for additional flexibilities
  • Someone enthusiastic about providing excellent patient care and keen to contribute to our positive practice culture

We understand the importance of flexibility. Well work with you to accommodate your commitments, including childcare and other responsibilities. You will be supported to develop your skills and interests, with 1 week of study leave per year alongside 6 weeks annual leave.

The post-holder will practice in accordance with accepted good medical practice and the various clinical policies of the Service, to include but not limited to:

The post-holder will make him/her-self available to undertake a variety of duties including surgery consultations, telephone consultations, video consultations and queries, visiting patients at home, checking and signing repeat prescriptions and dealing with queries, paperwork and correspondence in a timely fashion

Making professional, autonomous decisions in relation to presenting problems, whether self-referred or referred from other health care workers within the organisation or external organisations

Contributing to QOF, Enhanced Services and IIF requirements and recording data appropriately

Recording clear and contemporaneous consultation notes to agreed standards

Prescribing in accordance with the accepted prescribing formulary (or generically) whenever this is clinically appropriate

In general the post holder will be expected to undertake all the normal duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care, as set by Royal College of General Practitioners, General Medical Council, all other Royal colleges and councils applicable to the staff within the practice, Department of Health, NHS England, ICB and all other regulatory and standard setting organisations.

Were based in Quayside House (opened in 2019), a purpose-built, city-centre practice with excellent facilities.

Our friendly clinical team includes 2 GP partners, 6 salaried GPs, 2 paramedics, 4 practice nurses, and 1 healthcare assistant. Were also supported by a non-clinical managing partner, ensuring a well-rounded approach to care.

title: Clinical Pharmacist
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic, confident, patient-focused and practice based Clinical Pharmacist to become a valued member of our friendly, supportive practice team.

Ideally, you will bring previous General Practice experience with an IP qualification and a strong passion for delivering safe, high-quality, and effective care within primary care. This is an exciting chance to make a meaningful impact on patient care.

As a Clinical Pharmacist, you will work as an integral part of the multidisciplinary team, using your clinical expertise to optimise medicines, improve patient outcomes and promote the safe and effective use of medicines.

You will undertake structured medication reviews, support patients with long-term conditions, provide clinical advice to patients and colleagues, and contribute to medicines optimisation and quality improvement initiatives.

Although full time is preferable we can be flexible for the right candidate.

Undertake structured medication reviews and medicines optimisation to improve patient outcomes safety and adherence.

Provide clinical advice to GPs, nurses and the wider multidisciplinary team on prescribing and medicines-related issues.

Support the management of patients with long-term conditions, including medication review, monitoring and follow-up.

Identify and manage medication-related risks, including interactions, adverse effects, contraindications and inappropriate prescribing.

Support medicines reconciliation following hospital discharge and changes in care.

Provide patients with clear advice and counselling on their medicines, promoting adherence and shared decision-making.

Support safe, effective and cost-effective prescribing in line with NICE guidance, local formularies and practice policies.

Contribute to repeat prescribing, medicines safety, clinical audits, quality improvement and prescribing reviews.

Work collaboratively with community and hospital pharmacy teams and other healthcare professionals to ensure continuity of care.

Maintain accurate clinical records and comply with professional, legal, confidentiality and information governance requirements.

Participate in multidisciplinary meetings, clinical governance and service development.

Maintain professional competence through continuing professional development and work within GPhC standards

We are a progressive, friendly GP practice serving a diverse patient population. Our team includes GPs, Practice nurses, Specialist nurses (Respiratory, diabetes and family planning) HCAs, pharmacists, paramedics and administrative staff who work collaboratively to provide safe, effective, and holistic care. We value innovation, teamwork, and continuous improvement.

title: Consultant Child and Adolescent Psychiatrist in Eating Disorders
descriptionHtml:
This is a new post which has been created as part of a successful bid to expand community eating disorders for children and young people.

The post holder will provide senior clinical leadership and psychiatric expertise within a specialist multidisciplinary team delivering evidence-based care for young people with eating disorders. The service combines intensive day hospital treatment and home-based interventions, offering a flexible and family-centred approach to prevent or shorten inpatient admissions and support sustainable recovery. In addition, as it is a new service, the post holder will have the opportunity to provide medical leadership in its development.

Specific responsibilities may include:o Provide specialist psychiatric assessment and management for young people with eating disorders and co-occurring mental health conditions.o Lead on formulation, care planning, and review within a multidisciplinary team including psychologists, nurses, dietitians, family therapists, occupational therapists, and social workers.o Offer psychiatric input for both Day Hospital (maximum 6 patients) and the Intensive Support at Home Team (up to 5 patients) components of the service. While this is a new service, it is anticipated that there will be one new patient for each service weekly, although the day patients will likely already open to the home support team. Therefore, it is expected that the post holder will see one new patient per week for psychiatric assessment and 10 follow up reviews per week.o Oversee pharmacological treatments, physical health monitoring, and mental state management.o Participate in family-based interventions, working collaboratively with carers to promote recovery and resilience.o Support early identification of risk and contribute to crisis management plans.o Liaise effectively with community CAMHS, paediatric, education, and social care services to ensure continuity of care.o Contribute to admission avoidance and step-down care from inpatient units.

At Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership NHS Trust (CWPT), we deliver a wide range of physical, mental health, learning disability and autism services, and are proud to serve communities across Coventry, Warwickshire and beyond.

We put 'people at our heart'; this ethos is at the centre of everything we do and how we do it. We care for our staff and colleagues as much as they care for others and offer a wide range of benefits and development opportunities.

  • generous annual leave entitlement which increases during your time with us
  • excellent learning and development opportunities, including apprenticeship frameworks, distance learning, internal training, coaching and mentoring, and much more
  • salary sacrifice schemes for lease car/ vehicle, Cycle to Work, home and electronics, gym membership and more
  • discounts with a range of retailers, restaurants and entertainment venues through our Employee Assistance Programme and NHS discount schemes
  • wellbeing support, including an in-house counselling service, external helpline and more
  • staff networks and support group

We're always on the lookout for people who share our passion for improving the lives and wellbeing of people in our community, as well as our values of compassion, collaboration, excellence, integrity and respect.

title: PCN Frailty GP
descriptionHtml:
We have a fantastic opportunity for an experienced and motivated GP to join Folkestone, Hythe & Rural Primary Care Network as a Frailty GP.

We are an ambitious, innovative and forward-thinking PCN, recognised as being at the forefront of Integrated Neighbourhood Working across Kent and Medway.

Having been part of the national Neighbourhood Health Implementation Programme (NNHIP) pilot, we are helping to shape the future of neighbourhood healthcare.

This is a very exciting opportunity to join a progressive and dynamic environment, working within our established Integrated Neighbourhood Team to deliver a more proactive, responsive and joined-up approach to caring for patients living with frailty and complex needs.

We are looking for a GP who shares our ambition and enthusiasm for developing new ways of working.

Previous experience in frailty care would be highly desirable, although not essential.

Above all, we are seeking someone who is enthusiastic about integrated working and wants to play a key role in shaping the future of neighbourhood healthcare.

The post holder will act as a clinical leader for our established Integrated Neighbourhood Team, providing senior clinical leadership, oversight and guidance to a dynamic multidisciplinary team of clinicians and healthcare professionals.

The team delivers a combination of proactive and reactive care, supporting patients living with frailty, complex health needs and those at risk of deterioration or hospital admission.

The GP will play a key role in supporting clinical decision-making, managing complexity and ensuring a coordinated, patient-centred approach to care.

The role will involve working closely with a diverse range of professionals across neighbourhood services, providing clinical leadership and contributing to multidisciplinary discussions and care planning.

An important aspect of the role will be helping to lead and develop our innovative neighbourhood model, supporting new ways of working and shaping the future delivery of integrated care across our PCN.

Folkestone, Hythe & Rural Primary Care Network brings together seven GP practices serving a population of approximately 50,000 patients across a mixture of rural and urban communities.

Our member practices are Oaklands Health Centre, White House Surgery, Harbour Medical Practice, New Lyminge Surgery, Church Road Surgery, Sun Lane Surgery and Hawkinge and Elham Valley Practice.

Our population is diverse, covering communities with areas of significant deprivation alongside a high proportion of older patients and people living with frailty, multimorbidity and complex health needs.

We are an ambitious, progressive and forward-thinking organisation with a strong reputation for innovation, collaboration and developing new approaches to care.

Having participated in the national Neighbourhood Health Implementation Programme pilot, we have been at the forefront of Integrated Neighbourhood Working across Kent and Medway.

We have developed an established Integrated Neighbourhood Team, bringing together professionals from primary care, community health and wider partners to deliver more joined-up, proactive and responsive care.

We pride ourselves on creating a supportive and inclusive working environment where staff are valued, encouraged to contribute ideas and actively involved in service development.

This is an exciting time to join our PCN as we continue to build on our achievements and help shape the future of neighbourhood healthcare.

employer: University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Hepatologist
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a dynamic and enthusiastic Hepatologist to join our University of Derby and Burton Hospitals (UHDB) team of 6 Hepatology consultants and 8 specialist nurses.

The successful candidate will also work closely with our 14 luminal gastroenterologists in providing a 24/7 gastroenterology and liver service including a daily inpatient endoscopy list and endoscopy nurse supported out of hours GI bleed service.

This is a full-time position, but candidates wishing to work part-time or in a job-share are encouraged to apply. If a part-time or job-share person is appointed modification of the job content will be discussed with the appointee on a personal basis. Informal visits are welcomed.

Hepatology services are primarily based at the Royal Derby Hospital site, which is a level 2 liver centre. In 2023, the service achieved level 2 (full) IQILS (Improving Quality of Liver Services) accreditation. The assessment team highlighted several areas of excellence in the service. The unit is a tertiary referral centre for PTC and TIPSS and works closely with the Liver transplant unit in Birmingham in caring for patients pre and post liver transplantation.

Luminal and Hepatology services are provided on 2 separate dedicated wards at Royal Derby Hospital (RDH) and on 1 ward at Queens Hospital Burton (QHB). At RDH the Hepatology service is supported by 8 Clinical Nurse Specialists including 2 Viral Hepatitis, 2 Hepatology, and 4 HPB cancer nurse Specialists, together with alcohol liaison service. We have excellent endoscopy facilities which are all JAG accredited this includes a 3-room endoscopy suite at QHB and a 2-room endoscopy suite at SRP. We participate in the national bowel cancer screening programme across the Acute Hospitals.

As a trusted organisation at the heart of our communities, we recognise the important role we can play in supporting the public, patients, our own people and local partners in achieving the best of health for the local population and the communities in which they live by providing Exceptional Care Together

Our fundamental Values of Compassion, Openness and Excellence underpin how we intend to work as a Trust and the associated behaviours are becoming embedded in all aspects of how we work.

In return we will offer:

o Development opportunities, including both professional and leadership developmento On-going support through every step of the way from recruitment to when you join our team and beyond.o A variety of other staff benefits including employee assistance programme, discounted gym membership, onsite fitness classes, car schemes

Key Facts about our Trust:

o We see on average 4810 OP appointments per day.o We are the 4th busiest Trauma & Orthopaedic outpatients department in England - an average of 2077 per week.o An average of 1115 patients are seen in A&Es across our network every day - 3rd largest in the country.o Our hospitals admit an average of 195 emergency patients daily.o Last year we undertook almost 33,700 planned surgical operations in our 57 operating theatres.o We are one of only 7 Trusts nationally with more than 50 operating theatres.o We carry out more than 140 elective procedures each working day.

title: Locum Consultant Psychiatrist in Substance Misuse
descriptionHtml:

The Ridings Medical Group is a large, forward-thinking training practice operating as a single Primary Care Network, River & Wolds PCN, delivering high-quality primary care services to more than 48,000 patients across five sites in the East Riding of Yorkshire.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Salaried GP to join the Team for 5 sessions per week.

We are an established training practice for GP registrars and medical students with a practice list size of 11,000 patients. We work out of privately-owned premises.

We are a dispensing practice, use Systmone and achieve high QOF scores.

Barnard Castle lies in the rural beauty of Teesdale, being 1 hour drive to the Lake District and 30 minutes from Darlington, with rail connections to London or Edinburgh in around 2 hours.

We promote continuity of care with a usual GP system.

The practice endeavours to provide top quality primary care to patients in a courteous and professional manner.

We have a culture of openness and continuous learning and improvement.

We are supportive of clinician's interests and the development of portfolio careers.

13 patients in a standard surgery with 15-minute appointments.

Low number of house visits, which are supported by community paramedics.

Integrated clinical pharmacists, active care coordinator and social prescribers and practice based mental health practitioners.

Very well organised and efficient with a stable clinical and administration team.

title: PCN Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:

title: Employment Specialist Ref: 0187ZS
descriptionHtml:
Join our team as an IPS Employment Specialist in Torquay.

Do you believe you have the skills to help people return to employment, do you take pride in what you do, and can you think creatively about how different organisations can work together to deliver a better service? Are you happy to talk with employers and help match people into meaningful work? Are you a compassionate and motivated individual who wants to change peoples lives? If you are enthusiastic, creative and have a genuine desire to help others, wed love to hear from you.

As a leading charity supporting people with drug, alcohol, and mental health challenges, we operate over 80 services across England and Scotland, providing free and confidential support to more than 100,000 people each year.

Please use the Job Description to support your application.

Closing date: Sunday 12th November 2026. Please note this role may close earlier than the stated deadline if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. All applicants must submit a CV along with a cover letter explaining why they should be considered for this role.

As an IPS Employment Specialist, we offer a starting salary of £29,325 rising each year in line with our pay progression salary bands to £33,960 per year (This includes a Cornwall allowance of £1,000). For further details please reach out to a member of the recruitment team.

As an IPS Employment Specialist, you will support the IPS model as a specialism within a community substance misuse service and deliver support to people who are in treatment or recovery into employment. You will work directly with employers to secure

We have an exciting opportunity for an IPS Employment Specialist to join our team.

title: ARRS SALARIED GP
descriptionHtml:

title: Advanced Nurse Practitioner - Independent Prescriber
descriptionHtml:

2430 hours per week | Salary dependent on experience.

title: Receptionist
descriptionHtml:
Join our friendly and professional team at Harvey Group Practice, As the first point of contact, our receptionists play a vital role in ensuring patients receive the right care, support, and information when they need it most. Youll be part of a busy, welcoming environment where teamwork, compassion, and excellent communication are key.

No two days are the same from managing appointments and assisting patients with their queries to supporting the wider clinical team, youll be at the heart of the practices daily operations. title: Salaried GP - Bewdley Medical Centre
descriptionHtml:
Salaried GP Up to 6 Sessions

Bewdley Medical Centre | Wyre Forest Health Partnership

Looking for a General Practice role where you can enjoy medicine, develop your career and achieve a healthy work-life balance? We'd love to welcome you to the Bewdley Medical Centre.

As one of five practices within one of Worcestershire's largest GP partnerships, at Bewdley Medical Centre we provide care to approximately 15,000 patients. We combine the stability, opportunities, and support of a large organisation with the welcoming, friendly atmosphere of small local practice.

  • A welcoming culture where your ideas and well being matter

Whether you're newly qualified or an experienced GP, we'll support you to build a rewarding and enjoyable career.

You'll provide high-quality, patient-centred care within a well-supported clinical environment, allowing you to focus on delivering excellent General Practice.

We offer:

Wyre Forest Health Partnership is one of Worcestershire's largest GP partnerships, caring for approximately 73,000 patients across five practices with a team of around 360 colleagues, including more than 50 GPs. We're proud to invest in our people. You'll be joining a supportive multidisciplinary team, backed by experienced practice managers, a dedicated Head Office and wellbeing team, and colleagues who genuinely enjoy working together. Whether you're interested in developing a specialist clinical interest, teaching, research, leadership or a portfolio career, we'll help you achieve your ambitions.

Above all, we're committed to creating an environment where GPs can thrive. We're also proud to support the NHS ambition to achieve net zero and encourage colleagues to contribute to sustainable healthcare.

employer: The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust

descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen at The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust for a Specialist in Gastroenterology to join our existing team of accomplished Gastroenterologists and Specialist Nurses who have a passion for delivering high-quality care to our patients in the county of Shropshire, Wrekin and Mid Wales.

The department offers extensive opportunities to work independently and alongside consultants both in a clinic environment and in Endoscopy, with access to complex procedures, modern equipment and specialist interests.

Contribution to an out of hours on call rota is core to this role.

  • To provide specialist care for Gastroenterology/Hepatology patients including, in-patients, in-reach/review of referrals, day unit treatments, out-patient clinics and endoscopy lists.

The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust (SaTH) is the main provider of acute hospital services for around half a million people in Shropshire, Telford & Wrekin and mid Wales.

Both hospitals provide a wide range of acute hospital services including accident & emergency, outpatients, diagnostics, inpatient medical care and critical care.

Our Poppy's Promise Commitment

We believe that compassionate care sits at the heart of everything we do. Every member of our team -- clinical or non-clinical -- plays a vital role in ensuring that patients, families, and colleagues are treated with dignity, empathy, and respect at all times.

We expect all staff to demonstrate compassion not only through their words, but through their actions: by listening attentively, communicating clearly and kindly, and recognising individual needs, feelings, and circumstances of those in our care.

Effective communication is central to safe and high-quality healthcare. We value colleagues who take the time to understand others, explain information in a meaningful way, and respond to concerns with patience and understanding.

By joining our team, you are committing to uphold these values -- ensuring that every patient feels heard, respected, and valued, and that compassion is embedded in every interaction, every day.

title: Consultant Vascular Surgeon
descriptionHtml:
Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board wishes to appoint a full-time substantive Consultant Vascular Surgeon to join the existing team of eight Consultant Vascular Surgeons who provide the service across North Wales.

The post is a combination of replacement and expansion, in part arising as a result of a move to increase provision of surgical services at our spoke sites.

The successful candidates will form part of a rota consisting of 1 week in 8 as Vascular Consultant of the Week (VCOW) and 1 night in 8 on call overnight.

As part of the recruitment process, applicants who are successful at shortlisting will be invited to attend a Stakeholder Interview and an Advisory Appointments Committee (AAC) Interview on 11th December 2026.

Clinical DutiesThe post holder will:

  • work collaboratively with Consultant colleagues, as appropriate, to provide specialist services at the designated hospitals, with responsibility for the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of illness
  • have continuing responsibility for the care of patients in liaison with Consultant colleagues and for the proper functioning of the department in line with the Operational Policy and Strategic Plan (as amended from time to time).
  • be responsible for the professional supervision and management of junior medical staff. If appropriate the post holder will be named in the contracts of junior staff as the person responsible for overseeing their training and as an initial source of advice to such doctors regarding their careers.
  • be required to participate in continuing medical education in ways which are acceptable to the Educational Lead, Educational Director of Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, and the Chief Executive Officer.
  • be required to participate in, and contribute to, Clinical Audit in line with the Health Board's policy on the implementation of Clinical Governance.
  • participate in the North Wales Vascular Network on-call rota.

In collaboration with consultant colleagues within the Network, prospective cover arrangements will be required during periods of planned leave.

Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board (BCUHB) is Wales's largest health organisation, with a budget of over £2.4 billion and a workforce of over 20,000 staff.

BCUHB provides a full range of primary, community, mental health, acute and specialist hospital services for the population of North Wales, across three acute hospitals and a network of community hospitals, health centres, clinics, and mental health units. It also co-ordinates or provides the work of GP practices and NHS services provided by dentists, opticians, and pharmacists across the region.

The Health Board is an integrated health system that strives for excellent, compassionate care delivered in partnership with the public sector and other statutory and third sector organisations.

employer: Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Paediatrician with an interest in Diabetes
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to find a Consultant Paediatrician to join our friendly team at Blackpool Teaching Hospital. We are a team of 15 WTE consultants, delivering integrated care to Blackpool and the Fylde coast. The post is also an excellent opportunity for those with recent CCST or approaching CCST. The trust also offers a programme to new consultants that includes a well-designed leadership development programme that offers much consolidation of new skills to a recent CCST recipient. The trust also has an excellent CSSR programme, for those not yet on the Specialist Register.

For full details of the duties, please review the attached Job Description and Person Specification.

Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is a forward looking and innovative place to work and is committed to Values Based Collaborative Leadership and being a 'Great Place to Work'.

Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust was established on 1st December 2007. The Trust gained Teaching Hospital status and became Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust in 2010. In April 2012 the Trust merged with community health services from NHS Blackpool and NHS North Lancashire as part of the Transformation of Patient Pathways Programme. We are now a Vanguard site with Extensive Care Services provided for the complex elderly population within Blackpool, Fylde and Wyre.

The Trust serves a population of approximately 440,000 residents across Blackpool, Fylde, Wyre, Lancashire and South Cumbria and the North of England. The Trust is also responsible for the provision of Community services such as District Nursing and Midwifery to a large geographical area, extending from Lytham St Annes in the South to Morecambe and Carnforth in the North.

employer: St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Anaesthetist with an interest in Neuro Anaesthesia
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for Locum Neuro Anaesthesia Consultant post 10PAs and the post holders will join the Neuro on-call rota.

Upon appointment the post holder will be paired with a mentor for the first year. Furthermore, our set-up has much valuable support on-site as every day of the week, there is a senior Anaesthetic Consultant, acting as the Duty Floor Anaesthetist (DFA) for the overall smooth running of the operating theatres and providing urgent help and/or matching skills/experience of allocated anaesthetists with operating lists.

The post holder will join the Group of Neuro anaesthetists which consists of approximately 16 Consultants including Neuro Intensivists. This is a friendly, approachable, dynamic and diverse group, who are enthusiastic in both teaching colleagues and learning new skills from colleagues. There is emphasis in wellbeing and supporting each other. The case mix at St George's tends to be complex and challenging. Given the huge expertise in the department, it is easy to seek advice / discuss with an expert in a certain field or acquire new skills.

The post is for full time posts of 10 PAs, with 9 PAs for direct clinical care (DCC) and 1 for SPA in support of personal CPD, preparation for GMC appraisal, additional responsibilities of the post holder and revalidation with an opportunity to increase as interests develop.

The job plan template is based on an alternating working pattern, weeks AC and weeks BD. Some operating lists are three session lists, for continuity of care and theatre efficiency.

Session times (inclusive of CRA (clinical related activity time)

AM - 08:00-13:00 (5 hours - 1.25PA)

PM - 13:00-18:00 (5 hours - 1.25PA)

EVE - 17:00 - 21:00 (4 hours - 1PA)

All inpatient day sessions start at 08:00 and run until 18:00; 10 hours which equates to 2.5PAs. Half day sessions are 5 hours which equates to 1.25PAs. Three session lists equate to 3.5PA's.

The consultant job plan includes 'annualised sessions' which can be worked flexibly to meet the needs of the individual and the department. Each annualised session is equivalent to the PA value of the session worked. This flexibility allows individuals to organise working patterns to support a better work life balance, whilst also ensuring we have cover within the department. It is expected that the post-holder will contribute to a proportion of annualised sessions within the field of neuroanaesthesia. The remaining annualised sessions will be within the general anaesthesia subspecialties with in the skill mix of the individual anaesthetist.

The St George's Hospital Atkinson Morley Neurosurgical Unit is a leading UK centre for both adult and paediatric neurosurgery. It is a designated trauma centre with a specific neurosurgery service that manages all head injury patients. The Department of Anaesthesia covers all surgical specialities and is currently involved in many exciting initiatives. This is an excellent opportunity for an individual with the appropriate skills to join a first class team in an active and progressive London teaching hospital environment.

employer: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is seeking a Consultant Dermatologist to join our highly regarded Dermatology Department. As a regional centre for dermatology and skin cancer care, we provide specialist and general dermatology services to a large and diverse patient population, supported by exceptional facilities and a strong multidisciplinary team. The total workload is 10 PAs and you will be based at the Churchill Hospital, Oxford but may be required to support clinical activity at other clinics.

This role offers the opportunity to develop your clinical interests within a department that combines high-quality patient care, teaching, research and service innovation. You will join an experienced team of consultants, specialist nurses, trainees and allied health professionals, working in a supportive environment that encourages collaboration, professional development and continuous improvement

With increasing demand for dermatology services across the region, this is a chance to help shape the future of the specialty while contributing to one of the UK's leading teaching hospital trusts.

Care to join us...?

As a Consultant Dermatologist, you will provide expert clinical care across a broad range of dermatology services, including general dermatology, vulval dermatology and leg ulcer clinics. Working within a consultant-led service, you will deliver high-quality care for both outpatient and inpatient populations while supporting the continued development of specialist services.

You will:

Joining our team means becoming part of a department with an outstanding reputation for dermatology, skin cancer care, education and research, backed by modern facilities and a shared commitment to delivering exceptional patient outcomes.

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the UK's largest and most respected NHS teaching trusts, providing world-class healthcare across four hospitals: the John Radcliffe Hospital, Churchill Hospital, Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre and Horton General Hospital and over one hundred satellite sites.
