employer: University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust
title: Consultant Cellular Pathologist
descriptionHtml:
Coventry and Warwickshire Pathology Services (CWPS) invites applications for two replacement consultant cellular pathologists to join our forward-thinking and friendly team based at University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust (UHCW).

CWPS are a large pathology network in the Midlands, providing pathology services for UHCW, George Eliot Hospital NHS Trust and South Warwickshire University NHS Foundation Trust.We are seeking pathologists with sub-specialist interests in breast and gynaecological pathology, but would also consider dermatopathology, urology, haematolymphoid, thoracic, gastrointestinal and molecular pathology.

Participation in the autopsy service is welcomed but not essential.Participation in research and teaching (at undergraduate and post graduate level) is encouraged and supported by protected sessions. University of Warwick's Clinical Sciences Research Institute located on the UHCW site provides additional laboratory research facilities.

Informal enquiries should be addressed to Dr Sarah Read-Jones, Clinical Lead for Cellular Pathology: 02476 968320 sarah.read-jones@uhcw.nhs.uk

The appointee will provide a diagnostic consultation and advisory service to clinical colleagues in the Network and primary care. Histology reporting will be digital once the appointee has been trained and fully validated. Voice recognition training will also be provided as this is the preferred method of report entry.

The appointee will develop close collaborative links with clinicians working in their area of specialist expertise and work to develop services provided to patients in these areas to the highest standards including the adoption of best practice guidance, the development of diagnostic and treatment protocols and all other relevant guidelines.

University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire (UHCW) NHS Trust, rated as good by the Care Quality Commission, is one of the largest teaching Trusts in the UK.

We are extremely proud of our skilled employees across our hospital sites in Coventry and Rugby, with high quality patient care positioned at the heart of everything we do.

Boasting some of the most modern facilities in Western Europe, the Trust is renowned for being at the forefront of research and innovation as part of its blossoming reputation as a national and international leader in healthcare.

By joining our exciting journey, you will form part of a passionate, talented team and will be able to access a wide range of learning and development opportunities.

There has never been a better time to join our team.

title: General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
Spirit Primary Care is looking for a Salaried GP to join Satis House in Water Orton for 6 sessions per week.

Satis House is a single-handed practice, meaning you will be the sole GP working at the practice. This offers a real opportunity to build strong relationships with your patients and become an important part of the local community.

Although you will be the solo GP on site, you will not be working in isolation, the practice hosts a wider multi-disciplinary team including a nurse, pharmacist, HCA and patient services team.

You'll also have support of a GP Clinical Lead and Clinical Director throughout your journey, as well as colleagues across our other practices and triage team.

Your role will include:

  • Providing face-to-face, telephone and digital consultations, including home visits where required.
  • Managing a broad range of acute and chronic conditions, minor illness and injuries.
  • Providing continuity of care and developing strong, trusted relationships with patients.
  • Prescribing safely and appropriately and requesting and interpreting diagnostic investigations.
  • Providing preventative healthcare, health promotion, screening and vaccination advice.
  • Recognising and appropriately escalating safeguarding concerns.
  • Working with the wider MDT and external healthcare professionals to coordinate care for patients.
  • Supporting delivery of QOF and other contractual and quality requirements.
  • Participating in clinical governance, audits and quality improvement.
  • Keeping up to date with current clinical guidance, evidence-based practice and developments in primary care.
  • Maintaining your CPD, mandatory training and professional development.

Spirit Primary Care is an at-scale provider of GP services across Leicestershire and Warwickshire, supporting tens of thousands of patients across multiple practices.

We combine the benefits of working as part of a wider organisation such as shared expertise, resources, learning and support, with the individual identity and community focus of our practices.

We are committed to supporting our clinicians to deliver high-quality, patient-centred care while having the autonomy to use their professional judgement.

title: Locum Consultant in Medical Oncology
descriptionHtml:
This Locum Medical Oncologist role sits within a cohesive and supportive multidisciplinary cancer service in Hywel Dda University Health Board, where consultant input is highly valued and integral to service delivery. You will undertake a varied and clinically engaging workload across systemic anti-cancer therapies and outpatient care, supported by an experienced and approachable team of consultants, specialist nurses, and allied health professionals.

Working in Hywel Dda offers a distinctive way of practising medicine. The combination of smaller, well-connected clinical teams and a close-knit population allows for continuity of care, meaningful patient relationships, and visible impact across the patient pathway. Clinicians here often value the ability to focus on quality of care without the pressures typically associated with larger urban centres.The area itself provides a high standard of living, with easy access to coastline, countryside, and outdoor activities, alongside significantly reduced commute times and a more manageable pace of life. This supports a sustainable balance between clinical responsibilities and personal wellbeing--something increasingly important for consultants at all stages of their careers.

You will deliver Consultant-led outpatient clinics, providing assessment, treatment planning, and ongoing care for patients receiving systemic anti-cancer therapies. This includes developing individualised treatment strategies aligned with national guidance and MDT recommendations, while taking into account patient preference and overall clinical context.

You will play a central role in multidisciplinary team meetings, contributing specialist expertise to guide diagnosis, staging, and treatment decisions. The service benefits from strong collaborative working across oncology, palliative care, radiology, pathology, and surgical teams, enabling well-rounded and timely clinical decision-making.

The role includes responsibility for prescribing and overseeing systemic treatments, managing toxicities, and supporting patients through complex treatment pathways. You willalso contribute to the management of acute oncology presentations, ensuring safe and responsive care when patients become unwell.

Working across inpatient and outpatient settings, you will support continuity and consistency of care. There is close day-to-day collaboration with oncology nursing teams, pharmacists, and wider professionals, allowing for a coordinated and patient-centred approach.

Hywel Dda University Health Board plans and provides NHS healthcare services for people living in Carmarthenshire, Ceredigion, Pembrokeshire, and bordering counties.

We have over 13,000 staff and together we provide primary, community, in-hospital, mental health and learning disabilities services.

We work in partnership with the three local authorities, as well as public, private and third sector colleagues, including our valued team of volunteers.

Our services are provided in:

  • Four main hospitals: Bronglais Hospital in Aberystwyth; Glangwili Hospital in Carmarthen; Prince Philip Hospital in Llanelli; and Withybush Hospital in Haverfordwest
  • Five community hospitals: Amman Valley and Llandovery hospitals in Carmarthenshire; Tregaron Hospital in Ceredigion; and Tenby and South Pembrokeshire hospitals in Pembrokeshire
  • Two integrated care centres: Aberaeron and Cardigan in Ceredigion, and several other community settings
  • 47 general practices (six of which are health board managed practices); dental practices (including four orthodontic); 97 community pharmacies; 43 general ophthalmic practices; and 8 ophthalmic domiciliary providers
  • Numerous mental health and learning disabilities services

title: Specialty doctor

title: General Practitioner - Care Management Service

As a General Practitioner within the Care Management Service, you will provide clinical leadership and expertise within multidisciplinary neighbourhood teams, supporting the delivery of proactive care to patients with complex health and social care needs.

Support the identification, assessment and management of patients at high risk of unplanned healthcare utilisation.

Contribute to the development, review and optimisation of personalised care and support plans

employer: Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board
title: Specialist Grade Doctor in Ophthalmology
descriptionHtml:
These are newly created Specialist Doctor posts developed as part of the Medical Workforce productivity programme.

Specialist doctors are senior and experienced clinicians who will work autonomously to a level of defined competencies, as agreed within local clinical governance frameworks. Specialists will be responsible for patients in their areas of practice as an 'expert decision maker'.

Specialist doctors provide expertise in a specialised area, whether delivering care in a specific specialty or in a generalist service and will manage the full range of presentations in their area of practice. The role will primarily focus on providing direct clinical care, meeting service delivery and improvement requirements. However, the role will be supported by suitable development opportunities including management roles and leadership responsibilities in, teaching, academia research and service development. The details of the balance between clinical care and other elements of the role would be dis- cussed during the job planning process.

Specialist doctors are also expected to be involved in deliver teaching and training of others. They will be able to work as a member of a multi-disciplinary team, leading MDTs where appropriate.

Fixed term for up to 12 months to cover a Secondment

Provide clinical expertise and leadership to a defined outpatient and inpatient teams where appropriate

Provide specialist assessment and clinical management of patients with Ophthalmology problems

Provide medical liaison and advice regarding patients to local Specialist Doctors and GPs as necessary.

Provide supervision for the speciality doctor and core trainee, and to a Specialty Training Registrar if the post holder is approved as an Educational Super- visor and if an ST is allocated to the team.

Liaise effectively with members of the team, other services within the Health Board, general practitioners and other agencies.

This post is advertised as Welsh Desirable. Whilst the candidate doesn't need to have skills in Welsh, we'll consider it an advantage when short-listing and selecting candidates. This isn't 'fluency', just Speaking & Listening skills at Level 3 (equivalent to CEFR B2) or above. Level 3 means being able to communicate in Welsh during routine clinical situations, such as welcoming patients, discussing straightforward aspects of their care and answering routine questions. If you're comfortable holding everyday conversations in Welsh, we encourage you to apply. Your Welsh language skills will help us provide person-centred care and enable patients to receive services in their language of choice. Have a look at our 'Croeso Candidate' booklet below for more information.

Cwm Taf Morgannwg (CTM) University Health Board, part of NHS Wales, serves a large population across a diverse and beautiful region, steeped in history and heritage. With nearly 13,500 staff, our health board is one of Wales's largest employers.

Together, we are Team CTM; a workforce dedicated to offering excellent patient care and support to the 450,000 people across our three regions, Bridgend, Merthyr Tydfil, and Rhondda Cynon Taf. We operate three District General hospitals, several community hospitals, primary and community care facilities.

CTM's location offers the best of South Wales, just 20 minutes from Cardiff's vibrant city life, the natural beauty of the Brecon Beacons, and the serene coastline at Ogmore. Whether you enjoy lively urban amenities, peaceful countryside, or seaside escapes, our location makes an ideal setting for both work and personal life.

Our CTM 2030 Strategy--Our Health, Our Future--focuses on uniting our region around shared health and wellbeing goals. Our values guide us daily:

o We listen, learn, and improve

o We treat everyone with respect

o We work together as one team

CTM employees enjoy benefits including; a leading pension, generous leave, flexible work, career growth, and access to ongoing learning and development.

At CTM, you'll find a welcoming, team-oriented workplace that values diversity and compassion, where you can take pride in your work and the difference it makes.

employer: The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust
title: Locum Consultant Ophthalmologist with an interest in Oculoplastic
descriptionHtml:
The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust is looking for a locum Consultant Ophthalmologist with a sub-specialist interest in Oculoplastic, who will be predominantly based at the Royal Shrewsbury Hospital (RSH) Shrewsbury with responsibilities across both hospital sites.

Contribution to an out of hours on call rota is core to this role.

Main Clinical duties include:

  • Provide Ophthalmic services.
  • Complete clinical sessions in theatre, specialist Oculoplastic clinics, and general clinics.
  • Complete supporting professional activities.
  • Receive and coordinate referrals from urgent eye clinics, optometrist and other ophthalmic colleagues.
  • To develop enhanced clinical skills, especially in the assessment and management of acutely ill patients.
  • To have excellent team-working skills with the abilities and professional attitude to work well in a multi-professional team.
  • To deliver clinical and quality targets agreed both nationally and locally with clinical teams and commissioners.
  • To follow patients throughout their clinical pathways.

The Shrewsbury and Telford Hospital NHS Trust (SaTH) is the main provider of acute hospital services for around half a million people in Shropshire, Telford & Wrekin and mid Wales.

Our main service locations are the Princess Royal Hospital (PRH) in Telford and the Royal Shrewsbury Hospital (RSH) in Shrewsbury which are located 20 minutes' drive apart. Together they provide 99% of our activity. Both hospitals provide a wide range of acute hospital services.

Our Poppy's Promise Commitment

We believe that compassionate care sits at the heart of everything we do. Every member of our team -- clinical or non-clinical -- plays a vital role in ensuring that patients, families, and colleagues are treated with dignity, empathy, and respect at all times.

We expect all staff to demonstrate compassion not only through their words, but through their actions: by listening attentively, communicating clearly and kindly, and recognising individual needs, feelings, and circumstances of those in our care.

Effective communication is central to safe and high-quality healthcare. We value colleagues who take the time to understand others, explain information in a meaningful way, and respond to concerns with patience and understanding.

By joining our team, you are committing to uphold these values -- ensuring that every patient feels heard, respected, and valued, and that compassion is embedded in every interaction, every day.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Haven Health are seeking a Salaried GP to join their team in Felixstowe for 6-8 sessions per week with flexibility to discuss working arrangements. We welcome applications from experienced and newly qualified GPs who share our commitment to excellent patient care, enjoy working collaboratively and are keen to contribute to a positive team culture.

We are looking for someone who is approachable, compassionate and adaptable, with a positive attitude towards teamwork and continuous improvement. The successful candidate will be keen to contribute to the life of the practice, share ideas and help us deliver the best possible care for our patients.

You will provide high-quality, holistic care to our diverse patient population, including routine consultations, the management of acute and chronic conditions, and preventative healthcare. You will also have opportunities to contribute to the ongoing development of practice services, pursue areas of clinical interest and become involved in teaching and quality improvement initiatives.

We are committed to supporting the next generation of GPs and helping our clinicians build rewarding, sustainable careers within our organisation.

If you are looking for a practice where you can develop professionally, enjoy working as part of a supportive team and make a real difference to your patients, we would love to hear from you.

  • Provide comprehensive general medical services to registered patients, including assessment, diagnosis, treatment and ongoing management of acute and chronic conditions.
  • Undertake face-to-face, telephone and online consultations, as appropriate to clinical need and practice procedures.
  • Prescribe safely and effectively, following current guidance and practice policies.
  • Refer patients to secondary care and other services where clinically indicated.
  • Provide preventative healthcare, health promotion, screening and appropriate monitoring of long-term conditions.
  • Recognise and manage urgent and emergency presentations appropriately.
  • Maintain accurate, contemporaneous and confidential clinical records using the practice clinical system.
  • Support patients with complex needs, working collaboratively with the wider multidisciplinary team.
  • Duty doctor sessions
  • Minimal home visiting as a paramedic team is available
  • Clinical lead for an aligned Care Home

Suffolk Primary Care (SPC) is a forward-thinking partnership of GP surgeries across Suffolk. Our collaborative approach enables doctors and staff to share resources, ensuring the continued delivery of high-quality healthcare.

Why Join Haven Health ?

  • A supportive team: Work alongside an approachable partnership, experienced clinicians and highly trained multidisciplinary teams
  • A focus on clinical care: Benefit from well-developed systems and workflows designed to reduce administrative burden and support efficient working
  • Professional development: As a teaching practice covering a full range of specialties, we encourage learning, teaching and the development of individual interests.
  • A high achieving practice: We are proud of our strong QOF performance and high patient ratings.
  • Support at every stage: Whether you are experienced GP or newly qualified, we offer in-house learning and ongoing support to help you develop your skills and achieve your career ambitions.
  • A sustainable working pattern: We value work-life balance and aim to provide a positive environment where our GP's feel supported and able to thrive.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Greenwich Home Treatment Team
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen to join Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust as a valued Consultant based at Oxleas House, providing medical input into the Home Treatment Team in Greenwich.

The home treatment team is a busy multidisciplinary service providing acute treatment to adult patients with a range of mental health diagnosis and psychosocial stressors across the borough of Greenwich. There is an additional home treatment team that will cover older adults over the age of 65 but the three boroughs' for the Trust; Bexley, Bromley and Greenwich general adult mental health HTTs support this and with this in mind there may at times be patients on the general adult HTT workload who will be >65 years of age. The caseload size varies and is not capped, please refer to the Job Description with details on the referrals made to the team for the last few months. Greenwich HTT as part of Trust acute and crisis service line will work in close liaison with Bromley and Bexley HTTs.

The post-holder will work with other members of the MDT including but not limited to nursing, social workers and psychologists who will work together to monitor individuals' safety, providing a range of interventions and working closely with families and carers.

The team work closely with the other wards based at Oxleas House; Shrewsbury, Avery and The TARN and will be involved in the bed-management programme for the unit helping to facilitate discharges and help prevent unnecessary hospital admissions by working closely with community teams.

At Oxleas NHS Foundation Trust, we offer a wide range of NHS healthcare services to people living in South-East London and to people in prison across England. Our wide array of services includes community health care, such as district nursing and speech and language therapy, care for people with learning disabilities and mental health such as psychiatry, nursing and therapies.

Oxleas is a great place to work. It has been recognised as one of the Top 10 Best Places to Work 2023 by the Sunday Times amongst very big employers. Our staff survey results show that we are in the Top 5 in England and the highest in London for staff experience amongst similar trusts.

"We are always delighted to welcome new colleagues to the Oxleas family. We care about making Oxleas a great place to work - it's a big priority in our strategy. Come and join us - it's a place where our values, teamwork, equity, and wellbeing matter and where you can really help to improve people's lives."

title: GP ARRS (SDUC)

employer: NHS Cheshire and Merseyside Integrated Care Board
title: GP Clinical Lead for Primary Care and Neighbourhoods
descriptionHtml:
Clinical leads are responsible for providing clinical leadership and support into the various aspects of the work of the ICB, playing a pivotal role in ensuring that strategic commissioning decisions, and service transformation programmes are underpinned by robust clinical insight and aligned with national clinical standards and specifications.

Clinical leads are required to build strong partnerships across provider collaboratives, local authorities, public health bodies, primary care, community services, voluntary sector partners, and local populations. The role supports the Executive Clinical Director in improving population health outcomes, tackling health inequalities, enhancing productivity, and ensuring value for money in line with ICS objectives.

Clinical leads must demonstrate exceptional leadership, clinical credibility and the ability to collaborate across complex system boundaries. This role is critical in enabling the ICB to fulfil its statutory duties, drive continuous improvement, and deliver high quality, joined up care for local communities.

Portfolio responsibilities may vary and adapt over time to respond to the needs and strategic priorities of the ICB/ICS. However, the postholder is expected to fulfil the key functions of providing clinical leadership across primary care, shaping neighbourhood models, integrated working, and population health improvement.

Whilst there will be areas you will be responsible for leading across Cheshire and Merseyside, most of your work with practices and neighbourhoods will be based in Liverpool City Region

NHS Cheshire and Merseyside serves a population of over 2.7 million people across nine localities, working with 16 NHS provider organisations, 51 Primary Care Networks, local authorities and voluntary sector partners.

We are proud of Cheshire and Merseyside's record of collaborative working and there are countless examples of brilliant care, but there are also examples of variation in service which only serve to exacerbate health inequalities.

Our vision is for everyone in Cheshire and Merseyside to have a great start in life and get the support they need to stay healthy and live longer.

We will do this by working together, as equal partners, to support seamless, person-centred care and tackle health inequalities by improving the lives of the poorest fastest.

Our values are rooted in the NHS Constitution, and we strive to create a compassionate, collaborative and innovative culture where staff can thrive and make a real difference to local communities.

title: Recovery Workers - Glasgow
descriptionHtml:
Join our team as a Recovery Worker in Glasgow.

Are you a compassionate and motivated individual who wants to change peoples lives? Our team in Glasgow is looking for four Recovery Workers to join them in providing high-quality recovery care to a diverse client group. If you are enthusiastic, creative and passionate about helping others, wed love to hear from you. The roles are based across our services in North East, North West and South Glasgow.

As a leading charity supporting people with drug, alcohol, and mental health challenges, we operate over 80 services across England and Scotland, providing free and confidential support to more than 100,000 people each year. Find out more about us on our website.

Closing date: 22nd November 2026. Please note: This role may close earlier than the stated deadline if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. All applicants must submit a CV along with a cover letter explaining why they should be considered for this role. Applications will not be accepted without a cover letter.

Our vibrant and busy services across Glasgow provide support to people concerned about their own or someone else's alcohol or drug use. We have three Recovery Hubs (in North East, North West and South Glasgow), however much of our work is carried out in the local community. We work with people at all stages on their journey providing both one to one appointments and group work.

We are looking for a enthusiastic and dynamic Recovery Workers who are motivated to work as part of a thriving and diverse team, ensuring recovery opportunities are available for individuals at any point in their recovery journey. You will strive to work collaboratively with partners and communities, ensuring that we are as accessible as possible and that the principles of a Recovery Oriented System of Care and true person centred practice are at the heart of all that we do.

Our Recovery Workers play a vital role in supporting clients to identify their goals, ambitions, and passions. Youll work with them to create the best treatment plan for their needs and to guide them on their path to recovery.

This role is permanent and will work 37,5 hours per week across 7 days, evening and weekend work will be required. As a Recovery Worker, we offer a starting salary of £26,250 per annum, rising each year in line with our pay progression salary bands, to £30,000 per annum.

WithYou provides free and confidential support, without judgement, to more than 100,000 people every year experiencing challenges with drugs, alcohol and mental health across England and Scotland. Our name reflects who we are - a positive place where people can progress, connect with others and get friendly, expert help in a way that's right for them. Our staff team changes lives. If you're passionate about helping people get the support they need for issues with drugs, alcohol and mental health, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Consultant Luminal Gastroenterologist
descriptionHtml:
GI Medicine at MFT is undergoing one of the most significant periods of investment and transformation in its history, backed by sustained funding, we are expanding our services with a substantial increase in substantive clinical, nursing, allied health and administrative roles. This investment is focused on building a stable, future-proof workforce, reducing reliance on insourcing, and creating roles that are properly supported, well-resourced and designed for the long term.

As part of this investment, we are looking to recruit enthusiastic doctors to lead and transform how GI care is delivered at North Manchester General Hospital and at Manchester Royal Infirmary. New service models are being implemented across the Trust, including enhanced triage with Advice & Guidance and Straight-to-Test pathways, and innovative diagnostic approaches. These changes are already improving patient flow, reducing waiting times and supporting safer, more timely care.

GI Medicine operates as a managed single service MSS across North Manchester General Hospital (NMGH), Manchester Royal Infirmary (MRI), Wythenshawe Hospital and Trafford General Hospital (TGH). All roles will be expected to work across sites as part of a collaborative, cross-site working ethos that promotes shared learning, consistency of care and flexibility within job planning. There will also be an expectation of some evening and weekend working on a rota basis, particularly to support endoscopy and elective services

The exact duties of the appointees will be subject to discussion, but a proposed programme of weekly sessions is based on a working week of 10 PAs (units of Professional Activity) in accordance with the Terms and Conditions - Consultants (England) 2003. It is expected that PAs will be worked flexibly; flexibility in job planning is of particular importance for this roll because of the need to recover from the COVID-19 pandemic.

Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) is a leading centre of clinical excellence, renowned for pioneering patient care, advanced medical research, and a collaborative multi-speciality environment. We are the largest provider of specialist services, and our Oxford Road Campus in Manchester is the largest health academic campus in Europe - a great place to progress your career.

With over 30,000 employees, a turnover exceeding £3 billion, and 10 hospital and community services, join our team to help us deliver outstanding healthcare to our diverse communities.We offer an engaging and supportive environment, with access to state-of-the-art facilities and cutting-edge technology. Research and Innovation are at the heart of our work, offering opportunities to lead research that shapes the future of medicine, working alongside experts, advancing clinical practice, and improving patient outcomes.

At MFT, we foster a culture where every colleague is valued and empowered to thrive. Your expertise is recognised, your ambitions are supported, and your impact is felt at every level. Whether you want to develop your clinical skills, pursue research interests, or seek leadership opportunities, MFT provides the ideal environment to achieve your medical or professional aspirations.If you are dedicated to driving clinical innovation and delivering compassionate patient care, join us to shape tomorrow's healthcare; where clinical excellence, innovation, and your career will thrive.

title: Nurse
descriptionHtml:

InHealth is the UKs largest specialist provider of diagnostic and healthcare solutions, working in partnership with the NHS for more than 30 years to make healthcare better for more than 5 million patients each year.

For clinical colleagues, that means delivering high-quality care within modern settings, with state-of-the-art equipment across a wide range of community, hospital and mobile settings.

With flexibility, strong learning and development opportunities, and the chance to support people at important moments in their healthcare journey, you can build a rewarding career while making a real difference locally and nationally.

InHealth is a place where you're trusted to do your job well, supported by people who value your expertise and give you the space to act on it. Teams show up for each other, leaders back your judgment and help remove blockers rather than create them.

New opportunities open as we grow - whether that's progressing, moving sideways or taking on something different as your strengths evolve. And everything we do is focussed on making healthcare better - for patients, partners and the people delivering care.

Read more about us here: Who We Are - InHealth Group

At Cygnet, you'll enjoy excellent professional development, shopping, travel and leisure discounts as well as a range of healthcare and financial benefits to support you to be happy both in and out of work.

Apply now to enjoy excellent career prospects while reaping the rewards of making a difference to others every day.

title: Resident Medical Officer
descriptionHtml:
Planned Start Date: 01 April 2027

We are looking for an experienced and motivated Resident Medical Officer (RMO) to provide high-quality medical care for patients undergoing elective orthopaedic and spinal surgery within OHG Surgical Hub.

The successful candidate will provide continuous medical support to inpatients throughout their admission, working closely with consultants, anaesthetists, nursing staff and the wider multidisciplinary team to ensure safe, effective and responsive patient care.

This is an exciting opportunity to become part of a developing specialist elective surgical service committed to clinical excellence and outstanding patient outcomes.

  • Provide medical assessment and management of elective surgical patients throughout their inpatient stay.
  • Respond promptly to clinical concerns, patient deterioration and medical emergencies.
  • Undertake admission reviews, post-operative assessments and ongoing daily patient management.
  • Support the recognition and escalation of deteriorating patients using appropriate clinical pathways.
  • Liaise with consultant surgeons and anaesthetists regarding patient management and treatment plans.
  • Prescribe medications safely in accordance with local policies and national guidance.
  • Interpret clinical investigations including blood results, ECGs and diagnostic imaging where appropriate.
  • Maintain accurate, timely and comprehensive clinical documentation.
  • Participate in discharge planning and ensure appropriate follow-up arrangements.
  • Provide support during emergency situations, including medical emergencies and cardiac arrests.
  • Contribute to clinical governance, audit, patient safety and quality improvement initiatives.
  • Promote excellent communication with patients, relatives and members of the multidisciplinary team.

One Health Group was established in Sheffield in 2004 and has steadily and successfully grown to become a significant healthcare provider in the region. Commissioned by the NHS, we provide services for patients referred for Orthopaedics, General Surgery, Spine, Urology and Gynaecology and with clinics located in over 30 locations across Yorkshire, Derbyshire, Nottinghamshire, Leicestershire and Lincolnshire, we bring healthcare closer to where people live. We are committed to clinical excellence, and our mission is to provide innovative, high quality medical and clinical services for our patients, optimising outcomes so they can quickly continue healthy lives.

The One Health Group PLC Elective Surgery Hub is a specialist purpose-built elective surgical facility providing high-quality care for patients undergoing major orthopaedic and spinal procedures.

Our service includes:

  • One operating theatre.
  • Three-bay recovery unit.
  • Twelve inpatient bedrooms.
  • Dedicated pre-assessment clinic and outpatient facilities.

We specialise in elective surgery including:

  • Total hip and knee replacement.
  • Revision arthroplasty.
  • Spinal procedures including:
    • Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF).
    • Cervical/lumbar decompression.
    • Lumbar discectomy.
    • Spinal fusions

Our aim is to deliver safe, high-quality elective surgical care through excellent clinical practice, multidisciplinary teamwork and patient-centred care.

descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Locum Doctor (Consultant in General Psychiatry) to cover an assignment with the Ministry of Defence (MoD), at Donnington DCMH, in Telford, Shropshire.

This is a locum role (40 hours per week) and the successful candidate will deliver an exceptional standard of care to the MoD service personnel.

Hourly Rate- £83.47 per hour

Job Description:

  • To undertake clinical sessions (remote and face to face) for the Department of Community Mental Health (DCMH), carrying out fresh case assessments and reviews of all service personnel referred to the DCMH. This will include liaison with referrers and line management as required to facilitate the clinical and occupational management of the patient.

  • Must have completed sufficient Continuing Professional Development (CPD) in accordance with Royal College of Psychiatrists guidance on CPD.
  • Must hold current, valid personal medical indemnity insurance.
  • Must hold a full Driving Licence valid in the UK (in order to be able to conduct peripatetic clinics and assess personnel sick at home in exceptional circumstances).
  • Must be in date and able to provide certification for Safeguarding Children and Young People and Safeguarding Adults up to and including Level 3 training.

We are a contracted supplier to the MOD and have locum vacancies on military bases throughout the UK and occasionally overseas locations.

Military Medical Personnel offer an attractive package for candidates which may include the following:

  • Attractive rates of pay with weekly payments and choice of payment model
  • A generous Refer a Friend bonus scheme
  • Flexibility of long- and short-term assignments to suit your availability
  • Free uniforms provided (if required)

  • Free mandatory training
  • Weekly payments
  • Assigned an experienced consultant who will support you throughout your application and will continue to look after you during your assignment

employer: Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant T&O Surgeon with a Special Interest in Hand & Wrist
descriptionHtml:
The department works across all 3 hospital sites and is busy with daily trauma lists and other activity consisting of elective inpatient and daycases lists, fracture and outpatient clinics, and emergency department streaming clinics for minor injuries. It is equipped for the most modern orthopaedic procedures, being a well-equipped hospital with a full range of Clinical Support Services.

The well-developed is supported by dedicated occupational therapists and the Trauma and Orthopaedic Department as a whole has excellent specialist nursing input. Physiotherapy support in outpatient and inpatient areas is of a high standard, with well developed, dedicated teams. The orthopaedic surgeons have excellent links with radiology services, where radiologists have a keen interest in musculoskeletal imaging, particularly ultrasound. The Trust also has onsite access to CT and MRI. The Trauma and Orthopaedic Department works very closely with the Rheumatology Department within the Trust and it is expected that any appointee will continue with this team approach

As a senior employee of the Trust the post-holder will work in close co-operation with, and support, other clinical, medical professional and managerial colleagues in providing high quality healthcare to the Trust's patients.

Integral to the responsibilities of the posts are the following requirements:

  • To ensure the provision of a first class clinical service
  • To provide effective leadership to all staff engaged in the specialty
  • To undertake all work in accordance with the Trust's procedures and operating policies
  • To conduct clinical practice in accordance with contractual requirements and within the parameters of the Trust's and Business Unit's services plans

The post would suit a good team player dedicated to high quality patient care. The opportunity exists to work in a non-hierarchical setting and offer a wide range of orthopaedic procedures in this busy Trust. The postholder must be prepared to work cross site to allow development of services across northern Lincolnshire and Goole.

We are looking for an orthopaedic surgeon who has subspecialty interests in hand and wrist surgery.

The Humber Health Partnership is one of the largest acute and community Partnership arrangements in the NHS, seeing well over one million patients every year and managing a budget of over £1.3 billion.

Made up of two Trusts - Northern Lincolnshire and Goole NHS Foundation Trust (NLAG) and Hull University Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust (HUTH) - our Partnership has significant ambitions and is committed to delivering world-class hospital and community services for the 1.65 million people we serve.

Together we employ nearly 20,000 staff. Our five main hospital sites are Diana, Princess of Wales Hospital, Scunthorpe General Hospital and Goole and District Hospital, for NLAG and Hull Royal Infirmary and Castle Hill Hospital for HUTH.

As Teaching Hospitals working with the Hull York Medical School, we both lead and contribute to research in many areas - biomedical research, primary care, palliative medicine, cardiovascular and respiratory medicine, vascular surgery, cancer surgery and oncology.

We believe that by developing a diverse, inclusive, innovative, skilled and caring workforce, we can deliver excellent care to our patients and a great future for our employees, our Partnership and our community.

employer: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Senior Clinical Fellow in Gynaecology Urgent Suspected Cancer
descriptionHtml:
Senior Clinical Fellow in Gynaecology Urgent Suspected Cancer (USC)

Applications are invited for a post of Senior Clinical Fellow in the Department of Gynaecology supporting urgent suspected cancer and unit based activities,based at the Women's Centre, John Radcliffe and Horton Hospital, Banbury.

This is an exciting opportunity to work in a large tertiary teaching hospital, working alongside colleagues in a Thames Valley Cancer Centre. All the modern facilities, the relevant other multidisciplinary specialties and training opportunities that are required to provide top quality cancer diagnostic and low grade cancer treatments.

This post is suitable for candidates who wish to expand their knowledge and skills in the diagnosis and treatment of early Gynaecological cancers.

The post will be for 12 months in the first instance with the option of extending to two years in total, subject to satisfactory progress.

The post holder's duties will be primarily at The Women's Centre, John Radcliffe, and Horton Hospital, Banbury, but their presence may from time to time be required in other parts of the Trust. Appointee may be requested to share some clinical responsibilities with the wider Gynaecology Department.

Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the largest NHS teaching trusts in the country. It provides a wide range of general and specialist clinical services and is a base for medical education, training and research.The Trust comprises four hospitals - the John Radcliffe Hospital, Churchill Hospital and Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre in Headington and the Horton General Hospital in Banbury.

Our values, standards and behaviours define the quality of clinical care we offer and the professional relationships we make with our patients, colleagues and the wider community.

We call this Delivering Compassionate Excellence and its focus is on our values of compassion, respect, learning, delivery, improvement and excellence.

These values put patients at the heart of what we do and underpin the quality healthcare we would like for ourselves or a member of our family. Watch how we set out to deliver compassionate excellence via the OUH YouTube channel.

employer: Practice Plus Group - Health in Justice
title: Consultant Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
UNLOCK YOUR BEST WORK LIFE

+ MAKE A DIFFERENCE TO EVERY LIFE

We have an exciting opportunity for a Consultant Psychiatrists to join our healthcare team at HMP Brixton, a category B Prison located in South London.The site houses around 750 male patients aged 18+, many of whom have complex health needs.

We are looking for a dynamic Psychiatrist, who can be flexible in the way they work, and adapt quickly. You must be able to build a rapport with both officers and patients, as well as working along side the matrons to lead the teams.

Hours

Monday to Friday:09:00 - 17:00

This is a full time role working 40 hours a week 20% of the role can be worked from home for admin or CPD, which must be worked on a Thursday.

Salary

You'll receive an annual salary up to £185,000 per annum - depending on experience.

How will we support you?

  • You will be part of a team of 20 plus experienced and supportive Consultant psychiatrists
  • You will be able to attend monthly Consultant's meeting and 1:1 clinical supervision.
  • Bespoke induction, including our Introducing Health in Justice training course
  • Competency framework

As aConsultant Psychiatrist, your responsibilities will vary. You will

  • Provide excellent clinical care, assessment and treatment to patients on the case load onsite
  • Actively participate in the strategic direction of the mental health service, lead the senior mental health clinicians on service developments and provide clinical supervision
  • Work within the multi-disciplinary team to review referrals, determine appropriate treatment plans, conduct risk assessments, and engage in multi professional complex case reviews.

If you are interested incareer development,we have a wide range of opportunities for you to develop your skills and experience, which include bothinternal and external optionsfor development and learning.

It doesnt stop there we also offer:

  • Discounts on shopping and leisure activities
  • Support to grow in your role and continue your professional development
  • 24/7 employee assistance helpline and financial assistance when you need it

The Health in Justice team at Practice Plus Group makes a real difference across over 53 prisons, young offenders and immigration removal centres. Were the UKs leading independent provider of NHS services to over 40,000 patients in secure environments, always putting their needs first, regardless of their background.

Practice Plus Groups purpose is to Unlock your best work life and we stand by our core values:

  • We treat patients and each other as they would like to be treated
  • We act with integrity
  • We embrace diversity
  • We strive to do things better together

We are looking for caring, compassionate but also driven professionals who can help us drive our vision for a fair and inclusive healthcare access to all.

Requirements

  • Registered professional with current registration (GMC)
  • Specialist Registration in either General Adult or Forensic Psychiatry
  • Approved under section 12 (2) of the MHS 1983
  • Understanding of the complexities of multi-disciplinary and multi-agency working
  • Up to date knowledge in the adult psychiatry and PD
  • Awareness of current issues in mental health service provision, policy and legislation

Secure environments are one of the most challenging, yet rewarding places for healthcare professionals to work. If youre looking for a role where you can develop your existing healthcare skills and learn something new every day in an environment that never stands still, then this could be the right opportunity for you.

title: Urgent Primary Care Doctor (GP) - Bank
descriptionHtml: Urgent Primary Care Doctor  Bank (Home Visiting) Bring urgent primary care to the patients who need it most - in their own homes. Urgent care is General Practice at its most immediate. Not every patient who needs urgent care can come to us. Some are housebound, frail, approaching the end of life or have been clinically assessed as needing a face-to-face review in their own home. What they need is an experienced doctor who can listen, assess, make confident clinical decisions and get them to the right care. At IC24, we're looking for Urgent Primary Care Doctors to work within our Home Visiting Service across Kent. You'll work alongside our drivers, dispatch teams and wider urgent care colleagues, providing safe, timely and effective care to patients in their own homes. If you enjoy the variety of General Practice, the autonomy of home visiting and the clinical challenge of assessing and treating patients in their own environment, this could be the role for you. What you'll focus on  Assessing and treating patients in their own homes You'll provide face-to-face assesAs an Urgent Primary Care Doctor (GP) - Bank, you'll provide urgent primary care to patients in their own homes, primarily targeting individuals who are housebound, frail, or approaching the end of life. The role involves making autonomous clinical decisions, assessing risk, and ensuring patients receive appropriate care and management. You will work within the IC24's Home Visiting Service alongside drivers and dispatch teams, administering safe, timely, and effective care. The position requires GPs to be experienced in face-to-face consultations, confident in autonomous decision-making, and skilled in managing complex cases in various home environments. Flexibility is important, as the role includes work during evenings, weekends, overnights, and holidays, responding to the urgent needs of patients. The role offers an hourly pay of £58.69 plus enhancements for unsociable hours, along with opportunities for professional development and participation in the NHS Pension Scheme.Integrated Care 24 (IC24) is a leading not-for-profit Social Enterprise committed to providing primary and urgent care services. Being patient-focused, IC24 aims to improve access to health and social care, thereby reducing pressure on secondary care services. IC24 provides a wide range of healthcare services, including GP Out of Hours, NHS 111, Primary Care, and Integrated Urgent Care Services. Serving over six million patients, IC24 works tirelessly to ensure patients receive timely and effective care, tailoring services to meet immediate healthcare needs. IC24 celebrates diversity and offers equal opportunities to all applicants, fostering an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and feel they belong. IC24 is dedicated to patient safety and operates with high clinical standards, ensuring staff meet regulatory requirements such as GMC guidance and strive for continuous improvement through learning and development opportunities. The organisation is headquartered in Ashford, operating several locations throughout Kent, such as Canterbury and Margate.

title: Consultant Obstetrician & Gynaecologist
descriptionHtml:
Two consultant posts available:

1. With a specialist interest in Fetal Medicine

2. With a specialist interest in Rapid Access Gynaecology & Minimal Access Surgery (MAS)

We are looking for 2 proactive, motivated, forward thinking and dynamic individuals to join our Consultant team. These are substantive posts based at Royal Hampshire County Hospital and the successful applicants will provide cover for both obstetrics and gynaecology.

Specialist Interest in Fetal Medicine - The successful candidate will be expected to provide specialist fetal medicine input for our obstetric patients. The post will also include a gynaecology component to maintain skills across both obstetrics and gynaecology. On-call commitments provide cover for both obstetrics and gynaecology. The department would welcome a candidate with a specialist interest in fetal medicine scanning and multiple pregnancy who would like to maintain a commitment to gynaecology and work in a friendly, welcoming district general hospital

Specialist Interest in Rapid Access Gynaecology & Minimal Access Surgery (MAS) - The department would welcome a candidate committed to both Obstetrics and Gynaecology with a specialist interest in rapid access gynaecology and excellent minimal access surgical skills. This is a new post developed to support the 2 week wait pathway as well as address the long waiting times in general gynaecology and endometriosis. The post is available to start in April 2027.

All applicants should have completed the Labour Ward ATSM module and further ATSMs as relevant to the advertised post.

Applicants are expected to have been awarded CCT (or be within 6 months of award of CCT at the time of interview) and be on the GMC Specialist Register.

Hampshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (HHFT) provides hospital services to around 570,000 people living in Hampshire and parts of West Berkshire, and specialist services to patients from all over the country. We deliver a full range of district hospital services in a variety of locations.

title: Senior Clinical Fellow in Emergency Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Love Emergency Medicine? Love Weston-super-Mare.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust (BFT) is looking to grow its talented Emergency Medicine team at Weston General Hospital to help drive an ambitious vision for the future of emergency care across Bristol and Weston. This is an exciting time to join our organisation!

You will be working as part of a talented team in a beautiful part of the country, with Weston-super-Mare offering easy access to the coast and the surrounding Somerset countryside.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust seeks applications for the position of Clinical Fellow ST3+ in Emergency Medicine, working on a full-time contract for a 12-month fixed-term period from the date of appointment, with a start date as soon as possible.

The post is advertised as a full-time position working on the full middle-grade rota. Candidates wishing to be considered for less than full-time working hours are also encouraged to apply.

These posts reflect a firm commitment to maintaining and developing the middle-grade workforce within Weston General Hospital's Emergency Department. The post offers eligible clinicians an excellent opportunity for continued professional development within Emergency Medicine, working in a supportive team committed to delivering high-quality, safe and effective emergency care.

Weston General Hospital's Emergency Department is a vital part of the hospital's emergency front door, providing an opportunity to develop clinical skills, gain valuable experience and contribute to the ongoing development of emergency services for the local population.

Main duties (but not an exhaustive list):

o Providing direct clinical care to all patients

o Formulate a diagnosis and develop a management strategy or plan for each patient

o Provide patient management in accordance with Emergency Department protocols, practice standards and Trust policies

o Provide clear and precise written and electronic documentation of patient care

o Provide advice and support to junior doctors on all aspects of emergency medicine

o Participate in the current shift rota pattern

o Participate and lead on clinical audits

o Participate in the annual staff appraisal

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust brings together more than 28,000 staff to deliver over 160 clinical services across thirteen hospital locations,operatingfrom three main sites at Southmead, Bristol citycentreand Weston.

With an annual turnover of £2.3 billion, we are now one of the largest NHS trusts in the United Kingdom. Our hospitals are spread across Bristol and Weston, join us and you can enjoy the very best of both worlds; city living within a stone's throw of the countryside or beside the seaside, both with easy access to all that theSouth Westhas to offer.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust values all people as individuals. As an equal opportunities employer actively working towards a diverse workforce we aim to recruit andretaina workforce whichrepresentsthe rich diversity of the local population at all levels and are committed to designing our services around the needs of individual patients and those around them. Anonymous information will be used from your applicationin order toensurewe'remeeting our pledge.

employer: Palace Surgery, Dr Mangwana and Partners
title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Palace Surgery is looking for an enthusiastic and caring GP to join our friendly team as a salaried GP for 4 sessions per week. This is a permanent post, and we are happy to talk about which days and sessions would suit you best [our preferred days are Mondays and Wednesdays].

As a smaller practice, we offer the chance to really get to know your patients and colleagues, with good continuity of care and supportive, approachable partners. The post would suit an experienced GP, or a newly qualified GP looking for a well-supported first salaried role.

We offer:

  • A competitive sessional rate, depending on experience
  • NHS Pension Scheme membership
  • Annual leave and study leave, pro rata
  • Support with appraisal, revalidation and CPD, and the chance to develop a special interest

Informal enquiries and visits are very welcome. Please contact Nuwan Pathiranage, Practice Manager, on palace.surgery@nhs.net or 020 7736 6305.

You will provide safe, high-quality, patient-centred care to our registered patients across 4 clinical sessions a week. Sessions include a mix of face-to-face, telephone and online consultations, together with the admin that comes from your own clinics.

The main duties include:

  • Seeing and managing patients with a wide range of acute and long-term conditions
  • Taking a share of the duty doctor / same-day urgent care rota, pro rata
  • Home visits when clinically needed
  • Reviewing results, letters and prescriptions linked to your patients
  • Making appropriate referrals and keeping clear, accurate records
  • Taking part in clinical meetings, audit and significant event reviews
  • Helping the practice deliver QOF, enhanced services and PCN work

You will work closely with our GP partners, practice nurse, healthcare assistant and admin team, and with South Fulham PCN colleagues such as clinical pharmacists and paramedics. The full job description is set out below.

Palace Surgery is a friendly, well-established GP practice in Fulham, caring for around 5100 patients in the London Borough of Hammersmith and Fulham. We are a GP partnership and a member of South Fulham Primary Care Network, which brings together seven local practices, within NHS North West London.

Our patients are a relatively young population. Rates of long-term conditions are lower than average, but mental health needs are higher, so the work is varied and rewarding.

We are rated Good by the Care Quality Commission in all five areas: safe, effective, caring, responsive and well-led. The surgery is in a converted building over two floors, close to bus routes along Fulham Palace Road, and is open Monday to Friday, 8am to 6.30pm.

We value teamwork, respect and a healthy worklife balance, and we will make sure you feel welcome and well supported from your first day. We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from all backgrounds.

title: Salaried GP

employer: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Allergist (Subspecialty - Chronic Urticaria and Angioedema)
descriptionHtml:
The Adult Allergy Department is seeking a full time Consultant Allergist with Subspecialty in Chronic Urticaria and Angioedema to join a dynamic, enthusiastic and forward-thinking team. The Department offers a comprehensive range of allergy services and has been accredited as a Centre of Excellence by both the Global Allergy and Asthma European Network (GA2LEN) and the World Allergy Organisation (WAO).

Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust has 5 hospital sites which are Guy's Hospital, St Thomas' Hospital, Royal Brompton Hospital, Harefield Hospital and Evelina London Children's Hospital. These clinics will be predominantly at the Guy's Hospital, some clinics would take place at St Thomas' Hospital and the Royal Brompton Hospital.

As an organisation, we are committed to developing our services in ways that best suit the needs of our patients. This includes asking certain groups of staff to work more flexibly so that we can offer services to patients in the evenings and at weekends. We regard this flexibility as essential if we are to continue to provide first class patient care in the future. As a result, any offer of employment to a consultant post will be subject to you agreeing to work a new more flexible pattern of working in the future if required and in accordance with the provisions of the new Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust consultant contract.

The main clinical components of the full time post are:

  • 2.5 General Allergy clinics per week
  • 1 Severe Urticaria clinic per week
  • 1 Drug Allergy clinic per week
  • 1 Challenge clinic per week
  • Leadership of the Severe Urticaria Service (Allergy) and supporting with prescribing of biologics (homecare and outpatient)

The Trust consists of St Thomas' Hospital at Waterloo, including the Evelina Children's Hospital, Guy's Hospital at London Bridge, Royal Brompton Hospital at Chelsea and Harefield Hospital at Harefield. We are also part of King's Health Partners (KHP), which comprises King's College London, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust and South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust. KHP is one of just five accredited UK Academic Health Sciences Centres (AHSCs). Through our AHSC, we are committed to making research and education integral to the delivery of high quality clinical care. The King's Health Partners Integrated Cancer Centre (ICC) is the vehicle for developing and managing cancer research, clinical services, and training and development across all the KHP partner organisations.

Our hospitals have a long and proud history, dating back almost 900 years, and have been at the forefront of medical progress and innovation since they were founded. We continue to build on these traditions and have a reputation for clinical, teaching and research excellence.

employer: South Tees Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

10 PA CONTRACT

Current NHS Consultant Terms and Conditions

We support the'Making Every Contact Count'approach to behaviour change in the promotion of health and wellbeing of individuals and communities.

At University Hospitals Tees our main priority is, and always will be, to provide safe and high quality care to our patients every day; the kind of care we would want for ourselves and our loved ones. title: Consultant Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
This is a new consultant post created to provide medical leadership to Hounslow's new Intensive Outreach & Rehabilitation Service, which brings together the existing Community Rehabilitation Service (CRS) and a new Intensive Outreach (IO) function under a single clinical and operational structure, each delivered as a distinct pathway with a single Team Manager. The post holder will hold overall medical responsibility for the Intensive Outreach pathway working closely with the Consultant responsible for the Community Rehabilitation Service (CRS) pathway (already in post).

This is a full-time post of 10 programmed activities, made up of two components. Six PAs (0.6 WTE) are allocated to the Intensive Outreach pathway described above. The remaining four PAs (0.4 WTE) are allocated to the Hounslow Early Intervention in Psychosis (EIP) service, where the post holder will provide consultant psychiatrist input to the EIP multidisciplinary team.

Provide medical leadership for the Intensive Outreach (IO) pathway, working in partnership with the Band 8a Team Manager.

Undertake senior assessment and direct clinical input for the most complex cases within the IO pathway, including risk and medication management, diagnostic assessment, Mental Health Act assessments and CTO reviews.

Support the team's duty function for urgent concerns and assessments.

Provide consultant psychiatrist input and clinical leadership to the Hounslow EIP multidisciplinary team, working in partnership with the EIP Team Manager.

Undertake senior assessments and direct clinical input for more complex EIP cases, including diagnostic assessment, risk and medication management, Mental Health Act assessments and CTO reviews, and hold senior medical responsibility for care delivered by the EIP team.

Provide early, easy-access advice to GPs and Primary Care Networks under a liaison and consultation model, contactable by telephone or email during working hours.

Facilitate smooth transitions into and out of the EIP service, including transition of young people from CAMHS at 18, and onward transfer to MINT or the IO and CRS pathways where appropriate.

West London NHS Trust is one of the most diverse healthcare providers in the UK, delivering a range of mental health and physical healthcare and community services. The Trust runs Broadmoor Hospital, one of three high secure hospitals in the country, with an international reputation.

Our high secure services care for patients from South of England and we provide low and medium secure services across eight London boroughs. The Trust also provides mental and physical healthcare in three London boroughs (Ealing, Hounslow and Hammersmith & Fulham). We employ 4,500 staff, of whom 56% are BME. Our turnover for 2023-24 is £426m.

The Trust is rated as 'Good' overallby the Care Quality Commission. Forensic services are rated as 'Outstanding'.

The Trust is an established partner and contributor in the development of the evolving North West London Integrated Care System and the Integrated Care Board. The Trust leads the NW London Children and Adolescent Mental Health provider collaborative.

title: Health Care Assistant /Nursing Associate in Primary Care

Band 3/4 depending on experience

title: Consultant Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
Consultant Psychiatrist in Forensic Psychotherapy

6 Programmed Activities, 0900-1700 3 days or flexible of 4 days

We are looking for an enthusiastic and committed Consultant Psychiatrist in Forensic Psychotherapy with excellent clinical, interpersonal, and risk management skills, and who enjoys teaching, training and consulting to a wide range of colleagues, teams, and institutions within health, forensic and social care settings.

Candidates are requested to use the section "Supporting Information" on the application form to set out their reasons for applying and their suitability, referring to the person specification, for this post.

This is a six programmed activity (PA) Consultant Psychiatrist post to provide clinical services and contribute to the consultancy, teaching, and research activities of the Clinic.

Specifically, the post holder will provide assessments, individual and/or group psychotherapyfor patients, supervise a psychiatry specialist trainee in forensic psychotherapy, engage in the Clinic's other teaching and training programmes, offer consultancy to teams and organisations in the forensic field and engage in clinical governance, audit and outcomeresearch.

The Portman Clinic is a NHS England commissioned national specialist outpatient clinic offering psychoanalytically orientated assessment, treatment and management for children, adolescents and adults who suffer from problematic sexual behaviours or engage in delinquent, criminal or violent behaviour. Treatment offered is individual, group and couple therapy. The aim of the Portman Clinic is to develop a body of knowledge on criminality, sexual deviancy and violence through its clinical work and to disseminate this expertise through consultancy, teaching and training, research and publication.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist in Learning Disabilities - Carmarthen
descriptionHtml:
Join Hywel Dda University Health Board and play a key role in delivering and developing specialist Learning Disability Psychiatry services within one of the most picturesque regions of the UK, combining a rewarding clinical career with an exceptional quality of life. Working within a supportive and experienced multidisciplinary team, you will have the opportunity to provide expert clinical leadership, drive service improvement and make a meaningful difference to the lives of individuals with learning disabilities and their families.

Based in the heart of West Wales, this role offers the opportunity to combine a rewarding and varied clinical career with an exceptional quality of life. Hywel Dda serves the beautiful counties of Carmarthenshire, Pembrokeshire and Ceredigion, an area renowned for its stunning coastline, rolling countryside and welcoming communities. With award-winning beaches, national parks and excellent opportunities for outdoor activities, the region provides an enviable work-life balance for individuals and families alike.

The successful candidate will contribute to the future development of Learning Disability services, helping to shape innovative models of care, influence service delivery and support the Health Board's commitment to providing high-quality, person-centred care. The role offers the opportunity to engage in service improvement, education, leadership and multidisciplinary collaboration, while maintaining a fulfilling clinical practice.

The post holder will:o Communicate effectively with patients, families and carers, ensuring they remain central to all aspects of care and decision-making.o Manage patients with complex clinical presentations and provide specialist psychiatric expertise.o Maintain accurate, timely and high-quality clinical records in accordance with professional and organisational standards.o Liaise effectively with multidisciplinary teams and partner agencies to ensure coordinated care and positive patient outcomes.o Promote and apply evidence-based practice in all aspects of clinical work.o Participate in clinical governance, audit, quality improvement and patient safety initiatives.o Contribute to postgraduate education, teaching programmes, research activity and the supervision of trainees and other healthcare professionals.o Participate in departmental, professional and organisational meetings at local, regional and national level as required.o Work collaboratively with clinical and managerial colleagues to support the efficient and effective operation of services.o Contribute to the responsible use of resources in line with the principles of prudent healthcare.

Hywel Dda University Health Board plans and provides NHS healthcare services for people living in Carmarthenshire, Ceredigion, Pembrokeshire, and bordering counties.

We have over 13,000 staff and together we provide primary, community, in-hospital, mental health and learning disabilities services.

We work in partnership with the three local authorities, as well as public, private and third sector colleagues, including our valued team of volunteers.

Our services are provided in:

  • Four main hospitals: Bronglais Hospital in Aberystwyth; Glangwili Hospital in Carmarthen; Prince Philip Hospital in Llanelli; and Withybush Hospital in Haverfordwest
  • Five community hospitals: Amman Valley and Llandovery hospitals in Carmarthenshire; Tregaron Hospital in Ceredigion; and Tenby and South Pembrokeshire hospitals in Pembrokeshire
  • Two integrated care centres: Aberaeron and Cardigan in Ceredigion, and several other community settings
  • 47 general practices (six of which are health board managed practices); dental practices (including four orthodontic); 97 community pharmacies; 43 general ophthalmic practices; and 8 ophthalmic domiciliary providers
  • Numerous mental health and learning disabilities service

title: Associate Dean (South East)
descriptionHtml:
The role of the Associate Dean helps support the Postgraduate Dean in embracing corporate, statutory and non-statutory functions, aligning with the NHSE mandate. The role is focused firmly upon improving patient and learner safety and experience and ensuring effective educational outcomes.

The Associate dean is professionally accountable to the Postgraduate Dean and managerially by a deputy dean.This is a South East role and the exact balance of this role, and how it co-ordinates with other Associate Deans in the South East will be considered through the recruitment process.

Leadership

  • To work with the Postgraduate Dean
  • To provide effective clinical educator leadership, contributing to the strategic development of the NHSE Workforce, Training and Education Directorate
  • To contribute to the vision of the local NHS and to enhance patient care by providing leadership and direction with respect to the quality of education and training

Quality and safety

  • To work closely with the Postgraduate Dean and their deputies to implement the NHSE Quality Framework

Programme Management

  • Specialty-specific matters and trainee/trainer concerns
  • Postgraduate programme management, including assessments, progression, rotations, support and remediation, OOP management, trainee management, careers support, less than full-time training, inter-deanery transfer, academic training, study leave and relocation, supported return to training, flexible portfolio training along with other workstreams

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms -- enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services.

In March 2025, the Government announced that NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care will increasingly merge functions, ultimately leading to NHS England being fully integrated into the department.

If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR).This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. You may opt out at any stage of the process.

Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices.

title: Anterior Segment Fellow in Ophthalmology
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited to a one year Anterior Segment Fellowship which is unique in offering exposure to two subspecialities: Cornea and Glaucoma.The fellow will gain experience in the medical and surgical experience in the management of glaucoma, cornea and the anterior segment. The candidate is expected to already be competent and independent in cataract surgery.

We are a small, friendly department and provide world class care in our two Ophthalmological surgical centres, at St Richard's, Chichester and Southlands Hospital which is a state of the art centre, built in 2017. There has been a substantial investment in the service in recent years to help us manage our workload.

Outside of work, West Sussex is an incredible place to live, offering a life on the South coast, with Southlands Hospital within walking distance of the sea. Life with us offers opportunities outside of work - please get in touch and come for a look around.

The post will involve travelling between the 2 sites on the basis of a set timetable, which may change after 6 months, depending on progress and departmental factors.

The doctor's timetable may need to be flexible, to allow for internal unexpected staff leave cover.

Participation in the on-call rota is expected 1:9

The post holder accepts that they will also perform duties in occasional emergencies and unforeseen circumstances at the request of the appropriate consultant, in consultation, where practicable, with their colleagues, both senior and junior. While it has been agreed between the professions that they will perform such duties, the Secretary of State stresses that additional commitments arising under this sub-section are exceptions and you should not be required to undertake work of this kind for prolonged periods or on a regular basis.Attend mandatory training updates as required.Undertake training as necessary in line with the development of the post and as agreed with the line manager as part of the personal development process.Achieve and demonstrate agreed standards of personal and professional development within agreed timescales.Identify own learning needs and jointly plan training requirements with your line manager

title: Clinical Fellow in Endometriosis and Gynaecological Robotic Surgery
descriptionHtml:
The post is for a 6+ month period, and is due to become available to start as soon as possible. Applications are invited from a committed and enthusiastic doctor for the above post who will work within the BSGE accredited Endometriosis Centre at St Michael's, supported by the friendly and cohesive team. This post may suit candidates with various aims, including those looking to gain experience prior to applying for SITMs in Management of Complex Non-Malignant Disease or Robotic Assisted Gynaecological Surgery, gain first author publications in peer reviewed journals, learn specialist endometriosis ultrasound scanning and gain experience of advanced laparoscopic and robotic techniques including excision of rectovaginal disease. They will NOT have any on-call commitments and have 1 day per week protected for research, quality improvement projects or pursuing related areas of specialist interest. They will also gain experience in regular endometriosis, specialist endometriosis scan, reproductive medicine and general gynaecology clinics.

This post has no on-call commitment.

Annual leave and study leave are covered prospectively. As a valued member of the team you will be included in the educational and training activities of the unit and encouraged to contribute to the teaching of nurses, and other junior doctors. St Michael's Hospital is a large teaching hospital and is part of Bristol NHS Foundation Trust with close linked with the University of Bristol.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust brings together more than 28,000 staff to deliver over 160 clinical services across thirteen hospital locations,operatingfrom three main sites at Southmead, Bristol citycentreand Weston.

With an annual turnover of £2.3 billion, we are now one of the largest NHS trusts in the United Kingdom. Our hospitals are spread across Bristol and Weston, join us and you can enjoy the very best of both worlds; city living within a stone's throw of the countryside or beside the seaside, both with easy access to all that theSouth Westhas to offer.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust values all people as individuals. As an equal opportunities employer actively working towards a diverse workforce we aim to recruit andretaina workforce whichrepresentsthe rich diversity of the local population at all levels and are committed to designing our services around the needs of individual patients and those around them.
