This post offers the opportunity to work within a supportive department of 14 consultants and 2 specialist grade colleagues, providing a comprehensive and efficient cellular pathology service.

Based at Yeovil District Hospital, Yeovil, with access to modern facilities, including a recently installed Cerebro tracking system and a fully digital Philips Intellisite pathology system, advanced laboratory equipment, and excellent administrative support. The role includes participation in a broad portfolio of MDT meetings, with flexibility for home working where agreed.

You will play an active role in teaching, training, and supervising Specialty Registrars, as well as contributing to departmental audit, quality assurance, and service development. The Trust strongly supports professional development, offering protected SPA time, mentorship, and opportunities to develop a specialist interest. Optional participation in hospital and Coroner's postmortems is available.

Working pattern - Monday - Friday 8am-5pm

This post is offered with a standard 10 PA contract however candidates who wish to work part time are welcome to apply and will also be considered.

Relocation package - in line with Trust policy

Target Start Date: January 2027

AAC Interview - TBC

Deliver a comprehensive range of histological and/or cytological diagnostic services

Take responsibility for the organisation, management, and delivery of histological and/or cytological diagnostic services for patients,

Ensure full compliance with all Trust policies, procedures, and governance requirements.

Support the education and development of Junior Doctors through the effective planning and coordination of teaching and training activities.

Provide mentorship and coaching to histopathology trainees, including conducting assessments and appraisals and implementing appropriate remedial actions where required.

Contribute to the teaching and training of undergraduate medical students within the department.

Lead and oversee clinical audit projects, actively supporting the development, monitoring, and reporting of Clinical Quality Standards.

Maintain professional competence and expertise through participation in an accredited Continuing Professional Development (CPD) programme.

Participate in both general histology quality assurance schemes and specialty-specific quality assurance programmes relevant to their area of practice.

Undertake research activities

Carry out the administrative and budgetary responsibilities associated with patient care and the effective operation of the department.

Provide cross-cover for colleagues during periods of absence and respond to urgent clinical demands and emergencies as required.

Actively engage in the annual appraisal and job planning process.

At Somerset NHS Foundation Trust, we're committed to supporting our employees with a range of benefits designed to enhance your professional and personal life. We offer:

  • Flexible working options to help you balance work and life
  • NHS pension scheme for long-term financial security
  • Generous annual leave allowance to recharge and relax
  • A strong focus on career development to help you grow and achieve your potential

Additionally, you'll gain access to our Blue Light Card, unlocking exclusive discounts on shopping, dining, and leisure activities, as well as NHS-specific perks to support you both inside and outside of work.

We are proud to foster a diverse, skilled, and inclusive workforce, and we encourage applications from all backgrounds.

Why Somerset? Somerset offers the perfect blend of idyllic countryside, outstanding areas of natural beauty, and breathtaking coastlines, with vibrant cities like Bristol, Bath, and Exeter just a short drive away - and only two hours to London.

The region is home to excellent educational facilities, and with affordable housing compared to other parts of the country, it's a great place to build both your career and your future.

Somerset truly has it all - the peaceful countryside and cosmopolitan city life, with something for everyone to enjoy.

employer: Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust
title: Clinical & Molecular Histopathology Senior Clinical Fellow
descriptionHtml:
The appointed individual will undertake the cut up of complex musculoskeletal pathology cases under supervision of a consultant histopathologist, and will supervise more junior / less experienced staff undertaking this task.

The individual will draft histopathology reports on specimens received from RNOH and from referred hospitals. In the first instance these reports will be jointly authorised with a consultant histopathologist but with time, it would be expected that the appointee would have gained sufficient knowledge and experience to sign out cases.

The reports are based on the interpretation of the microscopic features of tissue, the gross and/or radiological findings and appropriate additional tests including immunohistochemistry, fluorescence in situ hybridisation, and PCR-based tests including generation sequencing in the light of clinical information. The clinical information should be provided by those requested the tests, but information can also be accessed at the multidisciplinary meetings.

Draft the microscopic findings of cases that s/he has cut up and present the reports to a consultant histopathologist for authorisation (with time it would be expected that the appointee would sign out cases independently)

Undertake under supervision the gross analysis of complex specimens (only at RNOH), and /or supervise biomedical staff when undertaking cut up of non-complex cases

Undertake, develop and interpret molecular pathology tests for the diagnostic service

Develop the transformation to digital pathology

Undertake audits of the work performed in the pathology department

To work as a team with other members of the department to ensure that UKAS accreditation is maintained, and that the standards of the service are being continually improved

To participate in bio banking of material for operations performed at RNOH

To participate in CPD

To participate actively in departmental and consultant meetings

At RNOH, we're committed to being actively anti-discriminatory and actively inclusive. We recognise our brilliant people do brilliant work, and we offer rewarding careers, no matter what their background. We continue to strive to break down barriers to be the Trust where people come together because what they do matters, makes a difference and where they can thrive.

Joining our organisation means enjoying a wide range of staff benefits, including:

  • A dedicated Staff Wellbeing Hub, providing a space to relax and recharge away from the work environment.

At RNOH, we are more than a workplace--we are committed to patients, to excellence and the wellbeing of our staff.

title: General Practitioner (GP)  Dermatology
descriptionHtml:

The role will involve working collaboratively with colleagues to deliver safe, effective and patient-centred care in line with relevant clinical guidelines and governance standards.

Medinet Group is a leading UK provider of specialist clinical services, working in partnership with NHS organisations to increase clinical capacity, reduce waiting times and improve patient access to high-quality care.

Through our community healthcare provider, HealthHarmonie, we deliver a range of NHS community services, bringing specialist care closer to patients' homes. Working with NHS Trusts, Integrated Care Boards, Primary Care Networks and GP practices, we provide services across specialties including Dermatology, Ophthalmology, Gastroenterology, ENT and Diagnostic Services.

With over 20 years of NHS experience and a network of more than 6,000 registered clinicians, we are committed to delivering safe, effective and patient-centred care. We pride ourselves on creating a supportive environment where clinicians can develop professionally and make a meaningful difference to patients and local communities.

employer: Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Senior Clinical Fellow in Stroke Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Following the expansion of our Thrombectomy service to 24/7, we are looking to expand our Senior Clinical Fellow team in Stroke Medicine to provide 24/7 cover senior medical cover for our stroke service. You will be based at Royal Preston Hospital. This post is a permanent.

You will support the day-to-day delivery of hyper-acute, acute and rehabilitation stroke services, predominantly on the Stroke Ward (Ward 21), and work closely with Consultant Stroke Physicians, the stroke specialist nursing team, Emergency Department and Acute colleagues.

Key elements of this role include participation in ward rounds and emergency TIA clinics, leadership and support for junior trainees (including out-of-hours cover), high-quality patient care and administration, and active involvement in teaching, audit, clinical governance and continuing professional development.

The post holder will:-

  • Participate in the day to day functioning of Stroke Medicine, predominantly on the Stroke Ward.
  • Liaise closely along with stroke specialist nurse, with Emergency department colleagues and Acute team assessing acute strokes for further management.
  • Participate in consultant ward round and emergency TIA clinics.
  • Provide leadership for more junior trainees, especially when covering out of hours.
  • Promote high professional standards of clinical care for patients, both through direct patient care and by the maintenance of continuing professional development.
  • Undertake administrative duties involved with the care of his/her patients.
  • Promote high professional standards of clinical care of patients and the health and safety of the critical care environment.
  • Maintain continuing education and professional development.
  • Actively participate in the audit process.

Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the major acute trusts in the North West, with all of the usual specialties on site, as well as being a Tertiary Centre for Lancashire and South Cumbria in the Departments of Neurosciences, Nephrology, Oncology, Plastic Surgery and Burns.

Undergraduate medical student teaching commenced in Oct 2003. We offer the full range of acute outpatient and inpatient services to the 380,000 people living in Central Lancashire.

Our department offers you the opportunity to develop knowledge and skills in CGA and experience in caring for patients with traumatic injuries. You will also develop non-clinical skills in service development and quality improvement. You will be exposed to clinical governance aspects of the service (for example observational attendance at Coroners Court). Although this is not a formal training post, you will receive close clinical supervision in a supportive learning environment. You will receive educational opportunities and time to develop your interests and Portfolio.

We will care for your health and wellbeing alongside our junior doctor team. You will work within this supportive team which is continually striving to learn and improve.

title: Consultant Liaison Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
Somerset NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to appoint a fulltime Consultant Liaison Psychiatrist to join our team at Yeovil District Hospital (YDH).

Contract: Permanent

Hours: 10 PAs per week (7.5 DCC/2.5 SPA)

Working Pattern: Monday--Friday, 09:00--17:00

On-call Requirement: None

Role Overview: The post holder will provide specialist psychiatric assessment, management, and advice for patients admitted to YDH who require mental health input during their inpatient stay. You will work closely with acute hospital colleagues, mental health teams, and wider multidisciplinary services to support high-quality, integrated care.

Cross-Site Working: Some cross cover with Musgrove Park Hospital may be required during periods of colleague leave.

What We're Looking For: A committed, collaborative consultant psychiatrist who values liaison work, enjoys multidisciplinary environments, and is motivated to contribute to high-quality patient care across Somerset.

Applicants who do not currently hold Consultant status may also be considered at Specialist grade, subject to meeting the relevant eligibility criteria and person specification requirements.

Assessment and Management - Support existing liaison staff in the assessment, diagnosis, and management of adults presenting with mental health problems

Medical Leadership - Provide senior medical expertise to YDH teams caring for patients with functional or organic mental health conditions. This includes supervising the clinical caseload of liaison team members and overseeing the work of any trainee doctors attached to the service.

Clinical Decision Making -- Work with the liaison team to determine the most appropriate interventions for referred patients. Responsibilities include facilitating safe and timely discharge planning and ensuring effective communication with Primary Care, Community Mental Health Teams (CMHTs), and Inpatient Services. The Consultant will provide clinical leadership, particularly for patients with complex needs or elevated risk.

Responsible Clinician Duties - Act as the Responsible Clinician (RC) under the Mental Health Act for patients detained at YDH. During periods of annual or study leave for Musgrove Park Hospital (MPH) consultants, RC responsibility will transfer to this post.

Liaison with Acute Hospital Teams - Develop and maintain effective working relationships with medical, surgical, nursing, and allied health professionals within the acute hospital. Provide advice on the application of the Mental Health Act and Mental Capacity Act where relevant.

Special Interests may be developed through discussion and agreement at job plan review meetings.

At Somerset NHS Foundation Trust, we're committed to supporting our employees with a range of benefits designed to enhance your professional and personal life. We offer:

  • Flexible working options to help you balance work and life
  • NHS pension scheme for long-term financial security

Why Somerset? Somerset offers the perfect blend of idyllic countryside, outstanding areas of natural beauty, and breathtaking coastlines, with vibrant cities like Bristol, Bath, and Exeter just a short drive away - and only two hours to London.

title: Senior Clinical Fellow in Anaesthetics & ICU
descriptionHtml:
Training and Development

This 12-month post is designed to support the Fellow's progression towards a formal anaesthetic training number. Extension may be possible after the initial term, subject to service vacancies, satisfactory progress and an ARCP-equivalent assessment.The role can be tailored to the successful candidate's interests and training needs. This may include time in elective theatres to maintain anaesthetic skills and, where appropriate, opportunities to develop competencies in anaesthesia, intensive care or obstetric anaesthesia.

Education and Supervision

Each Senior Clinical Fellow is allocated a trained Educational Supervisor, who will monitor progress and provide mentoring for training and wider professional development. Formal review meetings will take place every three months, with additional informal meetings arranged as required.

During day shifts, the Senior Clinical Fellow will be fully supervised by consultants. Overnight, immediate supervision is provided by other resident on-call doctors, which may include NHS Deanery trainees, Senior Clinical Fellows or senior Staff Grade doctors. Off-site emergency support is also available from a General Anaesthetic Consultant and an Intensive Care Consultant.

Advert may close early upon receipt of considerable number of applications.

Covering elective lists in main theatres, obstetrics and intensive care, according to service requirements.

Participating in on-call duties across emergency theatres, obstetric theatres and ICU, in line with current skills and clinical need.

Actively contributing to departmental education, governance, morbidity and mortality meetings, audit and quality improvement activity.

Department of Anaesthetics

The Anaesthetics and Intensive Care offices are located in the former Trust headquarters on Route 109. The department includes shared consultant office space, an open-plan secretarial office and an integrated kitchenette. It provides a pleasant working environment with easy access to the Anaesthetic and Chronic Pain secretaries. A hot-desking area is also available near the West Wing theatres and ICU, with an attached lecture/seminar room and kitchen.

Intensive Care and High Dependency Units

A state-of-the-art Integrated Critical Care Unit opened in December 2018, bringing HDU and ICU services together in one location. The development increased bed capacity from 14 to 18 beds within an overall footprint of 1,360m.

The department provides a 24/7 outreach and sepsis service, including Martha's Rule. Rehabilitation services and follow-up clinics are supported by the ICU consultant team and the wider multidisciplinary team, including physiotherapy, speech and language therapy, and dietetics.

As the only provider of NHS acute care in Walsall, we offer a unique opportunity to be part of a Trust making a genuine difference to local health outcomes. The Trust is a busy district general hospital offering compete range of acute services, alongside extensive community services.

A new Urgent Emergency Care Centre was opened in March 2023. The two-storey development has significantly improved emergency care facilities and capacity and has provided almost 5,000 square metres of additional clinical space.

Our strategy is aligned to delivering exceptional care together while supporting a workforce that reflects the communities we serve. We offer clear career development pathways, access to training and education, and opportunities to contribute to service innovation and improvement.

employer: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Junior Clinical Fellow in Neurosurgery
descriptionHtml:
This is a 6-month fixed-term, non-training clinical post within the Neurosurgery Department at King's College Hospital. The post holder will work as a Trust grade SHO, with clinical duties spanning the full breadth of neurosurgical subspecialties and close collaboration with ICU, anaesthetics and paediatrics.

Responsibilities include inpatient care and out-of-hours on-call duties. The post is ideal for doctors with an interest in Acute Medicine, Critical Care, Neurosurgery or Neurology.

The appointees will offer 24h cover over Neuro HDU (Kinnier Wilson) and Neurosurgery (three inpatient wards). There is continuous support by the neurointensive care consultants throughout the working week and by the neuroanaesthetists during the weekends.

The Trust provides a full range of local and specialist services across its five sites. In June 2026, we launched our new strategy for 2026-31. Our vision is to transform healthcare, and we have agreed six strategic ambitions to help us improve care for patients, and the working lives of our staff.

Our six strategic ambitions are deliveringhigh-quality patient care; creating a great place to work; leading pioneering research, innovation and education; building strong and successful partnerships; providing timely and efficient care; and ensuring long-term financial sustainability.

We have also agreed four new organisational values - Caring, Collaborative, Inclusive, Innovative - and these underpin everything we do, and how our teams interact with the patients under our care.

We are at a pivotal point in our history and we require individuals who are ready to join a highly professional team and make a real, lasting difference to our patients and our people.

King's is committed to delivering Sustainable Healthcare for All via our Green Plan. In line with national Greener NHS ambitions, we have set net zero carbon targets of 2040 for our NHS Carbon Footprint and 2045 for our NHS Carbon Footprint Plus. Everyone's contribution is required in order to meet the goals set out in our Green Plan and we encourage all staff to work responsibly, minimising their contributions to the Trust's carbon emissions, waste and pollution wherever possible.

title: Locum Consultant Oncologist Upper and Lower GI Cancers
descriptionHtml:
Our Oncology team is delighted to welcome a passionate and collaborative colleague who shares our commitment to delivering outstanding, patient-centred cancer care.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a dynamic and forward-thinking service that provides comprehensive oncology care to the communities of Gloucestershire and Herefordshire. As we embark on an ambitious expansion of our regional Cancer Centre in Cheltenham, including the development of the new Gloucestershire Cancer Centre, there has never been a more inspiring time to join our team.

Working 10 Programmed Activities (PAs), Consultants typically see 150-200 new patients annually (around four new patients per week). You'll work closely with our established upper and lower GI teams, with excellent opportunities to participate in clinical research and service development.

While the role is advertised as a 10 PA post, we are very happy to discuss flexible or less-than-full-time working arrangements. We also welcome applicants with specific clinical or research interests, and we encourage informal conversations to explore how this position can best support your career ambitions. Join us in shaping the future of oncology care in Gloucestershire and Herefordshire and help us make a real difference for our patients and community.

Our Oncology Department is a thriving, well-established service comprising 16 Clinical Oncologists and 6 Medical Oncologists, supported by 3 Consultant Radiographers and 1 Consultant Nurse. The team is further strengthened by 13 WTE Specialist Registrars in Clinical and Medical Oncology, 5 Specialty Doctors, 12 Resident Doctors, and 3 Clinical Fellows.

We are proud of our dedicated team of nurse practitioners, who provide comprehensive acute care for our patients, including inpatient services, a 24-hour Acute Haematology Oncology Unit, an Acute Oncology Service, and assessment for patients receiving SACT.

This Oncology post will provide specialist expertise in upper and lower GI cancers across Gloucestershire and Herefordshire, contributing to the delivery of exceptional, patient-focused care. The successful applicant will:

  • Continue to strengthen established links with site-specialised teams through regular multidisciplinary team (MDT) meetings
  • Play an active role in developing and enhancing our multidisciplinary services
  • Foster strong collaborative relationships with colleagues across Oncology, Palliative Care, Medical and Surgical specialties, and Primary Care
  • Support access to clinical trials, ensuring as many patients as possible can benefit from research opportunities

Gloucestershire Hospitals provides acute hospital services from Gloucestershire Royal and Cheltenham General Hospital, with maternity services based at Stroud Maternity. As the largest employer in Gloucestershire, our 9,000-strong workforce, representing over 95 nationalities, delivers outstanding, patient-centred emergency, elective and specialist care across a broad range of clinical areas. We take pride in placing people at the heart of everything we do, working together as one team driven by shared ambition for continuous improvement.

The Gloucestershire Cancer Centre, based in Cheltenham, serves as a regional Cancer Centre for Gloucestershire, Herefordshire and South Worcestershire, as well as parts of Shropshire and Powys. The Centre registers over 5,000 new patients each year and is expanding to create a new, purpose-built facility with the transformation of our existing estate. This modern, welcoming space will ensure we remain at the forefront of oncology care for years to come.

Gloucestershire was named the best place to live in the UK byThe Sunday Times in 2021. It offers Cotswold countryside, the historic Cathedral in Gloucester and the Regency spa town of Cheltenham, renowned for its annual Cultural festivals. With outstanding schools and excellent transport links to Bristol, Birmingham, London and Wales, Gloucestershire offers an exceptional quality of life.

title: Salaried GP at Manchester teaching practice
descriptionHtml:
Valentine Medical Centre, 2 Smethurst Street, Manchester

Salaried GP - up to 10 sessions available.

Are you looking to settle down and enjoy the benefits of a friendly, sociable, training practice? We are looking for new members of our GP team. We have sessions available across the week and hope to recruit more than one person to make the total of 10 sessions.

Sessions available now and in January - flexible start date for the right candidates.

Starting salary from £11,000 per session per annum, negotiable depending on experience, plus indemnity.

We pride ourselves on peer support and opportunity for professional development, offering one to one partner mentoring to newly qualified GPs, as well as an opportunity to explore interests and ambitions for experienced GPs. We have a culture of education and learning with regular practice education sessions which we take turns to lead.

An informal visit to come and look around the practice and have the opportunity to meet some of the team is encouraged. Please email rebecca.blockley@nhs.net to arrange.

Our practice ethos is to combine high standards of clinical care and training, in a supportive environment designed to encourage you to thrive and develop any interests or ambitions.

We have daily informal meetings to catch up and check in with each other and discuss cases. We offer a named mentor GP partner to support newly qualified colleagues. Experienced colleagues can expect support and opportunity to engage with personal and practice development.

We are a GMS contract training practice in North Manchester. The practice population is a diverse list of around 11,000 patients. Our team includes 3 partner GPs, 5 salaried GPs, excellent experienced nurses, HCA, a focused care worker, practice pharmacist and dedicated prescription team, and a stable, accomplished administrative team lead by skillful managers. CQC rated Good: https://www.cqc.org.uk/location/1-544352441

employer: Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals NHS Trust
title: Junior Clinical Fellow in Acute Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Junior Clinical Fellow in Acute Medicine

We don't believe in long job adverts: instead, we offer the following:

An opportunity for a post of Acute Medicine Specialty Junior Clinical Fellow to join a rapidly expanding, dynamic team of Acute physicians, Nurses and Managers

All doctors receive a Trust and local induction and are offered a 4-week shadowing period

Annual and study leave allowance

The Trust is investing in an mSDEC service with an exciting new expansion to the Acute Medicine department

We can support candidates who are looking to go into a HEE training programme

In return we are looking for candidates who have:

Full registration with the General Medical Council

MRCP part 1 and significant experience in Acute Medicine

Up to date Advanced Life Support (ALS)

Junior Clinical Fellow in Acute Medicine

The Acute Medicine team at Barking, Havering and Redbridge Hospitals Trust (BHRUT) spans across both Queen's (QH) and King George Hospital (KGH).

KGH has a separate Medical Receiving unit (MRU) which is 28 bedded and an mSDEC unit. QH has an mSDEC which has a bedded area within it. Both mSDEC units receive patients directly from the Emergency Department (ED) via medical on call. Consultants and Trust Clinical Fellows cross covers both sites. Queen's hospital has a short stay ward, Sky A, which is a 29 bedded ward, which is also under acute medicine.

The post holder will join our dynamic acute assessment team across both sites. The Acute medical team is continuously expanding with a wonderful vision of excellent patient care, quick turnover, improving patient flow as well as amazing training facility for our trainees and junior doctors. Acute Medicine team are looking to recruit Clinical Fellows, all posts are as part of the recent vacancy and expansion of our service.

After successful recruitment the postholder will have an extensive induction by the Trust and Department and a period of shadowing to understand the activities of the department as well as our hospitals. An electronic induction pack will be supplied prior to formal induction. Post holder will be encouraged to complete online mandatory training after successful recruitment.

We're an organisation that is getting better and better and our improvements are driven by a determination to deliver care we're proud of and our patients are happy with.

They are benefitting from a new electronic patient record (we were the last acute trust in London to introduce one) and our maternity services have been rated good by the Care Quality Commission.

We operate from two main sites - KGH in Goodmayes and Queen's Hospital in Romford. We have two busy emergency departments with more than 346,000 people visiting them last year. We're campaigning to secure the £35m we need to transform the A&E at Queen's and get rid of corridor care.

We're proud of our regional Neurosciences Centre, Radiotherapy Centre and Hyper Acute Stroke Unit. We're also part of the North East London Cancer Alliance.

We run a Women's Health Hub in Ilford; an Ageing Well Centre in Hornchurch; and Community Diagnostic Centres (CDC) at Barking Community Hospital and at St George's Health and Wellbeing Hub. These CDCs are open 12 hours a day, 7 days a week.

The majority of our 8,400 staff - who come from 146 different countries - live in the three diverse London boroughs we serve and are from black, Asian and minority ethnic groups. Many can work flexibly and more than 400 of them are on our Ofsted accredited apprenticeship programmes. We're proud to be a London Living Wage employer.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Forest Medical is looking to welcome an enthusiastic, committed and patient-focused Salaried GP to join our friendly and supportive practice team in Mansfield.

The role will involve delivering high-quality general medical services, including face-to-face and telephone consultations, management of acute and long-term conditions, prescribing, reviewing results and correspondence, referrals and contributing to the effective management of our patient population.

We are keen to appoint a GP who enjoys working collaboratively and wants to become an integral part of the practice. We aim to provide a supportive working environment where doctors can develop professionally while maintaining a sustainable working pattern.

We are looking for a GP who is:

  • Patient-focused and committed to providing high-quality general practice
  • A good communicator and team player
  • Comfortable managing the breadth of clinical presentations encountered in general practice
  • Committed to safe prescribing, clinical governance and continuous professional development
  • Willing to contribute to the wider clinical and operational work of the practice

We are a friendly, supportive and forward-thinking practice with an experienced multidisciplinary team. We value collaborative working and aim to provide high-quality, patient-centred care while maintaining a positive and supportive working environment for our staff.

We offer a structured induction for new GPs, ongoing professional development and support to help colleagues settle into the practice and develop within their role.

We are keen to welcome a GP who shares our commitment to excellent patient care, teamwork and the continued development of general practice.

title: Consultant Radiologist (interest in Nuclear Medicine)
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a committed individual with a specialist interest in nuclear medicine to help lead and develop the nuclear medicine department together with our incumbent nuclear medicine physician. The post holder must be able to cover a full range of nuclear medicine imaging and have an ARSAC licence or be in a position to apply for an ARSAC licence on being appointed to the consultant post.This is a replacement post covering both adult and paediatric cases including subspeciality oncology nuclear medicine and cardiac scans. PET-CT reporting will also be encouraged, there are plans to install a new digital PET- CT scanner on the BRI site in the next 12-18 months which will cover both paediatric and adult patients from Bristol and surrounding region..A further subspecialty interest in oncological intervention and whole body MRI imaging would be welcomed but not essential.There is a general/acute radiology component to the post covering acute CT and MRI sessions and general diagnostic on call 1:21 weekdays and 1:15 weekends. The post is funded as a full time position (10 PAs including on call commitment).

The successful candidate will be expected to comply with all relevant Trust policies relating to administration of patient care. This includes working to set timescales for the triage of requests the completion of discharge summaries prior to patients being discharged, following the specified process for the management of patients that do not attend (DNA) their appointment or admission, and the completion of all paperwork deemed necessary to support the management of their patients within agreed timescales. Radiologists are also expected to work with service managers and clinical colleagues to manage their caseload in a flexible way, to ensure both clinical, national and local priorities, such as maximum waiting times for referral to treatment, are achieved.

This is a teaching Trust and the appointee will teach medical students as part of the commitment of their division to undergraduate education. On occasions, a practitioner may be asked to give lectures to healthcare professionals.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust brings together more than 28,000 staff to deliver over 160 clinical services across thirteen hospital locations,operatingfrom three main sites at Southmead, Bristol citycentreand Weston.

With an annual turnover of £2.3 billion, we are now one of the largest NHS trusts in the United Kingdom. Our hospitals are spread across Bristol and Weston, join us and you can enjoy the very best of both worlds; city living within a stone's throw of the countryside or beside the seaside, both with easy access to all that theSouth Westhas to offer.

Bristol NHS Foundation Trust values all people as individuals. As an equal opportunities employer actively working towards a diverse workforce we aim to recruit andretaina workforce whichrepresentsthe rich diversity of the local population at all levels and are committed to designing our services around the needs of individual patients and those around them. Anonymous information will be used from your applicationin order toensurewe'remeeting our pledge.

title: Consultant Community Paediatrician
descriptionHtml:
As part of an expansion of the service, we wish to appoint a Consultant Paediatrician in Community Child Health. Wye Valley NHS Trust is committed to providing first class care to the children and families of Herefordshire.

The post is based at the Child Development Centre in the City of Hereford, there may be some peripheral clinics in the county's special schools.

A good general Community Child Health background is essential; we are particularly looking to recruit a paediatrician with an interest and experience in autism/neurodevelopment.

Other special interests to complement the team, for example, neurodisability, ADHD, safeguarding, are welcomed and the opportunity exists for on-the-job development of special interests. For the successful applicant there is scope for leadership roles.

Applicants wishing to work less than full time are welcome to apply. Other flexible working options such as condensed working hours, e.g. working 40 hours over 4 day, and/or some remote working will be considered.

There is no on-call commitment with this post.

Closing Date- Monday 4 January 2027

AAC Date - Friday 22 January 2027

  • Clinical responsibilities will be adjusted to meet expertise and may include:

-Provision of clinics for Statutory Health Assessments for Children in Care

- Provision of neurodevelopmental clinics/ completion of ASD assessments

- Provision of clinics in one of the county's special needs schools

- Provision of general clinics

- Provision of clinics to provide medical advice to education

  • Equal admin to clinical time is allocated, e.g. a four hour clinic will have four hours of admin timetabled
  • SPA allocation of 1.5 PA per week with possibility of additional time, up to 2.5 PA for specific responsibilities
  • 1 PA of DCC to be agreed within the job plan per week to cover activities as required e.g.:

- Multi-agency meetings (Team around the Child; child protection conferences, etc.)

- Nursery and school visits

- Multidisciplinary meetings for children with complex needs

- Any clinical admin undertaken as a result of delivering any of the above clinical activities

Wye Valley NHS Trust is a member of an NHS Foundation Group with South Warwickshire NHS FT , the George Eliot Hospital NHS Trust and Worcestershire Acute Hospitals NHS Trust.

Located on the border with Wales in the shadow of the Black Mountains, we provide acute and community services across Herefordshire and into parts of Powys and run Hereford County Hospital and the community hospitals in Bromyard, Leominster and Ross-on-Wye.

Worcestershire is our neighbouring county. The post holder will be required to travel between sites.

We are a progressive and forward looking trust with ambitious plans to improve quality and integrate patient pathways through close collaborative working with our partners to deliver the quality of care we'd want for our family and friends.

More than 3,500 people work for the Trust - they tell us it's a great place to work, blending the busyness of a DGH with the benefits of working in a beautiful rural and unspoilt county like Herefordshire.

We can offer a great work-life balance and have a fine tradition of working with staff to help them achieve their full potential.

Frances Martin, Trust Chairman: "The strength of the Trust is its amazing staff; a great place to work, a great place to develop your career and a great place to reach your potential."

Our values - Care, Accountability, Respect and Excellence - are at the heart of all we do. We believe in providing the right care in the right place at the right time...all the time.

title: MRI Radiographer
descriptionHtml:

Our mission is to provide high-quality services within local communities to over 7 million patients by 2030. We are committed to ensuring that patients receive a positive experience, maintaining a 97% patient satisfaction rate.

employer: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
title: General Consultant in Diabetes and Endocrinology

title: Healthcare Assistant / GPA

employer: The Princess Alexandra Hospital NHS Trust
title: GP Interface Fellowship
descriptionHtml:
Shape the Future of Integrated Care Across West Essex and East Hertfordshire

Are you a GP looking for an opportunity to broaden your experience beyond traditional practice boundaries?

Are you interested in improving the way primary care, community services and hospitals work together for patients?

PAHT and EPUT are seeking two enthusiastic and forward-thinking GPs to join a new two-year GP Interface Fellowship.

This unique opportunity has been designed to support the next generation of clinical leaders working across the healthcare interface. Fellows will spend one day per week working alongside senior leaders and clinical teams across PAHT, EPUT and primary care to improve pathways, strengthen relationships and support the development of neighbourhood health services.The GP Interface Fellowship is a joint initiative between The Princess Alexandra Hospital NHS Trust (PAHT) and Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust (EPUT).

The fellowship seeks to develop future clinical leaders capable of working effectively across organisational boundaries and improving the interface between primary care, community services and secondary care.

Aligned to the Department of Health and Social Care Interface Programme, the NHS neighbourhood health agenda and local integrated care priorities, fellows will work

on practical improvement projects designed to enhance patient experience, reduce fragmentation and strengthen collaborative working across the health and care system.

Two GP Fellows will be appointed for one day per week over a two-year period. Fellows will contribute to a portfolio of projects across PAHT and EPUT and will be supported through supervision, mentoring and leadership development opportunities.The Princess Alexandra Hospital NHS Trust (PAHT) is proud to care for the communities of West Essex, delivering safe, compassionate, and high-quality services. We are part of the Neighbourhood Wave; a national programme thats changing how care is delivered by focusing on prevention, early support, and more joined-up services across health, social care, and the voluntary sector.

This means were working more closely with local partners to bring care closer to home and support people to live healthier, more independent lives.

Were a supportive and inclusive organisation that values its people. We offer development opportunities, flexible working, and a strong focus on wellbeing. As a Disability Confident and equal opportunities employer, we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and experiences.

Join us and help shape the future of care in West Essex.

title: Specialist in Paediatrics
descriptionHtml:
Specialist - Paediatrics: Permanent (7.56 sessions per week)

We are looking for an enthusiastic associate specialist paediatrician to become part of the team in Stockport.. The paediatric department in Stockport is a busy general paediatric department. title: Salaried General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:

descriptionHtml:
St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, in partnership with Kingston Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, is seeking a full-time Locum Consultant ENT Surgeon with a specialist interest in otology and lateral skull base surgery. The post involves delivering complex tertiary care at St George's Hospital, contributing to general ENT services at Kingston Hospital, and working within a hub-and-spoke network serving South West London.

The successful candidate will join the Lateral Skull Base MDT, collaborating with neurosurgery, audiology, radiology, and oncology colleagues, performing advanced otology and skull base procedures, and supporting service development, audit, and teaching. Leadership, mentorship, and academic engagement are also key aspects of the role.

This is an excellent opportunity to develop subspecialist expertise, contribute to high-quality, patient-centred care, and shape ENT services across the region.

Fixed Term-1 year

The post holder will provide a comprehensive Otology and Lateral Skull Base service across St George's Hospital and Kingston Hospital. Key duties include delivering specialist inpatient, day case and outpatient care, and contributing to the multidisciplinary skull base service at St George's.

The appointee will support the development of the otology and skull base service, including participation in audit, clinical governance, service planning, and maintenance of surgical and national databases.

At Kingston Hospital, the post holder will deliver otology clinics and middle ear surgery, work collaboratively with audiology services, and contribute to general ENT outpatient and day case activity.

The role also includes participation in emergency ENT care and on-call duties, providing senior clinical support when required.

In addition, the post holder will provide leadership, teaching, and mentorship to junior medical staff and the wider multidisciplinary team, while actively contributing to training, appraisal, and continuous professional development.

St. George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is one of the largest healthcare units in the United Kingdom accommodating around 1170 beds and treating around 89,000 inpatient and day cases, and over 448,000 outpatients annually. The Trust employs over 6,000 staff incorporating 1,100 Medical & Dental Staff. It provides general acute services together with specialty services including neurosciences, cardiothoracic, and specialist children's services

The Trust is on three sites, St George's Hospital, the base for acute general medicine and surgical services, Queen Mary's Hospital, Roehampton (QMR), and St John's Therapy Centre, Battersea, where services for care of elderly patients previously at Bolingbroke Hospital are now based. The Trust serves a resident population of about 300,000 and serves two local Primary Care Trusts, Wandsworth and Merton which have a total population of approximately 600,000 between them.

As well as acute hospital services, we provide a wide variety of specialist and community hospital based care and a full range of community services to children, adults, older people and people with learning disabilities. These services are provided from Queen Mary's Hospital, Roehampton, 11 health centres and clinics, schools and nurseries, patients' homes and Wandsworth Prison.

The Trust works closely in association with the Medical School and forms a joint cancer centre with the Royal Marsden.

title: PCN Frailty GP
descriptionHtml:
We have a fantastic opportunity for an experienced and motivated GP to join Folkestone, Hythe & Rural Primary Care Network as a Frailty GP.

We are an ambitious, innovative and forward-thinking PCN, recognised as being at the forefront of Integrated Neighbourhood Working across Kent and Medway.

Having been part of the national Neighbourhood Health Implementation Programme (NNHIP) pilot, we are helping to shape the future of neighbourhood healthcare.

This is a very exciting opportunity to join a progressive and dynamic environment, working within our established Integrated Neighbourhood Team to deliver a more proactive, responsive and joined-up approach to caring for patients living with frailty and complex needs.

We are looking for a GP who shares our ambition and enthusiasm for developing new ways of working.

Previous experience in frailty care would be highly desirable, although not essential.

Above all, we are seeking someone who is enthusiastic about integrated working and wants to play a key role in shaping the future of neighbourhood healthcare.

The post holder will act as a clinical leader for our established Integrated Neighbourhood Team, providing senior clinical leadership, oversight and guidance to a dynamic multidisciplinary team of clinicians and healthcare professionals.

The team delivers a combination of proactive and reactive care, supporting patients living with frailty, complex health needs and those at risk of deterioration or hospital admission.

The GP will play a key role in supporting clinical decision-making, managing complexity and ensuring a coordinated, patient-centred approach to care.

The role will involve working closely with a diverse range of professionals across neighbourhood services, providing clinical leadership and contributing to multidisciplinary discussions and care planning.

An important aspect of the role will be helping to lead and develop our innovative neighbourhood model, supporting new ways of working and shaping the future delivery of integrated care across our PCN.

Folkestone, Hythe & Rural Primary Care Network brings together seven GP practices serving a population of approximately 50,000 patients across a mixture of rural and urban communities.

Our member practices are Oaklands Health Centre, White House Surgery, Harbour Medical Practice, New Lyminge Surgery, Church Road Surgery, Sun Lane Surgery and Hawkinge and Elham Valley Practice.

Our population is diverse, covering communities with areas of significant deprivation alongside a high proportion of older patients and people living with frailty, multimorbidity and complex health needs.

We are an ambitious, progressive and forward-thinking organisation with a strong reputation for innovation, collaboration and developing new approaches to care.

Having participated in the national Neighbourhood Health Implementation Programme pilot, we have been at the forefront of Integrated Neighbourhood Working across Kent and Medway.

We have developed an established Integrated Neighbourhood Team, bringing together professionals from primary care, community health and wider partners to deliver more joined-up, proactive and responsive care.

We pride ourselves on creating a supportive and inclusive working environment where staff are valued, encouraged to contribute ideas and actively involved in service development.

This is an exciting time to join our PCN as we continue to build on our achievements and help shape the future of neighbourhood healthcare.

title: PCN Clinical Pharmacist
descriptionHtml:
The post holder will work as part of a multi-site, multi-disciplinary team in a patient-facing role. The post holder will take responsibility for managing targeted areas of chronic disease management within the practice and undertake clinical medication reviews to proactively manage patients with complex poly-pharmacy.

The post holder will provide support to general practice staff with regards to prescription and medication queries. They will help support the repeat prescription system, deal with acute prescription requests, and medicines reconciliation on transfer of care and systems for safer prescribing, provide expertise in clinical medicines advice while addressing both public and social care needs of patient in the GP practice (s).

Repeat prescribing review Practice repeat prescribing policies. Oversee the repeat prescribing reauthorisation process by reviewing patient requests for repeat prescriptions, reviewing medicines reaching review dates and flagging up those needing a review. Ensure patients have appropriate monitoring tests in place when required. Reduce inappropriate poly-pharmacy and wasteful prescribing and address public health and social needs of patients through clinical medication review. This would be a level 3 medication review looking at the patients full clinical condition e.g. blood monitoring, interface care arrangements, social isolation. Reconcile medicines following hospital discharge and work with patients and community pharmacists to ensure patients receive the medicines they need post discharge. Contribute to reductions in medicine related hospital admissions and readmissions by supporting patients to get the best outcomes from their medicines and identifying and addressing medicines related issues. Interface with community and hospital pharmacy colleagues and develop referral processes between primary care professionals including the promotion of the repeat dispensing service.

Manage Practice formularies to improve the quality, safety and cost effectiveness of prescribing. Implement drug withdrawals and alerts e.g. MHRA aimed at improving medicines safety.

employer: Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board
title: Locum Consultant in Gastroenterology
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Locum Consultant Gastroenterologist to join the Gastroenterology team within Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board (CTM UHB).

This vacancy will be based at the Royal Glamorgan Hospital (RGH) in Llantrisant, however the successful candidate will be required to work across CTM.

The successful candidate will be part of the Senior Clinician team that manage the Gastroenterology Ward at RGH as well as joining the Gastrointestinal bleed rota for CTM.

A complementary specialist interest would be welcomed.

Please be aware this is a locum consultant role for a fixed term of up to 6 months to cover long term sick leave.

Welsh and/or English speakers are equally welcome to apply.

Work with the rest of the consultant body to provide strong professional leadership within the department and deliver a high-quality service following clear departmental policies and guidelines.

oProvide professional and managerial supervision of junior medical staff.

oFollow UpToDate evidence-based practice for patients under their care to deliver safe and robust gastroenterology management: allowing for proper delegation to, and training of staff, to ensure that concise agreed management plans are clearly documented in the medical notes of all patients.

oUndertake ward rounds to identify and assess problems, plan management of care, and be actively available during the working week so that medical and nursing staff can communicate and consult freely.

oEnsure that an appropriate model of care is adopted which recognises the involvement of the multi-disciplinary team, the holistic needs of the patient and their family.

oEnsure that the use of medical and nursing resources within the department are utilised to the maximum potential.

oDevelop and maintain good communication with clinical colleagues across the Health Board regarding the treatment of their patients and the appropriate use of the department's resources.

o The new appointee will participate in a 1 in 11 GI Bleed on-call rota across RGH and PCH sites.

Cwm Taf Morgannwg (CTM) University Health Board, part of NHS Wales, serves a large population across a diverse and beautiful region, steeped in history and heritage. With nearly 13,500 staff, our health board is one of Wales's largest employers.

Together, we are Team CTM; a workforce dedicated to offering excellent patient care and support to the 450,000 people across our three regions, Bridgend, Merthyr Tydfil, and Rhondda Cynon Taf. We operate three District General hospitals, several community hospitals, primary and community care facilities.

CTM's location offers the best of South Wales, just 20 minutes from Cardiff's vibrant city life, the natural beauty of the Brecon Beacons, and the serene coastline at Ogmore. Whether you enjoy lively urban amenities, peaceful countryside, or seaside escapes, our location makes an ideal setting for both work and personal life.

Our CTM 2030 Strategy--Our Health, Our Future--focuses on uniting our region around shared health and wellbeing goals. Our values guide us daily:

o We listen, learn, and improve

o We treat everyone with respect

o We work together as one team

CTM employees enjoy benefits including; a leading pension, generous leave, flexible work, career growth, and access to ongoing learning and development.

At CTM, you'll find a welcoming, team-oriented workplace that values diversity and compassion, where you can take pride in your work and the difference it makes.

title: Head of School – Anaesthetics
descriptionHtml:
An outstanding individual is sought to fulfil the role of Head of School for Anaesthetics.

The post will be available on the basis of a secondment arrangement to NHS England remunerated on the NHS Consultant Pay Scale - 3 PA / 12 hours per week.

All work undertaken is to be incorporated into the Consultant Job Plan.

As Head of School, you will be responsible for the overall quality, management and supervision of the programmes within your School. You will be responsible for ensuring all programmes meet the standards defined by Health Education England, the GMC and Royal College. You will work closely with Health Education England's senior educators, other Heads of Schools, Directors of Medical Education, and Training Programme Directors to ensure that each trainee is able to access a comprehensive range of experiences which will enable them to cover the speciality curricula.

You will be expected to maintain a clinical commitment. It is essential that you have a medical degree, membership/fellowship of the relevant Royal College/Faculty and have a current substantive contract as an NHS Consultant in a relevant specialty. In addition, you should possess excellent leadership skills and meet professional requirements for Continuing Professional Development and Revalidation and make a wider professional contribution through academic and managerial responsibilities.

The post is offered on a secondment basis and all candidates are reminded that if they are successful, they are responsible for securing written agreement from their employer for release from clinical work for the specified number of PAs.

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms -- enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services.

In March 2025, the Government announced that NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care will increasingly merge functions, ultimately leading to NHS England being fully integrated into the department.

If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR).This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. You may opt out at any stage of the process.

Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices.

Staff recruited from outside the NHS will usually be appointed at the bottom of the pay band.

We cannot offer visa sponsorship for external candidates.

employer: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

descriptionHtml:
Shape the future of genomics in the South West.

Are you a Consultant in Clinical Genetics, or a Specialty Registrar nearing the end of your training, whos ready to help shape the future of a regional service without compromising on flexibility or impact?

Join the new South West Clinical Genetics Service a forward-thinking, patient-focused collaboration hosted by the Royal Devon based at St Michaels Hospital, Bristol, at a pivotal moment in its transformation. title: Pharmacy Technician - Bank/Flexi Contract
descriptionHtml:

employer: Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
title: NHS Locum Consultant Psychiatrist in Perinatal
descriptionHtml:
The Essex Perinatal Services were established in 2017 and has expanded in the last 5 years with hubs around the 5 maternity hospitals, Colchester General hospital, Broomfield Hospital, Princess Alexandra Hospital, Southend Hospital and Basildon Hospital. This expansion has been in accordance with the NHS E LTP so as to see around 10% of the birth rate (Essex birth rate is around 24,000 births per year) and in order to meet the needs of our population there is a requirement to have 5 consultants leading each of the 5 hubs.

The Community Perinatal Services for Essex provides multidisciplinary, community specialist care for the assessment and treatment of woman with mental health illnesses in pregnancy and postnatally across the County of Essex. The post- holder will serve the needs of patients across the North of Essex mainly linked to the Mid and North East areas of Essex including the 2 Acute hospitals Broomfield hospital in Chelmsford and Colchester General Hospital in Colchester. This will be reviewed periodically to ensure appropriate resource allocation to the different areas and any changes made shall be after deliberation.

The post holder will be expected to have expertise in the prevention, assessment and management of mental disorders newly occurring or co-existing with pregnancy or the postpartum period, including the assessment and facilitation of the mother-infant relationship in the context of maternal mental illness.

You will be required to work independently and accountably as part of a team of clinicians offering Mental Health services.

You will be expected to develop excellent working relationships with all other related services including Primary care, Maternity services, Health visiting, Community adult mental health teams, Adult Psychology team, IAPT, Social care and Voluntary sector agencies.

You will clinically covering the areas of Mid Essex and NE Essex which includes close partnership with Broomfield and Colchester Maternity Unit. The post holder will share the trust wide roles required within the Service with the other Consultants. The Service works in partnership with maternity services and the post holder will provide care and liaise closely with maternity staff for women delivering in Broomfield and Colchester General Hospitals

A perinatal mental health clinical network has been established across Essex and it is anticipated that you will take an active role in this and other regional or national initiatives to improve the quality of care and outcomes for women and families across the care pathway.

Work that wraps around your needs

employer: University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust
title: Trust Registrar in General Surgery
descriptionHtml:
Ready to take the next step in your surgical career? Join University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust as an ST3+ Trust Grade Registrar in General Surgery / Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC) at Leicester Royal Infirmary. This role offers the opportunity to combine senior clinical responsibility with consultant support, develop your decision-making skills and help deliver timely, patient-centred emergency surgical care.

You will be part of a supportive multidisciplinary team, working alongside a dedicated SDEC Consultant, resident doctors, Advanced Clinical Practitioners and nursing colleagues. In a busy service managing approximately 30-40 patients per weekday, you will assess and manage acute gastrointestinal and general surgical presentations, with a focus on ambulatory care, safe discharge and avoiding admission where clinically appropriate.

We are looking for an experienced surgical doctor who is keen to develop their clinical leadership and emergency surgical expertise.

Undertake senior clinical assessment, investigation, diagnosis and management of acute GI and general surgical presentations in the Surgical Triage/SDEC service.

Make timely decisions about treatment, admission, discharge and specialist review, supporting ambulatory pathways and admission avoidance where clinically appropriate.

Recognise deteriorating or clinically unstable patients and escalate promptly to the SDEC or on-call consultant team.

Assess and manage emergency surgical patients admitted directly to the surgical admissions ward from the Emergency Department.

Ensure safe discharge planning, appropriate safety-netting and follow-up, supported by accurate clinical documentation.

Provide clinical leadership and day-to-day supervision for resident doctors, and support the development of Advanced Clinical Practitioners and medical students.

Work collaboratively with nursing colleagues, Emergency Department teams, primary care, community providers and specialist services to support safe patient flow and coordinated care.

Participate in the SDEC/triage rota and morning and evening handovers, as well as ward rounds, outpatient clinics and theatre activity according to service requirements.

Contribute to clinical audit, quality improvement, service development, undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, and research, while maintaining professional development and mandatory training.

Our new strategy, developed with the support and feedback of colleagues, patients, and partners, is our compass for the next seven years (2023-2030).

We have four primary goals:

  • high-quality care for all,
  • being a great place to work,
  • partnerships for impact, and
  • research and education excellence

And we will embed health equality in all we do - taking active steps to reduce the avoidable differences in healthcare that some people face, working in partnership with communities.

Our strategy is underpinned by new values and we will work to ensure they are an everyday reality for all:

  • we are compassionate,
  • we are proud,
  • we are inclusive, and
  • we are one team

This is an exciting moment as we look to the future with clarity on what we already do well and where we need to focus our energies to make an even bigger difference for the people we serve.

title: National Clinical Lead
descriptionHtml:
This post is secondment for 2 years

Applications are invited for the following National Clinical Lead roles:

  • Maternity, Neonatal, Women's & Children's Health
  • Chronic Conditions
  • Ageing Well & End of Life Care
  • Planned Care, Cancer & Diagnostics
  • Urgent & Emergency Care
  • Improvement & Transformation

About the Role

We are seeking experienced and influential clinical leaders to provide strategic clinical leadership across NHS Wales Clinical Programmes.

National Clinical Leads will play a pivotal role in shaping and supporting the delivery of national priorities, working collaboratively with Programme Directors, Programme Leads, healthcare professionals and wider system partners to improve outcomes, quality, safety and equity for the population of Wales.

These roles will help strengthen national clinical leadership capacity across the Clinical Programmes Division and establish the leadership foundations required to support the delivery of NHS Wales Performance and Improvement objectives.

Within NHSWP&I, clinical programmes are the core delivery mechanism for system improvement, aligned to national and health board priorities. Each programme acts as the 'knowledge-to-practice' element of the Learning Health and Care System described in the National Clinical Framework (NCF), connecting national policy and evidence with local delivery, with clinical leadership at its centre. Programmes move NHS Wales from fragmented, condition-specific working to integrated, pathway-based models, with clear accountability and measurable impact.

Each clinical programme exists to diagnose system challenges using data, quality intelligence and triangulated evidence; to provide improvement and implementation support that turns national policy and evidence into practical change; to enable collaboration between health boards, primary care and third sector partners; and to drive consistent, equitable standards and pathways that reduce unwarranted variation. Programmes work to five shared principles: outcomes, value, equity, a matrix and pathway approach, and data-driven improvement.

NHS Wales Performance & Improvement (formerly the NHS Wales Executive) has an important and valuable role in the delivery of key Welsh Government priorities:

o To support NHS Wales to deliver better health services for patients and the publico To support Ministers to hold NHS Wales to account for the provision of health servicesSince its inception in April 2023, strong foundations have been put in place within NHS Wales Performance & Improvement (NHS P&I) - including a more joined up and informed approach between policy development and operational NHS delivery, and improved coordination and collaboration across whole systems and pathways. Building on this foundation, NHS P&I aims to be an acknowledged centre of excellence in its field, efficient and responsive to the needs of both NHS Wales and Ministers, supporting best practice, and streamlining accountability.

NHS P&I will support the NHS by providing:

  • Improvement services
  • Innovation support
  • Value and sustainability support
  • Clinical expertise in service improvement, drawing on the best in Wales
  • Regional delivery support

NHS P&I will support Ministers by providing:

  • Financial delivery support

  • Planning advice
  • Advice to Welsh Government on use of powers of directions and intervention

The post holder will be supported and expected to develop into a recognised senior decision-maker within the department within 12 months of commencing the role.

Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust was created on October 1, 2007 by merging St. Mary's NHS Trust and Hammersmith Hospitals NHS Trust and integrating with the faculty of medicine of Imperial College London. One of the largest NHS trust in the country, we have come together to establish the UK's first academic health science centre (AHSC). The Trust has an annual turnover of over £950 million, approximately 10,000 staff, and it see over 500,000 patients a year.

The creation of the AHSC, a partnership between the NHS and Imperial College London, is a major advance for patient care, clinical teaching and scientific invention and innovation. The fusion of the different strands of our work and the achievements that can now be realised will lead to significant benefits for patients and greater advances in healthcare than could be delivered apart.

Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust already has a world-leading reputation. Hammersmith and St Mary's hospitals have two of the highest clinical ratings in the country, rated second and third best Trusts for clinical performance, quality of care and safety.

The Trust was awarded the status of a generic Biomedical Research Centre by the National Institute of Health Research (NIHR) in 2006 for its excellence in translational and clinical research - one of only 5 in the UK.

Working closely with thePCN Clinical Director, you will coordinate the day-to-day business of the PCN and ensure that our contractual, workforce, financial and strategic priorities are delivered effectively.

This is a broad and influential role. You will oversee PCN operations, workforce and HR processes, Network Contract DES and enhanced-service delivery, financial monitoring, governance, performance reporting, service improvement and the implementation of new initiatives. You will also help strengthen relationships between our practices and with neighbourhood, community, mental health, social care, voluntary-sector and NHS partners.

We are seeking someone who combines strong organisational discipline with sound judgement, initiative and excellent communication. You must be able to manage multiple priorities, follow work through to completion and provide clear, timely assurance to clinical and practice leaders.

Provide effective day-to-day operational management of Harrow East PCN, working with the Clinical Director to translate priorities into clear plans, actions and measurable outcomes.

Coordinate delivery of theNetwork Contract DES, enhanced services and PCN programmes, ensuring deadlines, submissions, performance, risks and actions are effectively managed.

Oversee thePCN and ARRS workforce, including workforce planning, recruitment, induction, training, supervision, appraisal and performance processes.

Monitorbudgets, funding, expenditure and claims, supporting effective financial management and value for money.

Produce clearreports, dashboards, Board papers and performance informationto support decision-making and improvement.

Maintain robustgovernance and assurance, including risk management, policies, action tracking and contractual requirements.

Build strong relationships across member practices and with theICB, other PCNs and health, social care and voluntary-sector partners.

Supportintegrated neighbourhood working, helping develop proactive, coordinated and joined-up care.

Supportpatient engagement and PCN communications, including the website and other public-facing information.

Harrow East Primary Care Network is a collaboration betweenHoneypot Medical Centre, Bacon Lane Surgery and Mollison Way Surgery, working together to improve access, quality, workforce resilience and outcomes for our local population.

We have a diverse multidisciplinary workforce delivering services including clinical pharmacy, care coordination, social prescribing, first-contact physiotherapy, mental health support, respiratory services, enhanced access and proactive and frailty care.

We have a strong focus onpopulation health, reducing health inequalities, patient engagement and continuous improvement. Our recent patient-access programme has included PCN-wide audits and surveys and a patient engagement event attended by approximately 200 patients.

The PCN is also actively involved in developing integrated neighbourhood working across East Harrow, alongside community services, mental health, social care, public health and the voluntary sector.

This is an excellent opportunity to join an ambitious, clinically led PCN and play a central role in its continued development.

employer: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locally Employed Doctor Higher in Rheumatology
descriptionHtml:
The Locally Employed Doctor (LED Higher) in Rheumatology will work as part of the multidisciplinary Rheumatology team at Solihull Hospital, providing high-quality, safe and effective care to patients with a range of rheumatological conditions. The post holder will participate in outpatient clinics, assess and review inpatient referrals and support patients attending the Rheumatology day-case service. The role will also include participation in the hospital medical on-call rota, contributing to the assessment and management of unwell medical patients. The post holder will work closely with consultants, nursing, therapy and wider multidisciplinary colleagues and provide specialist advice to primary and secondary care teams. The role provides opportunities to develop clinical expertise while contributing to teaching, clinical governance, audit, quality improvement and service development. Strong communication, organisational and clinical decision-making skills are essential, including the ability to manage competing priorities effectively. This post is part-time 32 hours a week, fixed term covering maternity until 04/01/2028.

*Deliver outpatient Rheumatology clinics and provide high-quality patient care.

*Assess and manage inpatient Rheumatology referrals.

*Support patients attending the Rheumatology day-case and infusion service.

*Participate in the hospital medical on-call rota, assessing and managing acutely unwell medical patients.

*Work collaboratively with consultants, specialist nurses, therapists and the wider multidisciplinary team.

*Provide Rheumatology advice to primary and secondary care colleagues.

*Contribute to clinical governance, audit and quality improvement.

*Support teaching and development of junior doctors, medical students and other healthcare professionals.

*Contribute to service development, improving patient access, experience and productivity.

*Maintain high standards of clinical practice, patient safety and effective communication.

University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust strives to have an inclusive culture where everyone feels like they belong, can thrive, knows that they add value and feels valued. We do this by developing compassionate and culturally competent leaders, being values driven in all that we do and by creating a welcoming and inclusive workplace that thrives on the diversity of our people. As such we want to attract and recruit talented individuals from all backgrounds, and for each of you to feel supported for the diversity you bring, to achieve your full potential.
