employer: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
title: Salaried General Practitioner - Willow Group
descriptionHtml:
The Willow Group are looking for a Salaried GP to join our ever expanding team. You will be part of a dynamic team responsible for providing sustainable, population-based health and social care, while ensuring our patients are seen in a timely manner by the most appropriate clinician within the Extended Primary Care Team.

The Willow Group is unique; we are partnered with Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, which is one of the largest Community and Mental Health Trusts in the UK. This comes with the opportunity to expand your knowledge and develop your skills within multidisciplinary teams in different specialties.

The Willow Group work over 4 Sites providing:

*GP led, working with a highly skilled team of ANPs, Nurses, Pharmacists, CPNs, First Contact Practitioners in MSK, Physician's Associate, Paramedic, Social Prescribers and supported by a motivated and efficient admin team

*Training for FY2s, GP Registrars, Nurses and Physicians Associates

*Primary Care Research

*Same Day Access Service

*Home Visiting Service

*A Strong MDT approach to routine care

*15 minute appointments offering flexibility of telephone, video, on-line or face-to --face consultations

*Clinical administration sessions

*Forward thinking and innovative PCN

In general the post-holder will be expected to undertake all the normal duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care including:

Making professionally autonomous decisions in relation to presenting problems

Consults with patients in the surgery, at home visits and via telephone or on-line mechanisms

Undertakes triage calls, triage visits, checking and signing of repeat prescriptions

Screens patients for disease risk factors and early signs of illness.

In consultation with patients and in line with current Practice disease management protocols, develops care plans for health.

Provides counselling and health education as necessary.

Admits or discharges patients to and from caseload and refers them to other care providers internally and externally as appropriate

Complies with all relevant clinical governance and Practice polices and protocols.

Assists in the establishment of appropriate systems to manage common chronic medical conditions.

Records clear and contemporaneous consultation notes to agreed standards.

Provides active input to the wider Primary healthcare team in the process of health needs research/base line data collection/clinical audit.

Compiles and issues computer-generated acute and repeat prescriptions, prescribing in accordance with the Practice/Fareham & Gosport CCG prescribing formulary

Meets professional learning and CPD requirements.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust provides joined-up mental and physical healthcare for around two million people across our communities. With over 13,000 staff working in the community and local hospitals, we deliver care at every stage of life, helping people live their best and healthiest lives.

Our mental health services include community-based support and early intervention in psychosis (EIP) for both adults and young people, alongside a network of specialist inpatient wards covering forensic, learning disability, eating disorder and older person's care.

We deliver extensive physical health services too, from urgent community response teams helping frail and older patients remain safely at home, to hospitals at home teams providing acute-level care in familiar surroundings. Our neurological services offer rehabilitation and treatment for conditions including Multiple Sclerosis, Parkinson's Disease, Motor Neurone Disease, Head Injury, Cerebral Palsy and Stroke. Across Hampshire, our community hospitals provide inpatient rehabilitation as a step down from acute care, and our dedicated teams also staff Treetops Sexual Assault Referral Centre in Portsmouth, offering expert, compassionate support.

Everything we do is underpinned by our CARE values of compassion, accountability, respect and excellence

employer: Alder Hey Children's NHS Foundation Trust

descriptionHtml:

Alder Hey Children's NHS Foundation Trust is seeking an enthusiastic and committed Consultant Paediatrician to join our evolving Children and Young People's Gender Service (CYPGS). This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to a multidisciplinary, holistic service supporting children and young people experiencing gender-related distress.

The post holder will play a key role in delivering specialist paediatric assessment and care, working collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team including psychology, psychiatry, nursing, and allied health professionals. You will help shape and develop a responsive, evidence-informed service focused on the wellbeing, safety, and individual needs of young people and their families.

This dedicated community-based service provides timely access to multi-disciplinary assessment and intervention to children and young people from across the country, predominantly those in the north, up to the age of 18. The North West service works closely and aligns with other regional hubs already 'live' or currently in development.

  • Provide comprehensive paediatric assessment and ongoing care for children and young people referred to the Gender Service
  • Work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team to develop personalised care plans and improve pathways for children and young people
  • Contribute to service development, clinical governance, and quality improvement initiatives
  • Development of pathways and protocols to improve care for children with complex
  • needs
  • Participate in safeguarding processes and holistic risk assessment
  • Support teaching, training, and supervision of junior medical staff and multidisciplinary colleagues
  • Engage in research and service evaluation where appropriate

As one of Europe's biggest and busiest children's hospitals, at Alder Hey Children's NHS Foundation Trust, we treat everything from common illnesses to highly complex and specialist conditions.In addition to our main hospital site, we offer paediatric services at a number of community sites and hold local clinics across Merseyside, Cumbria, Shropshire, Wales and the Isle of Man. We also provide specialist inpatient care for children with complex mental health needs in our recently relocated and newly opened state of the art facility.

Alder Hey has a thriving research portfolio and leads research into children's medicines, infection, inflammation and oncology. We are becoming recognised as one of the world's leaders in children's healthcare and research. We contribute to public health, lead cutting-edge research and teach the next generation of children's specialists. Alongside this is ourInnovation Hub, a dedicated space where clinicians and industries can come together to create new products and technologies.

As well as giving them the very best care, we set out to make them feel happy, safe and confident as they play, learn and grow. At Alder Hey we are here to look after a child and their family and that includes mums, dads, brothers and sisters.

title: Locum Consultant Child & Adolescent Psychiatrist (Inpatient CAMHS)
descriptionHtml:

Fixed Term - 12 months.

10 sessions per week.

Our mission is to make a positive difference to people's lives by improving the quality of life for all we serve. Our values are: We Care, We Respect, We are Inclusive - so we are looking for people who champions these qualities when supporting service users and carers, and in their relationships with colleagues in the Trust and our partner organisations.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Job summary

Why were recruiting. After over 30 years at Churchmere, our senior partner is retiring. Were looking for a permanent salaried GP to join us for 68 sessions. For the right person, there is the opportunity to progress to partnership in the future.

How weve built the GP role. Our nurse-led team handles much of the acute same-day demand. Our paramedic team do the bulk of home visits. Weve also worked hard to strip hidden admin out of the GP day.

Competitive salary, dependent on experience, on BMA model contract terms, plus the NHS Pension.

6 weeks annual leave and 1 weeks study leave.

15-minute appointments.

A fair, shared duty rota.

Daily clinical coffee at 11am where questions get asked, cases get shared, and nobody is left alone with a difficult decision.

Extended access and out-of-hours extra work opportunities (not essential) for additional income.

GP buddy scheme one-to-one mentoring and support from one of our GP partners.

Come and see us. For an informal chat or a visit, contact Jenny (managing partner) at jdavies12@nhs.net or Nick (GP partner) at nick.vonhirschberg@nhs.net. Wed rather meet you over coffee than over a form.

Skilled Worker visa sponsorship is available for eligible candidates.

Youll provide face-to-face and remote consultations, with the support of a nurse-led acute team and a paramedic home-visiting service. Youll manage results and correspondence for patients within a streamlined workflow, and youll be encouraged to develop a clinical or portfolio interest with practice support.

Churchmere Medical Group serves approximately 21,300 patients from a new purpose-built surgery in Whitchurch and a second site in Ellesmere, on the ShropshireWales border.

Were an established training practice with a long-standing reputation for GP education. There are teaching opportunities for GPs who want them.

They arent just a list of job titles. Theyre how weve designed a GP role that is sustainable and rewarding.

Were part of North Shropshire PCN, which covers six practices and around 80,000 patients. Through the PCN there are opportunities in care homes, cancer, education and leadership for GPs with portfolio ambitions.

Were within easy reach of Chester, Wrexham, Shrewsbury, Nantwich and Oswestry.

title: Locum Haematology Consultant - Acute Leukaemia & Stem Cell Transplant
descriptionHtml:
University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is delighted to offer a fantastic opportunity to work with us.

Job Title: Locum Consultant Haematologist with an Interest in Acute Leukaemia and Stem Cell Transplant

Start Date: Feb 2027

Contract Type: Fixed term - Maternity Cover

Fixed Term End Date: 1. 12 month contract 2, 6 month contract

Further details about the role can be found in the job description below.

We are looking for two locum haematologists with an interest in acute leukaemia and stem cell transplant. One post will be for 6 month and a second post for 12-months. The posts are available from February 2027. There is a plan for a substantive appointment in 2027.

The JACIE accredited Wessex Blood and Marrow Transplant and Cellular Therapy Service (WBMTCT) Programme has been providing an allogeneic transplant programme since 2001 with a catchment population of 3.7 million. The programme performs approximately 140 autologous transplants and approximately 60-70 allogeneic transplants per year. The CAR-T programme started in 2021 and been growing since. Our transplant outcomes are consistently ranked one of the best in Europe.

The post offers wide experience in the management of patients with haematological malignancies and stem cell transplantation, including teenage and young adult patients. This includes:

- Management of allogeneic transplant patients in inpatient, outpatient and day unit

- Inpatient attending on a 1:4 basis covering acute leukaemia, BMT and cell therapies

- 1:6 non-resident out of hours consultant cover for acute leukaemia BMT and cell therapies

- Active involvement with the delivery and development of the WBMTCT service

- Participation in the laboratory diagnosis of haematological malignancies

As one of the largest acute teaching Trusts in England, we offer learning and development opportunities to help you achieve the career you aspire to. UHS is rated 'Good' by the CQC and in the latest national NHS Staff Survey, we were in the top 10 acute trusts for staff engagement and for staff recommending the hospital as a place to work or receive care.

We support flexible working and will consider requests taking into account the needs of the service. UHS employees are able to access a range of NHS discounts, are entitled to a minimum of 35 days paid holiday (pro rata), and we offer a generous pension scheme.

Southampton is an attractive place to live and work situated on the south coast, with an international airport and direct trains to London. The New Forest National Park and beaches of the Jurassic coast are also right on our doorstep. The city offers living costs 30% lower than London and 17 schools rated outstanding by Ofsted.

employer: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Psychiatrist - General Adult Inpaitent
descriptionHtml:
This full-time Consultant in General Adult Psychiatry post is based on Trinity Ward, a female acute inpatient ward at Antelope House in Southampton. The post holder will provide senior clinical leadership within the Acute and Crisis Pathway, delivering assessment, treatment and ongoing management for adults with severe and complex mental health needs requiring inpatient care. The Consultant will act as Responsible Clinician for an allocated caseload, working closely with a multidisciplinary team that includes nursing, psychology, occupational therapy and medical colleagues. The role includes supervision of junior medical staff, participation in service development, clinical governance, teaching and quality improvement activities. The post comprises 10 Programmed Activities per week (7.5 DCC and 2.5 SPA), together with an additional inpatient PA and 10% responsibility allowance. The successful applicant will join the Southampton consultant on-call rota and will be supported through CPD, mentoring opportunities and leadership development within Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust.

The post holder will provide consultant leadership and clinical care on Trinity Ward at Antelope House, acting as Responsible Clinician for an allocated inpatient caseload and supporting the assessment and treatment of adults with severe and complex mental health needs. The role includes management of patients presenting with significant risk, complexity and acuity, ensuring care is delivered in line with recovery-focused and evidence-based practice.

The Consultant will work closely with colleagues across the Acute and Crisis Pathway, including inpatient wards, the Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team, community mental health teams and specialist services. They will provide supervision and support to junior medical staff, contribute to multidisciplinary decision-making, and participate in cross-cover arrangements with consultant colleagues.

The post holder will contribute to clinical governance, service development, audit and quality improvement activities, supporting learning from incidents, complaints and patient feedback. They will participate in teaching and training for medical students, doctors in training and multidisciplinary staff, while contributing to the ongoing development of inpatient mental health services. The role includes participation in the Southampton consultant on-call rota, leadership within the multidisciplinary team, and supporting the strategic development of services across the Acute and Crisis Division.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is a newly established organisation, bringing together expertise from across mental health, learning disabilities, community, and physical health services. We are dedicated to delivering compassionate, high-quality, and accessible care to the diverse communities of Hampshire and the Isle of Wight.

With over 13,000 dedicated staff working across more than 300 sites, we place patients and staff at the centre of everything we do. Our goal is to create an integrated healthcare system that improves accessibility and ensures more consistent care for patients. By working together, we aim to improve patient outcomes, drive innovation, and meet the unique needs of the populations we serve.

Our Trust unites services from Southern Health, Solent NHS Trust, Isle of Wight NHS Trusts community and mental health teams, as well as Hampshire CAMHS, originally part of Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust. This transformation enables us to deliver more seamless care across the region, ensuring that patients receive the right support, in the right place, at the right time.

Join us as we embark on this exciting journey to shape the future of healthcare across Hampshire and the Isle of Wight. We are deeply committed to our CARE values of compassion, accountability, respect, and excellence, and offer outstanding opportunities for career development, training, and collaborative working.

title: Brent Health Inequalities GP CYP
descriptionHtml:
Are you a GP passionate about tackling health inequalities and improving outcomes for children and young people?

An exciting opportunity has arisen to join Brent Health Matters (BHM) as a Salaried GP - Children & Young People (CYP), working 0.10 WTE within our Children's Health Inequalities Team, based in Brent (HA0 3HG).

Brent Health Matters is an innovative community programme focused on reducing health inequalities and improving access to healthcare for underserved communities. Our CYP service works proactively with children, young people and families who may experience barriers to accessing traditional health and community services.

Working as part of a supportive multidisciplinary team, including senior nurse clinicians, a healthcare coordinator and service lead, you will provide clinical expertise and contribute to holistic, person-centred care.

Our key priorities include improving immunisation uptake, supporting the proactive management of long-term conditions including asthma and mental health needs, and connecting children, young people and families with appropriate community services.

We are looking for a compassionate, collaborative and proactive GP who is passionate about making healthcare more accessible and helping us further develop the Brent Health Matters model.

This is an exciting role for someone with an interest in health inequalities and able to understand the current barriers affecting our population group along with utilising your existing knowledge of Brent and experience of working in Brent with BrentGPs.

In this role, you will be required to liaise with the registered child's GP for families who seldomly access health care, provide professional support to the services, clinically review and advise on abnormal investigations and medical escalations. You may occasionally support community events that are offered as part of the wider Brent Health Matters programme delivery.

We are currently recruiting to 1 session/ week for the children's BHM team - the main scope of the role will be to work alongside the clinical lead to ensure appropriate clinical governance across the service, to lead/ participate in a multidisciplinary team meeting, to support the team with clinical queries and to support liaison back with GP practices. If you have the passion to continue our ongoing work to support our identified patient cohorts and we particularly welcome applications from a diverse range of backgrounds or at any stage in their career.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
This is a new consultant post created to provide medical leadership to Ealing's new Specialist Outreach Psychosis Service, which brings together the existing Community Rehabilitation Service (CRS) and a new Assertive Outreach (AO) function under a single clinical and operational structure, each delivered as a distinct "pathway" of one team with a single Team Manager. title: Advanced Medical Practitioner - Care Homes
descriptionHtml:
South Doc Services (SDS) is hiring an Advanced Medical Practitioner (AMP) on behalf of West Heath Surgery.

This will be a full time, permanent role with a 37.5 hours per week contract arrangement. The job location is at West Heath Surgery, 194 - 196 West Heath Road, Birmingham, B31 3HB. Pay / Salary is dependent on experience level.

If you wish to have the full job description, please email rhiannon.aiken@nhs.net

The Advanced Medical Practitioner (AMP) will provide high-quality, safe, effective and person-centred clinical care to patients registered with West Heath Surgery who reside in designated care homes.

The post-holder will work as an integral member of the Practice multidisciplinary team, working collaboratively with GPs, advanced practitioners, practice nurses, clinical pharmacists, community nurses, therapists, care coordinators, social care professionals, care-home staff and other relevant health and social care professionals.

The post-holder will contribute to the delivery of proactive, personalised and coordinated healthcare for care-home residents, with an emphasis on:

  • prevention of avoidable deterioration;
  • early identification and management of acute illness;
  • proactive management of frailty and long-term conditions;
  • personalised care and support planning;
  • medicines optimisation in collaboration with the appropriate prescriber/pharmacy professional;
  • reducing avoidable hospital admissions;
  • facilitating timely access to secondary and community care;
  • supporting residents to remain in their preferred place of care wherever clinically appropriate;
  • effective multidisciplinary working;
  • continuity and coordination of care; and
  • safe, evidence-based clinical decision-making.

The role will support the Practice in delivering its contractual requirements under the current NHS England Network Contract DES and Enhanced Health in Care Homes arrangements. The current EHCH model is designed around proactive, personalised and integrated care for people living in care homes rather than a predominantly reactive model.

The post-holder will work within their individual scope of professional practice, competence and authority. Where an activity requires GP, consultant, specialist or other professional input, the AMP will recognise this promptly and escalate appropriately.

Please note, this role is for West Heath Surgery, not South Doc Services.

West Heath Surgery is located within West Heath Medical Centre. We aim to provide first class up to date healthcare to the community while maintaining a family doctor relationship with all patients enabling continuity of care throughout a patients life. The Practice will continue to provide patient focused services using the criteria of clinical excellence providing healthcare to the community with equity and equality of access.

title: GP Clinical Lead (Frailty)
descriptionHtml:
Hertsmere Proactive Anticipatory Care (PAC) Service

4.5 Sessions per Week (18.75 hours)

£12,000 per session

Help Shape One of Hertsmere's Flagship Neighbourhood Programmes

Herts Health Federation is seeking an enthusiastic and forward-thinking GP to join the new Hertsmere Proactive Anticipatory Care (PAC) Service.

The PAC service is one of Hertsmere's flagship neighbourhood transformation programmes, developed through a partnership between:

  • Herts Health Federation
  • Central London Community Healthcare NHS Trust (CLCH)
  • West Hertfordshire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust

with funding support from Macmillan Cancer Support.

The service has been designed to identify people earlier, intervene proactively and coordinate support around patients living with frailty, multiple long-term conditions and increasing risk of hospital admission.

Using population health management tools, multidisciplinary working and proactive case management, the service aims to improve patient outcomes whilst reducing avoidable deterioration and crisis-led care.

This is a new team and with recruitment underway for all roles we have an anticipated start date of 1st February 2027.

The hours are expected to be delivered during weekdays.

This is not a traditional GP surgery role and it is not a routine clinic.

The successful candidate will act as the Primary Care Interface GP within the PAC multidisciplinary team.

Working alongside a Clinical Operational Lead, Nurse, Physiotherapist, Paramedic, Pharmacist and Care Coordinators, you will provide senior primary care clinical leadership and help ensure patients receive timely, coordinated and holistic care.

The role focuses on helping the multidisciplinary team manage complexity within the service wherever possible and preventing unnecessary work being referred back into routine practice workflows.

The postholder will support the team with clinical decision-making, investigations, medications, risk management, advance care planning and pathway navigation for some of Hertsmere's most vulnerable patients.

This role will be working as part of an integrated neighbourhood team comprising staff from primary care and community services with links to secondary care.

Herts Health GP Federation is a membership organisation supporting 8 local GP practices in Hertsmere.

We are a warm and welcoming team with great links to our local practices and community.

title: CAMHS Consultant Psychiatrist
descriptionHtml:
Are you an outstanding Consultant Psychiatrist looking for new challenges, career development and a competitive salary?

We have an excellent full time opportunity at Cygnet Hospital Bury Forestwood. The hospital offers CAMHS Tier 4 PICU, General Acute and Low Secure services across four wards which provide a defined treatment pathway from admission through to intervention and discharge including rapid assessment and treatment.

The vacancy is based on Buttercup Ward, our CAMHS PICU for young people aged 12-18 with severe mental illness.

descriptionHtml:
**THE JOB DESCRIPTION FOR THIS POST IS PENDING ROYAL COLLEGE APPROVAL**

Would you like to be part of leading health and wellbeing service in the provision of mental health for inpatient and community care? Why not join Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust for the opportunity to flourish and excel in your career and be part of our dedicated medical team.

The doctor is required to be on the specialist register for Old age or any subspecialty of the mental health.

This community Team based at Sydervelt Centre, provide services mainly to the Dementia patients and to Elderly patients in Rochford, Rayleigh and Canvey Island.

title: Care Coordinator
descriptionHtml:
Are you organised, approachable and passionate about making a difference to patients' experiences of healthcare?

Martlesham Heath Surgery is looking for a motivated and enthusiastic Care Coordinator to join our team. This is a varied and rewarding role where no two days are quite the same. You will play an important part in helping patients access the right care, supporting clinical teams and ensuring the smooth coordination of services across the practice.

Working alongside our GPs, nurses, care coordination team and wider practice colleagues, you will help connect patients with the support they need, coordinate appointments and follow-up care, and contribute to the day-to-day running of a busy primary care environment.

We are looking for someone with excellent communication and organisational skills, a compassionate and patient-focused approach, and the ability to work confidently as part of a team. Previous experience in general practice or healthcare would be helpful, but the right attitude, willingness to learn and commitment to providing excellent service are just as important.

Join a friendly, forward-thinking practice where your contribution genuinely matters and where you can develop your skills while helping us deliver great care to our community.

You will play an important role in helping patients access the care and support they need, while supporting the clinical and administrative teams to deliver an efficient and responsive service.

The role will involve coordinating patient appointments and follow-up arrangements, responding to patient enquiries, supporting clinical administration and communicating with healthcare professionals and external services.

You will work across different areas of the practice, helping to manage patient information, process correspondence and referrals, and ensure that important tasks are followed through. You will also help identify and resolve day-to-day issues, escalating concerns where appropriate.

This is a varied, people-focused position where priorities can change throughout the day. You will need to be comfortable balancing patient contact with administrative responsibilities, working collaboratively with colleagues and using your initiative to keep things moving.

Full training and support will be provided to help you develop within the role. We are looking for someone who is adaptable, organised and genuinely enjoys helping people.

Martlesham Heath Surgery is a friendly, forward-thinking GP practice serving a local community of approximately 6,000 patients. We are part of a wider partnership with Embrace Medical Centre, working together to provide accessible, high-quality and patient-centred primary care.

Our team brings together GPs, nurses, healthcare professionals, care coordinators and administrative colleagues, all working collaboratively to support our patients. We value a positive working environment where people are approachable, supportive and willing to share knowledge and experience.

We are continually looking at how we can improve the way we work, embrace new approaches and make the best use of technology to enhance patient access and experience. As a training practice, learning, development and supporting people to build their skills are important parts of our culture.

Joining Martlesham means becoming part of a team where your contribution is valued. You will have the opportunity to learn, develop and take on new responsibilities, while working alongside colleagues who understand the importance of delivering a reliable, compassionate service to our community.

We believe that great patient care starts with a great team, and every role plays an important part in making that happen.

title: Consultant General Paediatrician with Interest in Epilepsy
descriptionHtml:
This post forms part of a team of 20 Consultant Paediatricians. The position is offered as a full-time appointment; however, applications from candidates wishing to work Less Than Full Time (LTFT) are warmly encouraged.

Applications are invited for the appointment of a dynamic, enthusiastic, and committed Consultant Paediatrician at Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust, based at Wexham Park Hospital. This is an exciting opportunity to join a well-established department comprising 19 whole-time equivalent (WTE) Acute Paediatric Consultants, working within a supportive and forward-thinking multidisciplinary team.

The successful candidate will contribute to the continued development and delivery of high-quality acute paediatric and neonatal services, while helping to shape the future direction of children's services across the organisation.

You will join a dynamic and supportive team of consultants who work collaboratively in a flexible working environment.

Each week, two consultants undertake the attending role: one for Paediatrics and one for Neonatology.

o The consultant attending the Paediatric Ward is responsible for the Paediatric Ward and High Dependency Unit (HDU).o The consultant attending the Neonatal Unit is responsible for babies on the Neonatal Unit, Delivery Suite, Postnatal Ward and Transitional Care.

The successful candidate will undertake approximately 8 weeks per year in the attending consultant role. The department also provides a consultant-led GP Hotline Service Monday to Friday, 09:00-18:00, offering acute referral management, advice and guidance to primary care colleagues.

On-Call Commitments

The out-of-hours consultant rota is 1 in 12, covering Paediatrics and Neonatology. Consultants on call are expected to attend the nightly handover.

All patients are reviewed by a consultant within 14 hours of a decision to admit. Consultant presence and oversight are embedded within the service, with every handover consultant supervised.

Weekend cover is shared between two consultants, who divide Children's Ward attending responsibilities during the week.

Epilepsy Service

The Epilepsy Team consists of:

o A Lead Consultanto A Specialty Doctoro An Epilepsy Nurse Specialisto The post holder

Specialist tertiary support is provided by the Paediatric Neurology Team at Oxford University Hospitals.

employer: Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust
title: Medical Director (Brent ICP)
descriptionHtml:
We have an exciting opportunity for an experienced and highly motivated GP to join Brent Integrated Care Partnership (Brent ICP) as Brent Integrator Medical Director.

This is a senior clinical leadership role within the Brent Integrator function. The postholder will provide visible and credible medical leadership across the borough and work with partners to shape and deliver integrated, high-quality and sustainable health and care services.

Working closely with the ICP Managing Director, CNWL Medical Director, Brent Borough Clinical Leads and system partners, you will provide clinical leadership for Integrated Neighbourhood Teams, population health management, primary care transformation, quality improvement and the reduction of health inequalities and unwarranted clinical variation.

You will help ensure that clinical evidence, professional expertise, patient experience and population health intelligence inform strategic decisions, service transformation and delivery across Brent.

The role requires strong clinical, strategic and system leadership, together with the ability to build effective relationships and influence partners across primary care, community services, mental health, acute care, local government, social care and the voluntary and community sector.

Interview will be held week commencing 4-Jan-2027.

Please note: We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of applications.

Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Provide visible, credible and effective senior clinical leadership for the Brent Integrator.
  • Lead the clinical development of Integrated Neighbourhood Teams across Brent.
  • Champion population health management, prevention and proactive care.
  • Provide clinical leadership to reduce health inequalities and unwarranted clinical variation.
  • Support primary care transformation and the delivery of integrated models of care.
  • Provide clinical advice and oversight relating to quality improvement, clinical governance, quality assurance and patient safety.
  • Lead, manage and develop the three Brent Borough Clinical Leads.
  • Strengthen clinical leadership and engagement across primary care and the wider Brent health and care system.
  • Build effective relationships with Primary Care Networks, provider organisations, local authority colleagues, community organisations and other system partners.
  • Support the implementation of relevant national and local priorities, including the Fuller Stocktake and the development of integrated neighbourhood working.
  • Promote co-production and ensure that residents, patients, service users and communities influence service development.
  • Represent Brent and the Integrator at relevant borough and North West London clinical and partnership forums.
  • Provide appropriate professional challenge and hold clinical colleagues to account where required.

Brent Integrated Care Partnership brings together health, care and community partners to improve the health and wellbeing of Brent residents.

The Brent Integrator supports integration, transformation and place-based working across the borough. It works with partners to strengthen neighbourhood delivery, reduce fragmentation and ensure that services are increasingly organised around residents and population need.

The Brent Integrator Medical Director will play a central role in this developing model, providing senior medical leadership and ensuring that clinical priorities are reflected in strategy, transformation, delivery and assurance.

You will work collaboratively with the ICP Managing Director, CNWL Medical Director, Clinical Leads, Primary Care Networks, NHS providers, Brent Council, social care, voluntary and community sector organisations and residents.

employer: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant in Emergency Medicine
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to appoint an enthusiastic and high calibre Locum Consultant in Emergency Medicine.

The ED provides care to a diverse and high acuity patient population and operates as part of a major tertiary centre, including Major Trauma Centre responsibilities. Effective management of clinical risk, patient flow and operational pressure is a key priority for the Trust, and the post holder will play a central role in providing visible senior clinical leadership on the shop floor, supporting safe, timely and high-quality patient care in line with RCEM guidance.

The successful applicant will work as part of a well-established and supportive team, contributing to Consultant delivered care, supervision of trainees and advanced practitioners, and the ongoing development of Emergency Medicine services at Queen Elizabeth Hospital. The department is supported by a multidisciplinary workforce including doctors in training, locally employed doctors, medical students, Emergency Practitioners and Advanced Care Practitioners.

The ED comprises resuscitation facilities, rapid assessment and triage areas, majors and minors areas, and a UTC, incorporating ambulatory care, minor illness and injury pathways, and GP service.

This post is offered as a fixed term Locum appointment for an initial period of 12 months, on 10PA job plan, with weekend working commitment of 1:6. Applicants must hold full GMC registration, be on the GMC Specialist Register for Emergency Medicine or within six months of achieving CCT

The Emergency Department comprises resuscitation facilities, rapid assessment and triage areas, majors and minors areas, and a Urgent Treatment Centre (UTC), incorporating ambulatory care, minor illness and injury pathways, and a GP in Emergency Department service. Consultants will have opportunities to contribute to service development, pathway redesign and quality improvement as these models evolve.

This post is offered as a fixed term Locum appointment for an initial period of 12 months, on 10PA job plan, with weekend working commitment of 1:6. Applicants must hold full GMC registration, be on the GMC Specialist Register for Emergency Medicine or be within six months of achieving CCT at the time of interview. We welcome applications from candidates who have a special interest in Paediatrics. The post would suit both newly appointed and established consultants seeking experience in a large, complex Emergency Department with strong clinical leadership, education and development opportunities.

For further information or to arrange an informal visit, please contact Mr Riad Hosein (Clinical Service Lead) via email Riad.Hosein@uhb.nhs.uk

University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust strives to have an inclusive culture where everyone feels like they belong, can thrive, knows that they add value and feels valued. We do this by developing compassionate and culturally competent leaders, being values driven in all that we do and by creating a welcoming and inclusive workplace that thrives on the diversity of our people. As such we want to attract and recruit talented individuals from all backgrounds, and for each of you to feel supported for the diversity you bring, to achieve your full potential. For those staff with a disability, including physical disability, long term health condition, mental health or neurodiverse condition, this also means being committed to making reasonable adjustments needed for you to carry out your role.

employer: The Hillingdon Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant in Stroke Medicine (9PAs)
descriptionHtml:
This post is partially a replacement but also a new post, created in response to the increasing demand for Stroke services provision both in hospital and the community. The successful candidate will work closely with the two existing Stroke Physicians.

The Hillingdon Hospital provides Acute Stroke service for the people of Hillingdon, Hayes, Harlington, Ruislip and part of Ealing.

Our designated 24 bedded Acute Stroke Unit offers intense stroke rehabilitation for patients referred by our local HASUs (NWLH & CXH). The team includes 1 x SpR from geriatric rotation, 1x CT1/2, 1x FY2 rotating every four months as well as a Trust Grade SHO. The team includes Neuro-physiotherapists, Neuro-occupational Therapists, SALT, Dietician and psychology input.

There is a dedicated Stroke Clinic every week and daily TIA clinics. There is a Stroke specialist nurse at Hillingdon hospital, who supports the Stroke/TIA clinics.

The post-holder will be responsible to the Divisional Director of Unplanned Care at The Hillingdon Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust. The post is a minimum of 9 PA including 7 PA DCC and 2 SPA. SPA includes clinical and educational supervision, audit, personal CPD and mandatory training. Personal CPD must be included as part of annual appraisal which is mandatory and required for the revalidation process.

The post holder will, together with his or her consultant colleagues and other health care professionals in the Directorate, provide an effective and comprehensive service on the Stroke unit and the outpatient Stroke clinics. The post holder will work closely with colleagues to support quality improvement and service development in the department.

The post holder will provide consultant input to the Stroke unit, ESD and outpatient Stroke services.

The Hillingdon Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is the only acute Hospital in the London Borough of Hillingdon and offers a wide range of services including accident and emergency, inpatient care, day surgery, outpatient clinics and maternity services. The Trust's services at Mount Vernon Hospital include routine day surgery, delivered at a modern treatment centre, a minor injuries unit and outpatient clinics.

The safety and well-being of our patients and of our staff is paramount and we are making urgent improvements to address this - particularly in infection prevention and control. We are making progress and going forward by working in partnership with local GPs, charities,community services, academic partners, our local authority, neighbouring hospitals and the wider North West London Integrated care system, and ensuring that we listen and work in partnership with our local population. We are absolutely focused on ensuring that our hospitalsprovide high quality, safe and compassionate care, while drive forward the building of the new Hillingdon Hospital.

We have over 3,500 members of staff that are proud to care for nearly half a million people, with a vision to be an outstanding provider of healthcare through leading health and academic partnerships, transforming services, to provide the best care where needed.

Please note : Once a sufficient number of applications have been received the vacancy may be closed prior to the published closing down date.

title: Salaried GP - Walsall Division
descriptionHtml:

employer: Cardiff and Vale University Health Board
title: Senior Clinical Research Fellow in Infectious Diseases
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited from medicine staff-in-training (core level training or above) for a full-time senior clinical research fellow post in infectious diseases. The main role of the fellow will be to support our expanding portfolio of clinical trials.The postholder will be expected to work autonomously within their level of competence across an active portfolio of NHS infectious diseases clinical trials. This requires current practical familiarity with NHS clinical governance, prescribing and documentation, multidisciplinary working, referral and escalation processes, and the safe management of research participants within NHS servicesThe post will commence on 5th February 2027 and will be fixed term for 12 months.

This is a full-time senior clinical fellow research post. No clinical commitments, aside from clinical trial work, are outlined in this job description.

The postholder will:

  • Join an enthusiastic and dynamic research team comprising of clinicians, specialty registrars and clinical research specialist nurses with ongoing commercial and non-commercial research projects. Successful candidates will be expected to lead the day-to-day running of the ID trial portfolio including recruitment and data collection for ongoing ID research studies. They may also be asked to support/provide cover for other studies outside of the ID specialty
  • Provide clinical cover for any research studies pertaining to their subspecialty that involve the patient clinical trial journey taking them via the CRF. This will include attending inpatient and outpatient areas
  • Be GCP (Good Clinical Practice) trained and keep this up to date for the duration of the appointment.
  • Become part of the Research Fellow Programme in Cardiff & Vale. All applicants will be expected to join the NIHR Associate Principal Investigator Scheme.
  • Be supported to attend departmental teaching and training sessions where possible on further discussion with their Line Manager.

Cardiff and Vale University Health Board was established in October 2009 and is one of the largest NHS organisations in the UK. We have a responsibility for the promotion of health and well-being of around 475,000 people living in Cardiff and the Vale of Glamorgan, the provision of local primary care services, running of health centres, community health teams, hospitals - providing treatment and care when health and well-being isn't the best it could be.

employer: Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Ophthalmologist Post Specialising in Oculoplastics
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a full time, 12 month fixed term, consultant ophthalmologist post specialising in oculoplastics.

The successful candidate will join an established prestigious tertiary service and will also provide general and emergency ophthalmic services.

We are looking for an enthusiastic individual with appropriate training and qualifications. This is a 10.0 PA (8.0 PA of direct clinical care and 2.0 PA of supporting professional activities) appointment, though individuals meeting the person specification criteria who wish to work less than full time are welcome and encouraged to apply. The post is based at the Aintree Universiy Hospital site of St. Paul's Eye Unit, which is part of the Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (LUHFT).

St. Paul's Eye Unit is a vibrant and innovative department. The successful applicant will join a group of almost thirty substantive consultants including five clinical academics at consultant level.

The proposed start date for this appointment is January 2027.

St. Paul's Eye Unit

St. Paul's Eye Unit is a part of the Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, a merger between the Royal Liverpool and Broadgreen Trust and the Aintree Trust. St. Paul's is located on three sites: Aintree University Hospital, Royal Liverpool University Hospital and South Liverpool Treatment Centre, Garston. Senior medical staff currently comprises almost thirty substantive consultants including five clinical academics at consultant level, locum consultants, two associate specialists and six specialty doctors. Doctors in training comprise two clinical lecturers, specialist trainees and sub-specialty fellows.

Liverpool University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust comprises Aintree University Hospital, Broadgreen Hospital & Royal Liverpool University Hospital.

We are part of NHS University Hospitals of Liverpool Group, formed on 1 Nov 2024 from the coming together of LUHFT and Liverpool Women's NHS Foundation Trust. The Group was born from a shared aim to improve the care we provide our patients.

UHLG is one of the largest employers in the region, with over 16,800 colleagues dedicated to caring for our communities - from birth and beyond.

For the 630,000 people across Merseyside, we are their local NHS. We provide general and emergency hospital care, alongside highly specialised regional services for more than two million people in the North West.

Aintree University Hospitalis the single receiving site for adult major trauma patients in Cheshire and Merseyside and hosts a number of regional services including an award-winning stroke facility.Broadgreen Hospitalis home to elective surgical, diagnostic and treatment services, together with specialist patient rehabilitation.Liverpool Women's Hospitalspecialises in the health of women and babies, delivering over 7,200 babies in the UK's largest single site maternity hospital each year. TheRoyal Liverpool University Hospitalis the largest hospital in the country to provide inpatients with 100% single bedrooms and focuses on complex planned care and specialist services.

For roles at Liverpool Women's, visit theircareers page.

10 sessions per week

Permanent

#JoinTeamEliot

Radiology

Pathology

Support services

excellence and safety in everything we do

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:

  • Sessions delivered between 08:45 and 18:30, with flexibility around finish times

  • Acting as Clinician of the Day (COD) on a rotational basis, supporting triage within a full total triage system and strong team-working framework

title: Resident Doctor,MN37 Post–CCT Fellowship in Robotic Colorectal Surgery
descriptionHtml:
We are pleased to offer a 12-month Post-CCT Fellowship in Robotic Colorectal Surgery at West Hertfordshire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, fully funded by the Intuitive Foundation. The post is ideal for newly accredited colorectal surgeons (CCT or equivalent) who want to build expertise in robotic colorectal surgery in a high-volume NHS teaching unit.

Our multi-platform robotic service has three da Vinci systems: the dV5 for complex elective resections, the Xi for day-case and short-stay surgery at St Albans City Hospital, and the X for emergency robotic surgery. You will receive structured mentorship from accredited robotic consultants, supervised console training, simulation and high-volume operating.

Core hours are Monday to Friday, plus supervised consultant-level emergency robotic on-call equivalent to four weekends per year. Full details will be discussed at interview.

Interview will take place on the 4th January 2027.

You will operate on consultant-supervised robotic colorectal lists across the dV5, Xi and X platforms, including right and left-sided resections, TME and emergency robotic surgery, and undertake day-case robotic surgery at St Albans City Hospital. You will also attend cancer clinic and the colorectal MDT, and contribute to teaching, audit, governance and research. Lower GI endoscopy lists are available.

We are looking for a surgeon on, or within 6 months of joining, the GMC Specialist Register in General Surgery, with comprehensive knowledge of colorectal and general surgical disorders, strong general surgical management skills and a commitment to teaching. Robotic training or experience, JAG accreditation in lower GI endoscopy, research publications and current ATLS are desirable.

With a new hospital planned for Watford, work underway to update theatres at St Albans City Hospital and plans for a neighbourhood healthcare centre in Hemel Hempstead, this is an exciting time to join us.

We are building on the success of our award-winning virtual hospital and re-imagining models of care, working closely with partners and making the most of advances in digital healthcare.

Staff wellbeing and development are a priority, as is the role of innovation in improving clinical care, outcomes and patient experience.

Our vision is Excellent patient care, together and our values are to be empowered, compassionate, professional and inclusive. They capture an important balance across what we must all do as individuals and to support others.

We offer a variety of flexible working options as we recognise the importance of a good work life balance.

www.westhertshospitals.nhs.uk/flexibleworking

Work collaboratively within a highly skilled multidisciplinary team including GPs, Advanced Nurse Practitioners, Physician Associates, non-prescribing clinicians and other healthcare professionals.

title: Clinical Research Fellow - Medical, Clinical or Haemato-Oncology
descriptionHtml:
Right to work: We actively promote diversity and inclusion. This role may be eligible for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker route. We recommend that you assess your eligibility before applying for this position. Skilled Worker sponsorship will be assigned in line with Trust procedure. Visit https://www.gov.uk/skilled-worker-visa

The Clinical Research Fellowship provides an opportunity for a specialist trainee who is interested in pursuing a career in academic oncology to undertake a period of research leading to the successful completion of a PhD.

  • Pursue a translational research project UoL ideally co-supervised by a clinical academic aligned to CCC and an academic partner from UoL.

Vision, mission and values :: The Clatterbridge Cancer Centre

title: Non-Medical Prescriber
locations: Lonsdale House 52 Blucher Street, United Kingdom
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Non-Medical Prescriber to join Change Grow Live Birmingham Homeless Service. You will be an integral member of a multi-disciplinary and multi-agency team delivering recovery orientated alcohol and drug intervention services.

Our NMP's are integral members of our multi-disciplinary and multi-agency teams, delivering recovery orientated alcohol and drug intervention services. Offering care for presenting clients, prescribing and/or making amendments to prescriptions of opiate and/or alcohol substitute treatments and other related medications, they take a lead role in developing the prescribing clinic, acting as a point of contact for other workers and partner agencies around prescribing issues.

Where: Birmingham

Hours: Full Time, 37.5 hours per week

Contract Type: Permanent

Full-time hours at Change Grow Live are 37.5 hours per week. For part-time roles, the salary and payments will be pro rata based on contracted hours.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Assess, diagnose, plan; implement and evaluate treatment/interventions and care forthose accessing clinical treatment.
  • Clinically assess service user needs and plan clinical care accordingly.
  • Identify and assess suitability of service users for in-patient alcohol and opioid detoxification as appropriate.
  • Pro-actively review and manage clinical treatment plans of the service user
  • Initiating and adjusting prescriptions for opiate and/or alcohol substitute treatments and other related medications.
  • Taking the lead in developing the prescribing clinic, serving as a point of contact for colleagues and partner agencies on prescribing matters.

About you:

  • Qualified Non-Medical Prescriber
  • At least one years relevant and recent experience of working within substance misuse treatment.
  • Sound and demonstrable knowledge of harm reduction and health promotion interventions
  • Ability to assess and recovery plan service users and formulate written reports, as necessary.
  • Ability to communicate confidently and effectively, verbally and in writing.
  • Full driving licence and access to own transport, or ability to demonstrate easy movement between services, if necessary

Believe in people

At Change Grow Live, above all else we believe in people. It's the one thing that acts as a foundation for all our work.

If you use our services: we understand what you're going through. We won't judge. We believe you can make positive changes in your life.

If you work or volunteer for us: we believe in your potential. We believe you can do brilliant, life-changing work.

Our mission and vision

Our mission is to help people change the direction of their lives, grow as individuals, and live life to its full potential.

The vision we're working towards is to develop, deliver and share a whole person approach that changes society.

We believe that having diverse people working as part of our team makes us the organisation that we are.

We actively encourage applications from people from all backgrounds to help us to provide the best possible experience for the people who use our services and to make Change Grow Live a great place to work.

The safety of vulnerable children, young people and adults is our absolute priority. We will support you in your role to make sure that you are equipped to support the safety of people who use our services and those around them, to the highest standard possible.

title: Specialty Doctor Emergency Medicine

title: Consultant Psychiatrist East Brighton NMHT (£45k RRP)
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a Consultant Psychiatrist to join the East Neighbourhood Mental Health Team (NMHT) formerly known as East Assessment and Treatment Service (ATS) in Brighton & Hove. You will be joining a mutually supportive, friendly and enthusiastic team with a real passion for what we do.

Brighton and Hove Community services are split into three main teams, East and West and Central NMHT, each NMHT has a geographical patch determined by alignment to a small number of GP surgeries, this helps facilitate good liaison with our Primary Care colleagues. This post will be in Ardingly Court Cluster. We are also fortunate to have a large array of third sector organisations in Brighton and Hove whom we have developed strong links with.

This job attracts aRecruitment and Retention payment of £45,000,in addition to(up to) £8000 relocation allowance.The RRP payment is paid in the following instalments:

o£15,000 payable upon successful recruitment

o£10,000 payable at 12 months' service

o£10,000 payable at 24 months' service

o£10,000 payable at 36 months' service

The Recruitment and Retention payment is pro rata for part time employees. If you would like further information, or to know the full terms of the Recruitment and Retention Payment and/or the Relocation Allowance, then please do not hesitate to contact our Medical HR Team - spft.medicalhr@nhs.net

We are a large multi-disciplinary community mental health team, which provides specialist assessments and treatment to patients presenting with a range of complex and unstable mental health and social needs.

As a consultant psychiatrist in our team, your main duties will be to:

Provide specialist medical /psychiatric assessment and evidence-based treatment to patients referred to the service.

Provide clinical supervision to the HST and informal advice and supervision to non-medical members of the team

Fulfil the duties of Responsible Clinician for patient's subject to Community Treatment Orders including attendance at Mangers Hearings and Tribunals.

Mental Health Act assessments for patients on the team caseload

Liaison with inpatient Responsible Clinicians

Liaison with the forensic team/drug and alcohol services and risk panel as required

Sussex Partnership provides mental health and learning disability care for all age groups across Sussex and for children and young people in Hampshire.

Brighton & Hove is a unique, vibrant and exciting place to live and work, offering a lively city life with the opportunity to get away from it all to the South Downs National park just on the doorstep. The city offers excellent access to London and is in close proximity to Gatwick Airport. Brighton is proud to be a diverse and inclusive city, and this is reflected in the staff mix employed by SPFT, and by the ethos of the Trust.

We encourage flexible working. We know that a positive work/ life balance brings about huge health-related benefits, which has a positive impact on the care we provide. Please speak to us about flexible working, for example, home-working, part time hours, flexible start/ finish times or anything else. If it works for you and works for the role, we'll do our best to make it happen.

title: Specialty Doctor General Surgery
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to recruit 1 fixed term Speciality Doctor in General Surgery. This post is for a surgeon who has had some experience of general surgery. It is useful for surgeons who are awaiting a training post and need to increase their experience and also for those who are not planning a consultant career. The post for Specialty Doctor in General Surgery would also be suitable for overseas surgeons wishing to spend some time working within the UK health service. This job is not formally recognised for training, although there is an on-going commitment from the surgical department to career development.

  1. The normal working day consists of covering the General Surgical wards from 8am-5pm.
  2. You will be expected to actively participate in the management of the patients on the wards, outpatients, operating theatres and endoscopy. Your skills and acumen will be utilised in the investigation of patients, the formulation and execution of patient care plans as guided by your colleagues on the team. Ward rounds are daily.
  3. Your participation in operating theatre and day case sessions is required and recommended. You will be able to carry out operative procedures under consultant supervision and be involved in the perioperative care of patients.
  4. Your career development is important to us and study leave with a budget for appropriate courses is available in line with the other trainees.
  5. You will be supported and expected to participate in audits, research, teaching and service improvement schemes.
  6. Participation in the registrar on-call rota.
  7. It is prospective cover and therefore you will cover other colleagues in their absence.
  8. Perform duties in the occasional emergencies and unforeseen circumstances at the request of the appropriate Consultant in consultation, where practicable, with the doctor's colleagues both senior and junior.
  9. The post-holder will undergo regular appraisal throughout the post and will be expected to undergo continuing professional development.
  10. You will work collaboratively with colleagues to further develop and improve the service.

Wye Valley NHS Trust is a member of an NHS Foundation Group with South Warwickshire NHS FT , the George Eliot Hospital NHS Trust and Worcestershire Acute Hospitals NHS Trust.

Located on the border with Wales in the shadow of the Black Mountains, we provide acute and community services across Herefordshire and into parts of Powys and run Hereford County Hospital and the community hospitals in Bromyard, Leominster and Ross-on-Wye.

Worcestershire is our neighbouring county. The post holder will be required to travel between sites.

We are a progressive and forward looking trust with ambitious plans to improve quality and integrate patient pathways through close collaborative working with our partners to deliver the quality of care we'd want for our family and friends.

More than 3,500 people work for the Trust - they tell us it's a great place to work, blending the busyness of a DGH with the benefits of working in a beautiful rural and unspoilt county like Herefordshire.

We can offer a great work-life balance and have a fine tradition of working with staff to help them achieve their full potential.

Frances Martin, Trust Chairman: "The strength of the Trust is its amazing staff; a great place to work, a great place to develop your career and a great place to reach your potential."

Our values -Care, Accountability, Respect and Excellence - are at the heart of all we do. We believe in providing the right care in the right place at the right time...all the time.

title: Portfolio General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
South Coast Alliance (SCA) is seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Portfolio General Practitioner to join our team, working across services in Portsmouth and South East Hampshire.

This is an exciting opportunity for a GP looking to develop a varied and rewarding portfolio career, combining clinical practice with opportunities to contribute to leadership, education, quality improvement and service development.

The role offers four sessions per week, comprising three out-of-hours sessions and one in-hours session, providing experience across a range of primary and urgent care settings.

We are looking for a GP who is passionate about delivering high-quality, patient-centred care, enjoys working collaboratively and is keen to contribute to the ongoing development of our services.

At South Coast Alliance, we are committed to supporting professional development, innovation and a positive working environment, giving you the opportunity to develop your interests while making a meaningful difference to patient care.

(NHS pension, annual leave entitlement)

The Portfolio GP will deliver high-quality, patient-centred care across South Coast Alliance services in Portsmouth and South East Hampshire, undertaking face-to-face, telephone and remote consultations.

The role involves assessing, diagnosing and managing a range of acute and urgent conditions, making appropriate referrals, prescribing safely and maintaining accurate clinical records.

Alongside clinical duties, the postholder will have opportunities to contribute to clinical leadership, education, quality improvement, service development and clinical governance, working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams to improve patient care and service delivery.

South Coast Alliance (SCA) is a collaborative healthcare organisation delivering primary and urgent care services across Portsmouth and South East Hampshire.

We work in partnership with local healthcare providers to deliver safe, effective and high-quality patient care, supporting patients to access the right care, in the right place, at the right time.

Our services bring together experienced GPs, nurses, allied health professionals and operational teams, working collaboratively to meet the needs of our local communities.

At SCA, we are committed to continuous quality improvement, clinical excellence and workforce development. We encourage innovation, shared learning and professional development, creating a supportive environment where our staff can make a positive difference to patient care.

title: Specialty Doctor in Paediatrics (FY2-ST1) 12 mth FTC
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Specialty Doctor in Paediatrics to make a lasting difference to children with brain injury and neuro-disability. On a twelve month fixed term contract starting in February 2027 and ending in February 2028.

You will gain unique experience in Paediatrics, Neurorehabilitation and management of Neuro-disability. Previous experience in Paediatric Neurodisability is not required.

Staff benefits include, free shuttle bus, and more Read more below.

Role Requirements

As a Specialty Doctor, you will be a key member of the Medical Team, providing clinical care for children with brain injury and neurodisability across The Childrens Trust. You will assess new children under supervision, identify clinical risks, write medical reports, and provide regular medical support. You will receive support from Consultants in Paediatric Neurodisability, Consultant Paediatrician and Senior Specialty Doctors in Paediatric Neurodisability.

Working hours are 9am - 5pm Monday to Friday, with no obligatory Out of Hours cover.

To succeed in this high profile and diverse role, you must demonstrate:

  • Full professional GMC registration and licence to practice and an MBBS or equivalent.
  • Strong clinical skills, combined with excellent child and family focussed interpersonal skills.
  • A caring, supportive and can-do approach.
  • Willingness to take study leave, and commitment to receive training in Paediatrics, Neuro-disability and Neurorehabilitation.

Interview Dates: Monday 7th December 2026

With experience of working in a complex environment, across a large and diverse workforce, you will be exceptionally organised with a high-level of attention to detail. You will naturally possess excellent inter-personal skills, and an ability to consult and positively engage with key stakeholders across the organisation.

For more detail, please see the Duties and Responsibilities in the candidate briefing pack.

About Us

The Childrens Trust is the UKs leading charity for children with acquired brain injury, providing expert rehabilitation, education, therapy, and care at our national specialist centre in Tadworth, and to children and their families across the UK, via our Brain Injury Community Service.

Boasting a beautiful 24-acre site in Surrey, we are located just outside of London, close to the M25 (accessible via Junction 8, A217 to Tadworth) and easily accessible via National Rail, by way of: Clapham Junction, Sutton, and Epsom.

Staff Benefits

The work we do is highly rewarding, and in addition to an attractive salary, we offer a valuable range of benefits, including, adoption pay, time off for fertility treatment, enhanced paternity leave, paid carers leave, time out days for those experiencing menopause symptoms, time off for gender reassignment.

We also offer additional annual leave days for those with long service, with entitlements ranging from 35 to 41 days (including bank holidays) depending on your length of service.

Other benefits include free on-site parking; a staff shuttle service from Epsom and Sutton train stations to Tadworth Court, subsidised cafeteria, on-site staff accommodation (subject to availability), the ability to retain your NHS pension (where applicable) or the opportunity to join an alternative scheme, and the opportunity to develop your career in a supportive and collaborative environment.

employer: Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Trust
title: Spinal Specialist Doctor
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking a full-time Spinal Specialist doctor with responsibility to support existing consultants in spinal surgery department for Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital for a fixed term appointment for 12 starting April 2027.

employer: University Hospital of North Midlands NHS Trust
title: Consultant Children's Intensive Care
descriptionHtml:
This post is based at Staffordshire Children's Hospital at Royal Stoke which is part of the University

Hospitals of North Midlands (UHNM) NHS Trust. The paediatric department at UHNM primarily delivers acute paediatric care to the local children of Staffordshire and beyond.

We are seeking a Paediatric Critical Care Consultant. The post holder will be providing 8 weeks of consultant of the week (COW) cover to PICU and 8 weeks to HDU per year, and take part in 1 in 5.5 on-call rota for PICU, including evenings and weekends.

In addition, there is also time allocated to do educational supervision and attending departmental meetings.

Staffordshire Children's Hospital is part of UHNM which has two sites: Royal Stoke University Hospital, located in Stoke-on-Trent, and County Hospital, located in Stafford. The Staffordshire Children's Hospital is based at the Royal Stoke site, all inpatient services for children are there. Outpatient clinics run at both sites.

The Paediatric Department is one of the largest in the country with a number of sub speciality areas receiving tertiary care referrals. The Trust has a purpose built Children's Centre comprising of inpatient wards, Children's A&E and admissions unit and outpatients department adjacent to the Child Development Centre. The Child Health Directorate provides a wide range of services encompassing acute paediatrics, paediatric and neonatal intensive care, outpatients and community paediatrics. We also provide consultant support to the children's emergency centre and deliver a range of paediatric general and speciality clinics on the County Hospital site.

Flexible working requests will be considered.

employer: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust
title: Cardiology Consultant specialist interest in Coronary Intervention/PH
descriptionHtml:
The role will cover general Cardiology, coronary intervention, and development in Pulmonary Hypertension (PH) services. Providing cover for the PPCI service, Cardiology Consultant of the week and the PH service. On call commitments with PPCI and PH

From flexible hours and generous benefits, to next level training, we make it easier to take your career to the topFor more information please follow link https://www.royalfreelondonjobs.co.uk/

title: Consultant Gynaecologist
descriptionHtml:
One Health is looking for a Consultant Gynaecologist to support and grow the One Health Group Gynaecology Team.

The successful candidate will have experience working within a similar role in a private or NHS setting. You should have a professional outlook, empathetic telephone manner and understand the importance of patient confidentiality.

  • You should currently be in a substantive NHS post OR in a long-term locum post (more than 12 months)
  • If not in current NHS post, should have been a substantive NHS consultant for at least 3 years before leaving the NHS
  • On GMC register and have no hearings or restrictions
  • Should have relevant sub specialist qualifications (FRCS {orth})

This role will involve assessing and operating on NHS patients referred to One Health, via the NHS e-Referral System. Appointments will be held across a number of outreach clinic sites. One Health was established in Sheffield in 2004 and has successfully grown to become a significant healthcare provider in the region. Our services are available to NHS and private patients, with clinics located at over 30 locations across Yorkshire, Derbyshire, Nottinghamshire and Lincolnshire. Our Head Office is based in Sheffield but will require the successful candidate to work from various locations remotely.

One Health brings healthcare closer to where people live by offering outpatient facilities over a wide geographical area. We are committed to clinical excellence and our mission to provide innovative, high quality medical and clinical services for NHS patients, optimising outcomes so they can quickly continue healthy lives.

Benefits of working with OHG are:

  • Flexible working options
  • Use of latest technology
  • Dedicated administrative support team

  • Voice Recognition

title: Senior Care Assistant
descriptionHtml: As a Senior Carer at HC One, Kindness will be at the core of everything you do. It touches upon every aspect of our Dementia, Nursing, Residential and Specialist care homes.
