employer: South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
title: Clinical Fellow in Informatics
descriptionHtml:
As a Fellow in Clinical Informatics you will join a multi-disciplinary team which works across all aspects of developing and deploying the digital tool, LUCI (locating useful clinical information). LUCI supports the use of clinical data to inform and improve patient care in mental health services. The team provides a supportive, fast paced environment where members work flexibly to contribute to the services' work in data science, user-led design, digital implementation and training. You will be supported to develop as an expert digital clinician within mental health working alongside the CIS technical team, clinical informaticians, and digital clinicians as well as academic partners within the Maudsley Biomedical Research Centre.

This is a fixed term 12 months full-time post for a Fellow in Clinical Informatics, designed for a Specialty Trainee (years 4-5) in psychiatry to undertake as an Out-of-Programme Experience (OOPE) from their training rotation.

We encourage people interested in the role to contact the CIS Clinical Leads to learn more about the service and role.

***Please note that this vacancy may close prior to the advertised closing date if a sufficient number of applications are received.***

The post holder will be an integral member of the Clinical Informatics Service and have the opportunity to observe and contribute to all aspects of its work. They will be involved throughout the development cycle of the LUCI clinical data platform. This may include, but will not be limited to:

Development, validation and testing of data models built from data in SLaM's clinical systems. They will work alongside clinical informaticians, contributing as a domain expert on clinical questions, how SLaM's services work and how clinical systems are used by clinicians.

Development of new LUCI tools and dashboards, working alongside clinical end users and the wider LUCI team to define the clinical questions, the data required to answer them, and design and test visualisations as part of user-led design sprints.

Supporting the risk, governance and digital clinical safety processes.

Working with the LUCI Digital Nurses to support implementation of LUCI within SLaM .

The role is designed to develop expertise across all aspects of the development and implementation of data and digital in healthcare. The post-holder will have the opportunity to shape the focus of their work within this, dependent on their interests and skills in:

  • Data science and analytics
  • User-led design for health care
  • Quality improvement
  • Digital Clinical Safety
  • Training
  • Evaluation
About South London and Maudsley:

South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust (SLaM) provide the widest range of NHS mental health services in the UK as well as substance misuse services for people who are addicted to drugs and alcohol. We work closely with the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology and Neuroscience (IoPPN), King's College London and are part of King's Health Partners Academic Health Sciences Centre.

About the Clinical Informatics Service:

The Clinical Informatics Service (CIS) supports the maintenance and ongoing development of LUCI (Locating Useful clinical Information). LUCI finds,summarisesand visualises information from SLaM's clinical systems, providing clinicians and service planners with actionable insights to improve patient care. Its current use cases focus on general adult community mental health care, population health management within the psychosis pathway and medications information used by pharmacists and prescribers.

The CIS aims to:

Release time to care by giving clinicians quicker access to comprehensive information they need to do their jobs.

Identify unmet needs and link information to the actions clinicians can take to address them.

Motivate and facilitate action on inequalities by allowing professionals to see whether care adheres to national and SLaM pathways, plan action to address inequalities and understand whether their plans are working.

employer: North Cumbria Integrated Care NHS Foundation Trust
title: Specialty Doctor in Emergency Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Cross site working across Cumberland Infirmary, Carlisle & West Cumberland Hospital, Whitehaven

We are excited to present the opportunity for two capable and experienced specialty doctors within Emergency Medicine at NCIC. The successful candidates will work as part of our 'Senior Decision Maker' rota alongside Higher Specialist Trainees and RCEM Credentialed Senior Advanced Clinical Practitioners

You will be actively involved in departmental management activity, quality improvement, and governance. You will be encouraged to develop your knowledge, skills, and experience in these non-clinical aspects of emergency medicine. You will help provide support and training to our composite medical workforce of postgraduate doctors in training, clinical fellows, and advanced practitioners.

  • Be involved in the initial reception and management of patients attending the ED.
  • As a capable and experienced ST4+ clinician, you will be expected to independently manage the department overnight, ensuring the delivery of safe and effective patient care
  • Be involved in the full spectrum of Emergency Department patients including resuscitation and assessment of seriously injured and ill patients, dealing with complex cases, paediatrics and minor injuries.
  • Assist the consultants and senior nurses in the running of the shop floor, ensuring that patients are seen by appropriate staff in a timely fashion and that junior staff are appropriately supervised along with nursing staff and medical students.
  • Assist in maintaining flow of patients through the department and support national Quality Indicators.
  • Undertake some administrative responsibilities, for example, reviewing x-ray and pathology results.
  • Have the facility under the auspices of the Emergency Consultant to develop special interest for clinical research and to undertake audit projects or support audit projects of the junior medical staff.
  • Share the responsibility of conducting an observation ward round in the Emergency Department
  • Actively attend, participate and contribute towards teaching sessions for his/her own team as well as colleagues of varying levels
  • Maintain and develop own skills and learning
  • Maintain professional standards and obligations as set out by the GMC
  • Adhere to Trust Policies and Guidelines

At NCIC, we have an ambition to deliver outstanding hospital and health services to half a million people. Established on 1st October 2019, the Trust is creating a centre of excellence in providing rural and remote healthcare and provides a wide range of community and acute services throughout north Cumbria and beyond. We're responsible for delivering over 70 services across 15 main locations and we employ more than 6,500 members of staff.

Our 5 key principles demonstrate our belief in the delivery of 'safe, high quality care every time'.

  • Being a clinically led organisation

  • Quality and safety at the heart

  • A positive patient experience every time

  • A great place to work

  • Managing our money well

As an organisation we are serious about supporting a diverse workforce that reflects our local community and are very much focused on being an inclusive and compassionate place to work.

employer: South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Liaison Psychiatry
descriptionHtml:
This is a 8 PA locum consultant post within the well-established General Adult Liaison Psychiatry team at King's College Hospital, for a fixed nine-month period. The post provides additional consultant capacity to support the team during a period of temporary change in consultant sessions. The post holder will join a supportive multidisciplinary team providing psychiatric assessment and management to adult inpatients and Emergency Department attenders at a major London teaching hospital and major trauma centre.

The post offers an excellent opportunity to work at the interface of mental and physical healthcare, managing complex presentations across medical and surgical specialties, with opportunities to contribute to teaching, service development and quality improvement.

The post holder will provide consultant-level psychiatric care within the liaison psychiatry service, including assessment, diagnosis and management of patients presenting with complex mental health needs in acute hospital settings. They will work as part of a multidisciplinary team, providing clinical leadership, supervision and support to junior doctors and other professionals. The role includes active participation in clinical governance, quality improvement, teaching, training and service development.South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust is one of the leading mental health trusts in the UK, providing a wide range of services across South London and nationally. The Trust is part of King's Health Partners Academic Health Sciences Centre, bringing together world-class research, education and clinical care. The liaison psychiatry service at King's College Hospital is a large, well-established and RCPsych-accredited service, delivering high-quality care within a busy acute teaching hospital environment. The Trust is committed to innovation, equality and staff wellbeing, offering excellent opportunities for professional development, research and leadership.

title: Emergency Care Assistant
descriptionHtml:
As an Emergency Care Assistant (ECA), you will play a vital role in supporting frontline clinicians to deliver safe, compassionate, and effective pre-hospital care. Working alongside Paramedics and other healthcare professionals, you will respond to emergency and urgent care incidents, assist with patient assessment and treatment, and help ensure patients receive the highest standard of care.

The role involves providing clinical and practical support, safely driving emergency vehicles when qualified, maintaining vehicles and equipment, and contributing to a professional, patient-centred service. This is a rewarding opportunity for individuals who thrive in a fast-paced environment, enjoy working as part of a team, and are committed to making a positive difference in their community.

  • Support Paramedics in delivering safe, effective, and compassionate patient care.
  • Respond to emergency and urgent care incidents and assist with patient assessment and treatment.
  • Safely drive emergency vehicles when authorised and transport patients as required.
  • Maintain accurate patient records and communicate effectively with colleagues and patients.
  • Ensure vehicles, equipment, and medical supplies are clean, stocked, and ready for use.
  • Comply with all clinical, health and safety, infection prevention, and safeguarding policies.
  • Participate in mandatory training and ongoing professional development.

Established in 2002, Alliance Pioneer Group is a Care Quality Commission (CQC) registered ambulance and medical services provider, delivering frontline ambulance, patient transport, and event medical services across the UK. Working in partnership with NHS Trusts and other healthcare organisations, we are committed to providing safe, compassionate, and high-quality patient care. Our experienced, HCPC-registered clinicians are supported by a culture of professionalism, continuous development, and excellence, ensuring the highest standards of care for every patient we serve.

employer: Alder Hey Children's NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Paediatric Respiratory Consultant
descriptionHtml:
This is a part-time locum post in Paediatric Respiratory Medicine at Alder Hey Children's NHS Foundation Trust, commencing as soon as possible for a period of 23 months. The post would suit someone wishing to work at tertiary respiratory level alongside another role. The post is for an average of 2 PA per week, but hours will be calculated on a per annum basis.

The successful applicant will work alongside the other consultants and share responsibilities and work load with support from other members of the team In line with the agreed team objectives, the successful applicant will:

Maintain a high quality tertiary service for children with complex respiratory disorders.

  • Contribute to theconsultant of the weekand on-call commitment
  • Contribute to the inpatient and outpatient management of children with general/ complex respiratory disorders
  • Contribute to the high quality training programme in paediatric respiratory medicine.

The respiratory consultants provide a busy respiratoryservice to all theclinical teams in the hospital on a day to daybasis. They also providesupport for paediatricians in the Mersey region and for colleagues in primary care. This support is provided by the consultant of the week and the post holder will share this responsibility with 5 other consultants. The post holder will have 4 HOT weeks in a 12 month period.

The appointee will lead a weekly respiratory/asthma clinic, with support from nurse specialists and respiratory function testing. In addition,there may be the opportunity to run regular clinics dedicated to providing a higher level of care for patients with complex respiratory disease.

The appointee will take a full share of responsibility for training undergraduates and postgraduates, audit, clinical governance, and development of the service.

As one of Europe's biggest and busiest children's hospitals, at Alder Hey Children's NHS Foundation Trust, we treat everything from common illnesses to highly complex and specialist conditions.In addition to our main hospital site, we offer paediatric services at a number of community sites and hold local clinics across Merseyside, Cumbria, Shropshire, Wales and the Isle of Man. We also provide specialist inpatient care for children with complex mental health needs in our recently relocated and newly opened state of the art facility.

Alder Hey has a thriving research portfolio and leads research into children's medicines, infection, inflammation and oncology. We are becoming recognised as one of the world's leaders in children's healthcare and research. We contribute to public health, lead cutting-edge research and teach the next generation of children's specialists. Alongside this is ourInnovation Hub, a dedicated space where clinicians and industries can come together to create new products and technologies.

We know that a children's hospital is different and that our job is more than just treating an illness. To us, every child is an individual. As well as giving them the very best care, we set out to make them feel happy, safe and confident as they play, learn and grow. At Alder Hey we are here to look after a child and their family and that includes mums, dads, brothers and sisters.

title: Consultant in Stroke medicine
descriptionHtml:
East Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust is seeking a dedicated stroke physician to join their high-performing Stroke MDT, providing daily consultant-led care and support to patients on the stroke unit. The role involves contributing to clinical governance, risk management, and providing teaching and supervision to junior medical staff. The trust is undergoing a reconfiguration of unscheduled care services, including the potential opening of a HASU as part of the Lancashire and South Cumbria Stroke service. This full-time substantive post supports the comprehensive service for Stroke patients, both in the hospital and the community, and offers opportunities for research and teaching.

  • Delivering daily consultant-led care to stroke patients and supporting the stroke unit staff.
  • Contributing to clinical governance, risk management, and ensuring appropriate standards of care.
  • Providing teaching, educational, and clinical supervision to junior medical staff.
  • Participating in the delivery of 7-day TIA and rapid access clinics.
  • Collaborating in the reconfiguration of unscheduled care services, including potentially opening a HASU.
  • Supporting sub-acute rehabilitation for stroke patients in community hospitals and settings.
  • Sharing responsibility for acute and rehabilitation stroke wards.
  • Participating in medical audit and postgraduate teaching.
  • Being part of the MDT on acute and rehabilitation stroke units.
  • Participating in acute stroke and Telestroke rotas.

East Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust is a large integrated healthcare provider with a reputation for high-quality stroke care. The trust offers a comprehensive service for Stroke patients in both hospital and community settings. Strong links with universities provide opportunities for research and teaching. The trust values flexible working arrangements and welcomes candidates interested in part-time roles. The successful applicant will have the chance to contribute to the development of stroke medicine services.

employer: Kingston and Richmond NHS Foundation Trust
title: Locum Consultant Geriatrician - Frailty
descriptionHtml:
Kingston and Richmond NHS Foundation Trust is excited to be recruiting for a Locum Consultant Geriatrician with a special interest in Acute/Front Door Frailty and Interface Frailty, to help shape the future of frailty care across South West London. We are at the forefront of frailty service transformation. This is an exceptional opportunity to join a forward-thinking team at a Trust rated Outstanding by the CQC for both quality and leadership. Our Trust has a proven track record of innovation in frailty, and we are proud to have been part of the first cohort of the NHS England Frailty Improvement Collaborative since 2025.

Postholders will deliver high-quality specialist geriatric medicine across the acute, interface and community zones of the integrated systemwide frailty pathway

Our new model of care offers flexible roles spanning the Acute Frailty Unit (AFU) within the Emergency Department (ED), front-door frailty triage, ED and AMT liaison and a wide range of roles: clinical, educational and strategic, for the virtual ward and Home First pathways and alongside the wider frailty system.

A critical component of the role will be to coordinate, assess, triage, advise and manage patient flow in both directions across the hospital front door. This will include driving timely Home First discharges and admission onto our integrated Virtual Ward, and streamlining access for patients in the community who require hospital-based assessment and services. The emphasis will be on ensuring timely, efficient, appropriate and safe patient pathways, with coordinated movement into and out of hospital and joined-up services responding to agreed clinical action plans.

There will be opportunities to develop, lead and contribute strategically to the Integrated Virtual Ward, the Proactive Anticipatory Care (PAC) team, and others.

The role will also involve developing strong working relationships with our GP partners and providing clinical, strategic and organisational leadership in the governance, improvement and development of the integrated Virtual Ward, and integrated frailty system as a whole .

Your growthand personal happinessmatterto us.After all, we can't expect the best from you if we don't invest in your development and nurture your wellbeing.From the moment you join us, we're committed to fostering your professional and personal development within a supportive, empowering environment. Whether you're just starting your career or looking to advance further, we provide you with the tools and opportunities you need to succeed.We actively support colleagues to take part in research, quality improvement and innovation, whatever their role or level in the organisation.

To support your wellbeing, we offer an extensive range of resources, including an on-site staff nurseryat Kingston Hospital,wellbeingpractitioners,regular wellbeing classes,dedicatedstaffphysiotherapist, comprehensiveoccupationalhealth services, 24/7employeeassistanceprogramme, and a range of other support and activities.

We also take every opportunity to thank and recognise the work our teams do, through weekly 'shoutouts' and patient feedback, monthly and annual awards.

Wherever you work across our organisation, we look forward to welcoming you.

employer: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant- Healthcare for Older People
descriptionHtml:
* The Department of Healthcare for Older People at University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust (UHB) provides comprehensive, integrated care for older people across acute hospital and community settings. At Birmingham Heartlands Hospital, we are committed to delivering high quality, compassionate and person centred care for older people, with a particular focus on those living with frailty and complex healthcare needs. Our department has experienced significant growth and development in recent years, supported by the establishment of one of the largest centralised fractured neck of femur services in Europe, a comprehensive Older Person Assessment and Liaison (OPAL) service providing specialist assessment at the hospital front door, the Older Persons Assessment and Decision (OPAD) Unit, and a weekday Frailty Same Day Emergency Care (FSDEC) service. Together, these services provide an exciting platform for the continued development of our acute frailty pathways, early specialist assessment and integrated models of care.The post holder will be expected to contribute to the delivery of excellent, safe and effective clinical care for older people across inpatient, outpatient and acute front door settings. Responsibilities will include: Clinical care: Assessment, investigation and management of older inpatients and older people referred to the front door frailty services, including OPAL, OPAD and FSDEC, providing specialist geriatric input and Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment where appropriate. Administrative responsibilities: Completion of clinical documentation, correspondence, discharge summaries, results review and other administrative duties directly related to patient care. Education and training: Contribution to undergraduate and postgraduate medical education, continuing professional development and the teaching and supervision of resident doctors, medical students and other healthcare professionals, including Allied Health Professionals (AHPs), as part of the multidisciplinary team. Meetings and governance: Regular participation in departmental, specialty and Clinical Group meetings, including clinical governance, morbidity and mortality meetings and service development discussions. Research and quality improvement:

University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust strives to have an inclusive culture where everyone feels like they belong, can thrive, knows that they add value and feels valued. We do this by developing compassionate and culturally competent leaders, being values driven in all that we do and by creating a welcoming and inclusive workplace that thrives on the diversity of our people. As such we want to attract and recruit talented individuals from all backgrounds, and for each of you to feel supported for the diversity you bring, to achieve your full potential. For those staff with a disability, including physical disability, long term health condition, mental health or neurodiverse condition, this also means being committed to making reasonable adjustments needed for you to carry out your role.

title: General Practitioner (GP)
descriptionHtml:
Salaried GP

Join a friendly and supportive practice where teamwork and high-quality patient care are at the heart of what we do.

St Helens Medical Centre is seeking an enthusiastic Salaried GP to join our established and welcoming team. We are open to applications from both experienced GPs and those newly qualified who are looking to develop their career within a supportive primary care environment.

This is an excellent opportunity to become part of a practice that values continuity of care, clinical excellence and collaborative working.

The successful applicant will:

  • Provide high-quality, patient-centred general medical services to our practice population.
  • Undertake a mixture of face-to-face and telephone consultations.
  • Assess, diagnose and manage a broad range of acute and chronic conditions.
  • Prescribe safely and effectively in accordance with national and local guidance.
  • Review pathology results, clinical correspondence and other patient-related documentation.
  • Check and sign repeat prescriptions.
  • Screening patients for disease risk factors and early signs of illness.
  • Record clear and accurate consultation notes.
  • Undertake home visits where clinically appropriate.
  • Work collaboratively with the wider multidisciplinary team.
  • Participate in quality improvement activities, clinical audit and service development.
  • Support safeguarding responsibilities for children and vulnerable adults.
  • Providing counselling and health education.
  • Engage fully with appraisal, revalidation and continuing professional development.
  • The post-holder will undertake all the usual duties and responsibilities associated with a GP working within primary care.

St Helens Medical Centre is a friendly, well-established practice serving approximately 6,700 patients across St Helens, Bembridge, Seaview and the surrounding communities.

We are proud to maintain the ethos of traditional family practice medicine whilst embracing modern ways of working. We have a strong reputation for delivering high-quality patient care and consistently achieving excellent clinical outcomes.

We operate from a well-equipped, purpose-built practice with air-conditioned consulting rooms and a Branch Surgery in neighbouring Bembridge. As a long-established training practice, we are committed to supporting the development of future healthcare professionals and fostering a culture of continuous learning.

Our multidisciplinary team includes GPs, Advanced Nurse Practitioners, Practice Nurses, a Paramedic, Pharmacy Technician, Social Prescriber, First Contact Physiotherapist, Care Coordinator, Healthcare Assistants and an experienced Administrative Team. This collaborative approach allows us to provide comprehensive, patient-centred care whilst ensuring clinicians are well supported in their day-to-day work.

employer: London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust
title: Clinical Fellow in Anaesthesia
descriptionHtml:
This is an exciting opportunity for the appointee to work in a major NW London NHS trust, with areputation for educational excellence within a friendly and supportive culture!This post is based at Ealing Hospital theatres, which is one of three sites within our trust (NorthwickPark, Ealing and Central Middlesex Hospitals). Successful candidates will further their experiencein a range of surgical subspecialties, to include elective and emergency upper & lower generalsurgery, orthopaedics/trauma, gynaecology, endoscopy, and dental surgery. The upper GI servicehas recently expanded, providing increased capacity for surgery such as laparoscopiccholecystectomy and an upper GI hub is planned for the near future.

There is a dedicatedemergency/trauma theatre list 24/7, with weekday consultant cover. In addition, the departmentprovides an outreach service for ECT and for DC cardioversions in the Coronary Care Unit. Alsoincluded are potential opportunities to work at the Northwick Park Hospital site to broaden this casemix, to include major head & neck, vascular, obstetrics, urology and major colorectal surgery.

The post holder must:- Know when to ask for help, whom to ask for help, and not act beyond the level of his/her own competence. There is always an anaesthetic middle grade onsite and also a supervising consultant/duty consultant for guidance and assistance- Effect detailed hand-over at the end of a duty shift- In the event of a list cancellation or early finish, be available on site for possible reassignment to other lists.OBJECTIVESEnsure familiarity and compliance with:- Corporate policies and procedures (available for viewing on the Trust intranet)- Workplace policies and procedures- Quality improvement measures- Patient safety initiatives- Theater efficiency initiativesParticipate in:- Continuous professional development (CPD)- Clinical governance- Critical incident reporting- Mandatory in-house training- Teaching- Assessments appropriate to training/CPDLOCATION OF DUTIESDuties will be primarily based on Ealing and Northwick Park sites.The post holder should be prepared to perform duties in occasional emergencies and unforeseen circumstances. Commitments arising in such circumstances are however exceptional and the post holder will not be required to undertake work of this kind forprolonged periods or on a regular basis. All efforts will be made to ensure that work of this kind does not result in continuous hours of duty which exceed the New Deal continuous hours of duty limits.

London North West University Healthcare NHS Trust (LNWH) cares for the people of Brent, Ealing, Harrow and beyond.

Our team of more than 8,200 clinical and support staff serve a diverse population of almost one million people.

We run major acute services at:

  • Northwick Park Hospital: home to one of the busiest emergency departments (A&E) in the country. The hospital provides a full range of services including the country's top-rated hyper-acute stroke unit and one of only three hyper-acute rehabilitation units in the UK
  • St Mark's Hospital: an internationally renowned specialist centre for bowel disease
  • Ealing Hospital: a busy district general hospital providing a range of clinical services, as well as 24/7 emergency department and urgent care centre, and specialist care at Meadow House Hospice
  • Central Middlesex Hospital: our planned care site, hosting a range of surgical and outpatient services and collocated with an urgent care centre.

We are a university teaching NHS trust, in recognition of the important role we play in training clinicians of the future and bringing the benefits of research to the public.

title: Consultant Psychiatrist - Eastbourne (£45k RRP)
descriptionHtml:
We have an exciting opportunity for a General Adult Consultant Psychiatrist to join the Eastbourne Crisis and Home Resolution Team (CRHTT) and the Haven in Eastbourne, East Sussex, with the added option of joining the Digital Directorate as Digital Medical Lead.

The Crisis Resolution Home Treatment Team (CRHTT) provides a 7 day per week service to people experiencing an acute psychiatric crisis. The team provides an alternative to acute hospital treatment by offering intensive community-based interventions and gatekeeping all potential hospital admissions. Where a hospital admission does occur, CRHTT can assist in shortening the inpatient stay by facilitating supportive discharge back to the community.

The post also provides medical input to the Haven. The Haven is a 4-chaired, nurse-led, community-based mental health crisis service designed to provide rapid assessment (up to 24hrs) and short-term support for individuals experiencing acute mental health distress.

In addition, successful applicants to the post will have the opportunity to be seconded for 2 PAs per week to the Digital Directorate to work as a Digital Medical Lead. The Digital Medical Lead role will be focused on our new electronic patient record and prescribing systems.

For further information with regards to the main duties of this role, please see the attached job descriptions for details.

This job attracts a Recruitment and Retention payment of £45,000 structured over a three-year period as follows:

£15,000 payable upon successful recruitment

£10,000 payable at 12 months' service

£10,000 payable at 24 months' service

£10,000 payable at 36 months' service

The Recruitment and Retention payment is pro rata for part time employees. Please contact spft.medicalHR@nhs.net for full details and terms and conditions.

title: Consultant in O&G - DAU & FMU
descriptionHtml:
The postholder will provide consultant obstetric care across antenatal, intrapartum and postnatal services and act as medical lead for the Day Assessment Unit (DAU). The role combines direct clinical care, multidisciplinary leadership, teaching and clinical governance within a 10 PA job plan.

The principal commitments are antenatal clinics (ANC), a weekly Wednesday afternoon elective caesarean section list, participation in Friday obstetric on-call at a frequency of 1 in 3, and protected time for DAU leadership. Fetal medicine scanning experience and a fetal medicine ATSM or equivalent training are desirable

Please see the attached JD for full details.

  • Professional practice

Maintain accurate and timely electronic records, practise within professional competence, and ensure clear communication with women, families, primary care and other teams. Respect individual preferences, promote informed consent and use interpretation and accessible information where required.

  • Antenatal care
  • Elective caesarean section service
  • Labour ward and emergency obstetric care
  • Day Assessment Unit Medical Leadership

The postholder will be the DAU medical lead, working in partnership with the DAU midwifery lead, obstetric leadership and operational team. A proposed protected allocation of 1.0 PA per week is included within the 10 PA total for this leadership responsibility, subject to agreement in the final job plan

Homerton Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is a high performing and flourishing organisation serving the population of Hackney, East London, The City and beyond.

We are extremely proud of the fact that Homerton Hospital has recently attained the highest possible rating of "Outstanding" from the Care Quality Commission (CQC).

Our integrated Trust provides comprehensive hospital and community health services for its local population and a range of specialist services for a wider group of patients. In addition, the Trust manages services out of St Leonard's Hospital and the Mary Seacole Nursing Home.

Homerton aims to ensure equality and value diversity, and we are committed to inclusion for all of our staff. This is reflected in our policies, procedures and People Plan. All of our staff are expected to embody our Trust values at all times.

We are also committed, through our Fair Recruitment Standards, to ensuring all applicants are treated fairly.

Homerton has a proud tradition of supporting and developing its staff, including its well-regarded and valued nursing community, and all staff are able to take advantage of a great range of benefits.

Homerton is proud to have been included on the HSJ & Nursing Times Best Places to Work list.

title: Full-Time Salaried Clinical Pharmacist
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an enthusiastic, experienced and proactive Clinical Pharmacist to join The Castle Practice on a full-time, permanent basis. The successful candidate must have demonstrable primary care experience in a GP practice or Primary Care Network (PCN) setting.

This is a hands-on clinical role designed to add meaningful capacity to the practice. You will work closely with our GPs and wider multidisciplinary team, with a particular focus on providing daily clinical pharmacy support to the Duty Doctor, managing medicines-related workload autonomously and helping patients receive safe, timely and effective care.

A key part of the role will be taking ownership of acute prescription requests and medication-related queries from patients, community pharmacies, reception and clinical colleagues. We are looking for a proactive problem-solver who will investigate and resolve issues within their scope of competence rather than routinely passing work back to the GP or reception team. Appropriate escalation to a GP will always be supported where clinically necessary.

The balance of work will vary according to practice demand. The successful candidate will therefore need to be flexible and comfortable moving between acute workload, long-term condition reviews, structured medication reviews, medicines optimisation and other clinical priorities.

Provide daily clinical pharmacy support to the Duty Doctor and wider practice team.Manage acute prescription requests and medication queries, including urgent supply issues, monitoring requirements and queries arising from hospital correspondence or transfer of care. Undertake long-term condition reviews and associated medication reviews, including appropriate monitoring and medication optimisation. Undertake structured clinical medication reviews, particularly for patients with complex polypharmacy, frailty, high-risk medicines or multiple long-term conditions, with a proactive focus on appropriate deprescribing and reduction of dependence-forming medicines, including controlled drugs and benzodiazepines, in partnership with patients and in line with clinical guidance. Support safe and efficient repeat prescribing, medicines reconciliation and discharge medication processes. Prescribe, initiate, stop or titrate medicines within scope of competence and in accordance with local and national guidance where appropriately qualified. Provide expert medicines advice to patients and members of the practice team. Identify recurring medicines-related problems or inefficient processes and proactively develop practical solutions with the practice team. Support medicines optimisation, prescribing safety, quality improvement, QOF and relevant enhanced service work. Work flexibly across clinical priorities according to day-to-day practice workload.

The post holder will be supported by experienced GPs and will work as an integral member of the practice multidisciplinary team. We are looking for someone who wants to make a visible difference to patient care, prescribing safety and the day-to-day workload of general practice.

title: Specialty Deputy Head of School for Psychiatry
locations: Flexible across the South West Region, United Kingdom
descriptionHtml:
Two outstanding individuals are sought to fulfil the roles of Deputy Head of School in Psychiatry working across the South West.

The two posts will be available on the basis of a secondment arrangement from their host institution to NHS England - 1.25 PA per week each (5 hours), worked flexibly. The contracts are until the 31 October 2027 in the first instance.

All work undertaken should be incorporated into the Consultant Job Plan. The role of Deputy Head of School is to work with the Head of School and support the Postgraduate Dean in leading the delivery of a wide range of functions, aligned to the NHS England mandate.

The Deputy Head of School will work with the Head of School in focussing upon improvement of learner supervision, assessment and experience, engagement of faculty and ensuring effective educational outcomes, both now and in the future.

The ideal candidates will be an experienced clinicians with a thorough understanding of education and training across the region. They will also have strong leadership and communication skills and be able to work effectively as a member of a multi-professional team.

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms -- enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services.

In March 2025, the Government announced that NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care will increasingly merge functions, ultimately leading to NHS England being fully integrated into the department.

If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR).This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. You may opt out at any stage of the process.

Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices.

We cannot offer visa sponsorship for external candidates.

employer: University Hospitals of Leicester NHS Trust
title: Higher Clinical Fellow
descriptionHtml:
Essential Requirement: Applicants must have successfully passed both MRCP Part 1 and MRCP Part 2 to be eligible for this role. Applications from candidates who do not meet this requirement will not be considered

MIDDLE GRADE REGISTRAR POSITION - IM3 OR ST3

descriptionHtml:
Registrar Post in Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery

Grade: Registrar

Specialty Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery

Reason for Vacancy: Maternity Cover

Supervising Consultant: Barbara Gerber

Average hours work per week : 40hrs with 1:8 on call

Work Pattern: Fixed term until 30th September 2027

This post is non-residential. You will carry a bleep and be on-call with others on a 1:8 on call rota.

As a locum you are responsible for managing your work hours but you must ensure you are safe to work. The registrars timetables are such that they are firm based and registrars will rotate as determined by the registrars lead, Miss Barbara Gerber.

It is vital for patient safety that you takeover and handover jobs and patient information at the start and finish of each shift or day. The handover will normally be supervised and attended by a Consultant once a day, however it is the responsibility of all concerned to ensure that duties and jobs are handed over correctly at all times.

The day starts at 8am with Board Ward Round at the JRH or at the Churchill hospital (Blenheim ward) during Oncology blocks. This should be attended by the on-call team, all SpR's and Consultants and any juniors who are not otherwise engaged. You should attend the board round when on training days in the JR and on Audit days.

Registrars who are timetabled to be in theatre should miss the board round and attend the ward at 7.30am to see all patients for the list on that day and ensure they are consented and ready for theatre and an 8.15 WHO.

You may have your own MOS sessions which will initially be supervised as required.

There will be a second handover and ward round at 5pm, attended by the on-call team including the SpR and sometimes the Consultant on-call. This meets in the board room.

title: GP Clinical Lead, Proactive Care Service
descriptionHtml:
The Primary Care Alliance CIC is seeking an experienced and motivated GP to join our innovative Proactive Care Service (PCS) as a GP Clinical Lead. This is an exciting opportunity to shape and clinically lead a new model of proactive, integrated care for some of the most vulnerable patients across Berkshire West.

Working alongside frailty GPs, prescribing clinicians, care coordinators, a Geriatrician Clinical Lead and wider system partners, you will provide clinical leadership, governance and oversight for a service supporting approximately 1,000 high-risk frail and complex patients.

This is a unique opportunity for a GP who enjoys service development, system leadership and improving outcomes for patients with frailty, multimorbidity and complex care needs. You will play a pivotal role in establishing and refining a service designed to intervene earlier, reduce avoidable deterioration and support patients to remain independent for longer.

Main Duties of the Job

As the GP Clinical Lead, you will:

  • Provide senior clinical leadership and act as the principal GP lead for the Proactive Care Service.
  • Support the mobilisation, implementation and ongoing development of the service.
  • Develop and maintain clinical pathways, SOPs, governance arrangements and escalation processes.
  • Provide clinical oversight and support for frailty GPs and prescribing clinicians.
  • Lead clinical supervision, case discussions, learning and workforce development.
  • Support quality improvement, governance, incident management and service evaluation.
  • Work collaboratively with primary care, community services, acute providers, Adult Social Care and VCSE partners to deliver coordinated care.
  • Help refine and improve the service through a test-and-learn approach using clinical outcomes and service data.

Primary Care Alliance CIC is committed to delivering innovative, integrated healthcare services that improve outcomes for local populations. Our Proactive Care Service has been developed to identify patients at highest risk of deterioration and provide coordinated, multidisciplinary support before health crises occur.

title: TPD for ACCS - Emergency Medicine WM
descriptionHtml:
The role of Training Programme Director is to work with and support the Head of School in leading the delivery of a wide range of functions, aligned to the NHS England mandate.

The Training Programme Director is professionally and managerially accountable to the Head of School. The Training Programme Director will focus upon improvement of learner supervision, assessment and experience, engagement of faculty and ensuring effective educational outcomes, both now and in the future. The role is evolving and will also focus on whole workforce transformation and developing multi-professional links.

To support the Postgraduate Dean, Training Programme Directors will work across the spectrum of health and where relevant, social care, within the context of a team, so that the provision of education reflects changing service models. This will deliver an integrated workforce comprising individuals from a spectrum of professional and other backgrounds.

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms -- enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services.

In March 2025, the Government announced that NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care will increasingly merge functions, ultimately leading to NHS England being fully integrated into the department.

If you currently work within the NHS and if successful at interview, we will initiate an Inter Authority Transfer (IAT) via the Electronic Staff Record (ESR).This retrieves key data from your current or previous NHS employer to support onboarding, including competency status, Continuous Service Dates (CSD), and annual leave entitlement. You may opt out at any stage of the process.

Colleagues with a contractual office base are expected to spend, on average, at least 40% of their time working in our offices.

We cannot offer visa sponsorship forexternal candidates.
