  • Drive service transformation and collaborative working across agencies.

#TeamNottsHC comprises over 11,000 dedicated colleagues who #MakeADifference every day. We deliver intellectual disability, mental health, community health, forensic, and offender healthcare services across Nottinghamshire, Leicestershire, Lincolnshire, and South Yorkshire. Our care is provided from over 200 sites.

We are one of the largest mental health and community Trusts in the East Midlands and one of Nottinghamshire's biggest employers. We also host national and regional services, such as the National High Secure Deaf Service and the Nottingham Centre for Transgender Health.

We offer a variety of employee-led staff networks, including Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI) groups, the Green Champions network, the Freedom to Speak Up network, the Health and Wellbeing Champions network, and the Menopause Champions network. These networks play a vital role in supporting our diverse workforce and promoting a culture of inclusivity.

The health and wellbeing of our colleagues is a top priority. We invest significantly in this through our in-house occupational health and staff counselling services, supported by a dedicated Health and Wellbeing team.

The Trust is committed to reducing its carbon emissions, with a specialised Energy and Environmental team working to ensure compliance with environmental legislation, enhance our environmental performance, and achieve our net-zero commitment.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are looking to recruit aSalaried GP working 4-6 sessions per week at Penn Hill Surgery in Yeovil, caring for approximately 10,350 patients.

The role involves delivering the full range of general practice services within a total triage model (AskMyGP), including a mix of remote and face-to-face consultations, supported clinical administration, and multidisciplinary team working. GPs work with structured workloads and support from a wider clinical and non-clinical team.

This opportunity arises from a combination of practice growth and the relocation of a long-standing GP, allowing us to further develop our service and meet increasing patient demand.

We are a training practice with a strong team ethos, aiming to provide a supportive, collaborative, and sustainable working environment.

The role includes the full range of general practice duties, with a balanced and supported workload:

  • Consultations (remote and face-to-face) within a triage model
  • Management of clinical workload including results, prescriptions, and correspondence
  • Delivery of high-quality, patient-centred care
  • Working collaboratively with the multidisciplinary team
  • Participation in practice meetings, training and development activities

Working patterns are flexible, with sessions agreed between the successful candidates and the practice.

Penn Hill Surgery is a well-established training practice providing care to approximately 10,350 patients.

We are committed to delivering a high standard of general practice, with continuity of care through personal lists, while also working closely with neighbouring practices as part of the Yeovil Primary Care Network.

We use EMIS Weband a range of digital tools to support efficient, modern primary care.

Our team includes:

  • 4 GP Partners
  • 2 Salaried GPs
  • 5 Practice Nurses
  • Clinical Pharmacist
  • Health Coaches
  • Experienced non-clinical team including prescription clerks, reception, medical secretaries and management team

We place a strong emphasis on teamwork and sustainable working. This includes daily clinical huddles and informal coffee breaks, a shared approach to workload (including admin support), and an open-door culture for advice and discussion.

We support ongoing development through regular training, including a monthly half-day closure, and aim to maintain a realistic workload and good worklife balance for all team members.

title: Senior Locally Employed Doctor in Infectious Diseases
descriptionHtml:
The Infectious Diseases Directorate at MFT is delighted to invite applicants for Senior Clinical Fellow (SCF) posts in the Infectious Diseases Managed Single Service based at Wythenshawe Hospital, with the potential to undertake infection related clinical activities at other Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) sites.

Please note: MFT is not a right to work sponsoring organisation for Tier 5. Should a candidate require Tier 5 sponsorship, they must apply through the Academy of Royal College via the MTI Scheme.

The post is available for 12 months with a start date in October 2026 covering maternity leave.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to gain a breadth of experience across the inpatient and outpatient services in Infectious Diseases. They will work closely with the senior medical team to deliver high quality care to patients referred to the team.

The post holder must be able to formulate appropriate diagnostic and management plans, taking into account patient preferences. The post holder will supervise the work of junior colleagues and provide advice & support as necessary. They will be expected to act in a professional manner, knowing their own limitations and liaising with the senior colleagues when required.

The Infectious Diseases team is a highly supportive and effective team. The post holder will be required to be responsive and flexible to the varying needs of the department and its staff, and should have good team working skills that supports them working in partnership with colleagues of all disciplines.

The postholder will be allocated an Education Supervisor who will be responsible for offering support, guidance and supervision during the placement. Whilst, this post is not a formally recognised HENW training post, it will deliver a similar experience. The postholder will be encouraged and supported in developing and maintaining a portfolio evidencing their progress and personal development.

Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) is a leading centre of clinical excellence, renowned for pioneering patient care, advanced medical research, and a collaborative multi-speciality environment. We are the largest provider of specialist services, and our Oxford Road Campus in Manchester is the largest health academic campus in Europe - a great place to progress your career.With over 30,000 employees, a turnover exceeding £3 billion, and 10 hospital and community services, join our team to help us deliver outstanding healthcare to our diverse communities.We offer an engaging and supportive environment, with access to state-of-the-art facilities and cutting-edge technology. Research and Innovation are at the heart of our work, offering opportunities to lead research that shapes the future of medicine, working alongside experts, advancing clinical practice, and improving patient outcomes.

At MFT, we foster a culture where every colleague is valued and empowered to thrive. Your expertise is recognised, your ambitions are supported, and your impact is felt at every level. Whether you want to develop your clinical skills, pursue research interests, or seek leadership opportunities, MFT provides the ideal environment to achieve your medical or professional aspirations.

If you are dedicated to driving clinical innovation and delivering compassionate patient care, join us to shape tomorrow's healthcare; where clinical excellence, innovation, and your career will thrive.

title: General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
Rothwell and Desborough Healthcare Group are seeking an enthusiastic and patient-focused General Practitioner to join our friendly and supportive team.

Working across Rothwell Medical Centre and Desborough Surgery, the successful candidate will join an established and collaborative team committed to delivering excellent standards of care.

The post holder will work autonomously within their scope of practice and will work collaboratively with clinical, management, and administrative colleagues to support the achievement of practice objectives and the delivery of safe, effective, and responsive patient care.

As a training practice, you will also contribute to providing a positive learning environment for students and trainees.

The successful candidate will:

  • Be a fully qualified GP with GMC registration and a licence to practise
  • Demonstrate excellent communication and interpersonal skills
  • Be committed to delivering high-quality, patient-centred care
  • Work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team
  • Share our commitment to continuous learning and service improvement

If you are looking to join a welcoming practice that values teamwork, professional development, and exceptional patient care, we would love to hear from you.

We are a 2 site practice located in the towns of Rothwell and

Desborough (1 mile apart). Our list size is around 22000 and increasing.

We currently have 7 GP partners, 9 salaried GPs, as well as our nursing team including nurse practitioners.

The practice is supported by a management team and very experienced admin, secretarial and reception teams.

We would welcome a candidate who is invested in General Practice to provide quality patient care and drive our innovative business forward.

title: GP Womens Health
descriptionHtml:
An exciting to join the Berkshire West Women's Health Hub as part of our innovative and Community Gynaecology Service.

We are ideally looking for GP's who have Advanced BMS/CoSRH Certificate in Menopause Care.

We are looking for enthusiastic and experienced General Practitioners with significant experience and passion for Women's Health who wish to develop advanced knowledge and practical skills within a supportive, multidisciplinary team.

Working alongside experienced GPwERs, Community Gynaecologists, and collaborative partnership, you will deliver high-quality, evidence-based care closer to home whilst helping transform women's healthcare across Berkshire West.

We have multiple roles available, ideally we are looking for Salaried GP's however we will consider locums.

An exciting opportunity to provide specialist assessment and management of women referred into the Berkshire West Women's Health Hub, delivering high-quality, patient-centred care within agreed clinical pathways whilst further developing your specialist skills, through a structured and supportive environment for professional growth.

Responsibilities include:

  • A mix of triage, virtual and face to face consultations
  • Assessment, diagnosis and management of a wide range of benign gynaecological conditions within the Community Gynaecology Service.
  • Independent management of patients within agreed competency levels.
  • Performing community-based gynaecological procedures appropriate to training and competence such as
  • Removal of lost IUS
  • Difficult insertion of IUS
  • Cervical polypectomy
  • Assess and manage incontinence and prolapse symptoms including vaginal pessary
  • Cervical cautery
  • Participation in MDT and other clinical meetings where appropriate.
  • Contributing to clinical governance, audit, teaching and service improvement initiatives and ensure service is complaint with CQC legislation.
  • Supporting delivery of Berkshire West Women's Health pathways and promoting consistent evidence-based care across Primary Care.
  • Continuous Learning: Maintain an up-to-date knowledge base in womens health, actively engaging in the training and professional development

The Primary Care Alliance is a primary care provider collaborative. We have 36 general practice members. The Alliance became a Community Interest Company in 2026.

Our mission

  • Our mission is to support and sustain the practice ownership model. We seek to do this through:
  • Acting as a united face of primary care across Berkshire West.
  • Supporting the collaboration of members whilst preserving local identity.
  • Giving members access to skills and capabilities they could not access by working alone.
  • Contracting for services that need to be provided at scale.

We are not:

  • Commissioners of health care services. We bid for services we think would best be provided through our primary care partners.
  • Legal or contractual representatives of general practices, these are the respective roles of the Local Medical Committee and the Integrated Care Board.
  • Competitors with practices and PCNs. If a component of primary healthcare is to be commissioned and is most appropriately delivered at practice or neighbourhood level then we are quite clear that the GP practice is sovereign, and in its turn, the PCN.

employer: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
title: Senior Clinical Fellow - Emergency Medicine
descriptionHtml:
Interested in living and working in London?

Want to work in the exciting field of Emergency Medicine?

We are looking for doctors with at least 4 years NHS postgraduate experience to work at Registrar level in Emergency Medicine.

The posts are for 12-months duration, full time, commencing from December 2026 onwards. The post is at Denmark Hill ED which is a designated Major Trauma Centre (SE5 9RS)

Successful candidates will join a dynamic emergency workforce treating a wide spectrum of emergency medicine presentations. This is a great opportunity to broaden your experience while working in a friendly and supportive environment.

There is a strong training culture incorporating lecture-room teaching and clinical supervision, opportunities to attend relevant clinics and courses, and full immersion simulation sessions. There may be opportunities for flexible working, provided all shifts are covered.

The post holders will work up to 48 hours per week (including night shifts and weekend duties).

The rota is self-rostered.

Successful candidates will join a dynamic emergency workforce treating a wide spectrum of adult and paediatric emergency medicine presentations.This is a great opportunity to broaden your experience while working in a friendly and supportive environment.

There is a strong training culture incorporating lecture-room teaching and clinical supervision, opportunities to attend relevant clinics and courses, and full immersion simulation sessions.There are also opportunities for flexible working.

The post holders will work up to 48 hours per week (including night shifts and weekend duties).

Salary is based on the Specialty Registrar payscale - MT04 and above.

Interview dates can be flexible. In addition, whilst face to face interviews are ideal, alternative methods are also acceptable (e.g. TEAMS, Zoom, etc.).

The Trust provides a full range of local and specialist services across its five sites. In June 2026, we launched our new strategy for 2026-31. Our vision is to transform healthcare, and we have agreed six strategic ambitions to help us improve care for patients, and the working lives of our staff.

Our six strategic ambitions are deliveringhigh-quality patient care; creating a great place to work; leading pioneering research, innovation and education; building strong and successful partnerships; providing timely and efficient care; and ensuring long-term financial sustainability.

We have also agreed four new organisational values - Caring, Collaborative, Inclusive, Innovative - and these underpin everything we do, and how our teams interact with the patients under our care.

We are at a pivotal point in our history and we require individuals who are ready to join a highly professional team and make a real, lasting difference to our patients and our people.

King's is committed to delivering Sustainable Healthcare for All via our Green Plan. In line with national Greener NHS ambitions, we have set net zero carbon targets of 2040 for our NHS Carbon Footprint and 2045 for our NHS Carbon Footprint Plus. Everyone's contribution is required in order to meet the goals set out in our Green Plan and we encourage all staff to work responsibly, minimising their contributions to the Trust's carbon emissions, waste and pollution wherever possible.

employer: Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant Forensic Psychiatrist (HMP Bronzefield)
descriptionHtml:
CNWL Health & Justice Services

Consultant Psychiatrist in Forensic Psychiatry

HMP Bronzefield

10PAs (additional PAs can be considered)

Be part of something extraordinary at the largest female prison in Europe.

Are you passionate about providing high-quality mental health care in a unique and dynamic setting? Do you want to be part of a team that values diversity, inclusion, and innovation?

We are offering the opportunity of a part clinical and part research post with the Institute of Psychiatry specifically looking into areas of improving health to women in prison. As part of this work, we will be reviewing data on short sentences and the risks these pose to women, family life and long term health and identifying areas of research with the potential to influence policy and explore expanding sentencing options for women.

We offer a generous annual and study leave entitlement, NHS pension scheme, support with relocation expenses for up to 8K and a range of lifestyle benefits, such as various staff discounts including discount on the purchase and leasing of new cars.

We areseeking an enthusiastic Consultant Psychiatrist/Forensic Consultant to join our Health & Justice Services at HMP Bronzefield, the largest female prison in Europe. This is a rewarding opportunity to lead and develop mental health care in a complex but highly supportive environment, making a real difference to the lives of women in custody.

? Forensic experience is not essential--we welcome applications from psychiatrists across general adult, community, liaison, or forensic backgrounds who are keen to bring their skills into the secure environment.? A strong commitment to Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI) is central to this role, ensuring that care is trauma-informed, gender-responsive, and culturally competent.? Significant opportunities for research and innovation--whether in quality improvement, digital transformation, or AI in healthcare, with consideration for additional time to pursue these interests.? Potential for an honorary academic post at University College London (UCL) for research-active candidates with appropriate experience and qualifications.? Leadership development--access to formal training and mentoring to support career progression within CNWL and beyond.? Optional paid extra work in court liaison and diversion services, for those interested in gaining additional experience at the interface of health and justice.

CNWL's Health & Justice Service Directorate is experienced in applying for prison and secure settings contracts. We currently provide a range of services (including mental health, substance misuse, sexual health and primary care) to the following prisons: HMPs Bronzefield, High Down, Downview, Coldingley, Aylesbury, Felltham and Woodhill, We also provide community forensic services in North West London, Liaison and Diversion services to police stations and Magistrates' Courts (Uxbridge, Hillington, Willesden and Westminster), to the Central Criminal and Harrow Crown Court, as well as low secure specialist forensic services at Park Royal.

The Mental Health Team in HMP Bronzefield works closely with prison staff and other health and non-health contracted services to provide a person-centered, continuous service that promotes positive health and social care outcomes, sustainable resettlement and reduction in re-offending.

HMP & YOI Bronzefield is a modern purpose-built prison for women which opened in 2004. It performs the function of a local prison, accepting prisoners direct from the courts.Accommodation: 3 main residential units holding approximately 135 women each. A fourth residential unit holding 77 women was opened in 2010. Bronzefield also has Level 4 Healthcare provision with inpatient facilities for 18 women. A smaller 10-bed Help & Direction Unit which served as an intermediary unit between Healthcare and main residence was decommissioned by MoJ in 2010.

employer: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
title: Clinical Fellow in Colorectal Surgery - Heartlands (April 2027)
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a fixed term 12 month post to work at registrar level in Colorectal Surgery to backfill Deanery vacancies from 07/04/2027 - 04/04/2028.

University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust serves the largest populations in the UK and is comprised of four hospitals namely the Queen Elizabeth Hospital, Heartlands Hospital, Good Hope Hospital and Solihull Hospital. This post represents a new and exciting opportunity for General Surgeons in Training, aimed at surgical trainees at above ST3 level in General Surgery based at Heartlands Hospital, as part of University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Trust. The post on offer is for 1 year, with a view to extending. Initial assessment of progress will be made at 6 months with extension beyond this mutually agreed. The appointed candidate will be expected to provide support for an emergency general surgery as well as elective colorectal services.

The successful applicant will be appointed to the Colorectal and General Surgery service at Heartlands Hospital. The post will be particularly suited to ST3 or above applicants who are wishing to develop their clinical portfolio. Applicants will be expected to participate in departmental audit and research appropriate to their educational requirements.

Clinical duties will include being part of the 1 in 16 general surgical registrar on-call rota. The clinical work will be based at Heartlands and Solihull clinical sites. UHB represents the largest acute Trust in the country and as such has one of the largest and most ethnically diverse surgical patient and clinician cohorts in the UK. There is a well-established surgical and research teams across all sites.

University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust strives to have an inclusive culture where everyone feels like they belong, can thrive, knows that they add value and feels valued. We do this by developing compassionate and culturally competent leaders, being values driven in all that we do and by creating a welcoming and inclusive workplace that thrives on the diversity of our people. As such we want to attract and recruit talented individuals from all backgrounds, and for each of you to feel supported for the diversity you bring, to achieve your full potential. For those staff with a disability, including physical disability, long term health condition, mental health or neurodiverse condition, this also means being committed to making reasonable adjustments needed for you to carry out your role.

employer: Herefordshire and Worcestershire Health and Care NHS Trust
title: Speciality Doctor in Sexual Health
descriptionHtml:
This post offers an exciting opportunity to join a highly motivated team of health professionals providing high quality sexual and reproductive healthcare across Worcestershire. The post holder will be re based at the Aconbury North, Worcester site, but required to also do some clinics at Kidderminster Sexual Health clinic as part of their weekly role. They may be also required to cover the Arrowside sexual Health clinic at Redditch should the need arise due to absences or other circumstances. to cover other sites if required.

Seven sessions/week - minimum 6 sessions per week substantive/permanent post.

The post holder will provide medical input to the Worcestershire Integrated Sexual Health service. The team is a countywide (Worcestershire) service that aims to provide a level 3 sexual health service

The post holder will be expected to have access to a car and hold a driving licence. Post holder will be expected to maintain good communication with wider healthcare professionals in the community e.g GPs, in the spirit of person centred and joined up care, within the bounds of confidentiality within Sexual health.

The post holder will be required to maintain a good standard of practice, including the assessments of patients, liaison with other professionals, record keeping, and other associated duties as directed.

To provide clinical services in sexual health, contraception and reproductive healthcare for patients with reference to national guidelines and within limits defined in locally agreed operating procedures

To be prepared to provide emergency contraception and counselling and referral of clients requesting abortion.

To provide non-judgemental counselling on all sexual health issues and to refer appropriately any service user. To provide counselling on all the available options to women presenting with an unintended/unwanted pregnancy. To work within the legal processes for abortion , in conjunction with the nurse-led early medical abortion service

To participate in service quality governance, audit and medical meetings across the county wide Sexual Health Service, as well as undertake departmental audit, as appropriate.

To be approachable, non-judgemental and responsive to client needs, irrespective of their age, gender, race, religion or sexuality. Ensure patient confidentiality is maintained at all times

To have a keen interest and to be responsible for keeping up to date

To provide in-clinic teaching, training and supervision of junior doctors, medical students, physician associate students, foundation year pharmacists and nursing students who come to observe in the department, once a sufficient level of experience is reached.

Comply with the GMC Duties of a Doctor at all times

At Herefordshire and Worcestershire Health and Care NHS Trust, we are working together to deliver outstanding care. We run community hospitals and community health services across Worcestershire and provide mental health and learning disability services across both Herefordshire and Worcestershire.

Our people (all 4500+ of them) provide services for people of all ages, experiencing both physical and/or mental health conditions from over 100 sites.

We will support you to thrive; offer flexible working options for a great work-life balance, help you fulfil your ambitions, and empower you to make positive changes within your team or service. We value diversity and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, cultures, and ethnicities.

What we offer;

  • 27 days leave plus bank holidays, increasing up to 33 days with long service
  • Generous NHS pension and enhanced pay when you work unsocial hours
  • Flexible and agile working opportunities
  • Great maternity, paternity, and adoption support
  • Wide range of supportive staff networks
  • Health and wellbeing opportunities

If you would like to know more, please visit our website Staff benefits | Herefordshire and Worcestershire Health and Care NHS Trust

Sharing your data -As a data controller we may sometimes need to process your data to pursue our legitimate business interests, for example to request a survey from you (optional), to support the Trusts understanding of where you gained interest in working for the Trust.

title: Admin Assistant
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an enthusiastic and motivated Administrative Assistant to join our busy, friendly and caring GP practice. This is an excellent opportunity for someone eager to develop their skills in a supportive primary care environment. As the first point of contact for many of our patients and a key member of our administrative team, you will play an important role in helping us deliver high-quality, compassionate care.

We are seeking someone who is proactive, organised, and committed to providing excellent service. If youre keen to learn, enjoy working with people, and want to be part of a practice that values teamwork, kindness, and professionalism, we would love to hear from you.

  • Front Desk Support: Provide a welcoming and efficient reception service, greeting patients, answering queries, and directing them appropriately.

  • Appointment Management: Book, amend, and cancel appointments using the clinical system, ensuring smooth patient flow throughout the day.

  • Patient Communication: Handle incoming calls, emails, and requests promptly and professionally, providing accurate information and support.

  • Administration & Records: Maintain and update patient records, process registrations, scan and file documents, and ensure confidentiality at all times.

  • Prescription Support: Assist with repeat prescription requests, ensuring they are processed accurately and in line with practice protocols.

  • Workflow Management: Manage daily administrative tasks including incoming post, tasks, and document routing to the clinical team.

  • Collaboration: Work closely with clinicians, nurses, and other admin staff to support the smooth running of the practice and deliver high-quality patient care.

  • General Office Duties: Carry out routine tasks such as emailing, data entry, and maintaining an organised workspace.

  • Service Quality: Uphold the practices values of care, compassion, and professionalism while providing excellent customer service.

York Road Group Practice is a busy, town-centre surgery providing high-quality, patient-centred care to our local community. We are proud to offer a welcoming and supportive environment, underpinned by a strong, multidisciplinary team that brings together a wide range of clinical and administrative expertise.

Our clinical team includes five GP Partners, four Salaried GPs, and one Advanced Nurse Practitioner, supported by an Occupational Therapist, Clinical Pharmacist, a Pharmacy Technician, and dedicated Care Coordinators. We also have a highly skilled Nursing Team that plays a vital role in delivering routine and complex patient care.

Behind the scenes, our multiskilled Administrative Team ensures the smooth running of the practice. This includes our Medical Secretary, Admin Coordinator, Team Leader, and Practice Manager, all working collaboratively to provide an efficient and responsive service for both patients and staff.

As a forward-thinking and dynamic practice, we strive to maintain excellent standards of care while continually adapting to the changing needs of our community.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
We are currently seekingdedicated and motivated Salaried General Practitioners (GPs) to join the friendly and forward thinking team at Chiltern House Medical Centre, based in High Wycombe.

The role offers multiple clinical sessions per week, with flexibility in working days to suit the right candidate and the needs of the practice. You will work within a supportive multidisciplinary team that includes nurse practitioners, clinical pharmacists, paramedics, and other allied health professionals.

The position offers a competitive salary and the opportunity to work in a collaborative and patient focused environment.

Chiltern House Medical Centre is committed to delivering high quality, patient centred care and provides an excellent environment for GPs who value teamwork, innovation, and making a meaningful difference while contributing to the practice's continuous improvement.

The Salaried GP will be responsible for delivering high-quality primary care services to patients, including conducting face-to-face and telephone consultations, managing long-term conditions, handling acute presentations, and carrying out clinical administration such as prescriptions, referrals, and test result reviews. The role also includes participation in on-call duties, supporting clinical audits, contributing to practice development, and collaborating with the wider multidisciplinary team to ensure seamless, patient-centred care. Home visits may be required on occasion, although these are typically supported by the practices paramedic team.

Chiltern House Medical Centre is a well-established NHS primary care practice located in High Wycombe. The surgery provides a comprehensive range of primary healthcare services focused on promoting patient wellbeing, preventing illness, and managing long-term conditions.

The practice is supported by a multidisciplinary team that includes GPs, nurses, and allied health professionals, working collaboratively to deliver high-quality, patient-centred care. Chiltern House Medical Centre places a strong emphasis on continuity of care, patient confidentiality, and ongoing service improvement.

The surgery is part of the local Primary Care Network (PCN), enabling close collaboration and shared resources with neighbouring practices to enhance patient outcomes. Patient feedback is actively encouraged through compliments, suggestions, and complaints, supporting the practices commitment to continuous improvement and excellent service delivery.

employer: Honeybeerecruitment.com Ltd. trading as Military Medical Personnel (MMP)
title: General Practitioner
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for a Locum Doctor (General Practitioner) to cover an assignment with the Ministry of Defence (MoD), at Albermarle Newcastle Medical Centre, in Newcastle-upon-Tyne, Tyne And Wear.

This is a locum role (37 hours per week) and the successful candidate will deliver an exceptional standard of care to the MoD service personnel.

Hourly Rate - £69.12 per hour

Job Description:

  • Undertake Primary Healthcare (PHC) clinics for Military and entitled personnel.
  • Examinations and Occupational Health (OH) fitness for work assessments within the locum doctors scope of experience and qualification.
  • To inform the local medical authority of any case that may affect a servicepersons ability to undertake their duties.
  • To complete reports and documentation in accordance with MOD policy or the requirements of any other government department.
  • To attend individual management reviews or case conferences with Primary Healthcare (PHC) and/or line management as required.

Essential requirements/ Qualifications/ Experience:

  • Registration with the General Medical Council both on the main register and on the General Medical Council (GMC) GP Register without Restrictions.
  • Must have a current, satisfactory in date annual appraisal in line with the requirements of the General Medical Councils (GMCs) Good Medical Practice (GMP).
  • Must be in date and able to provide certification for Safeguarding Children and Young People and Safeguarding Adults up to and including Level 3 training.
  • Must be on the UK NHS Performers List and provide an NHS Performer number.

About Military Medical Personnel and Our Benefits:

Military Medical Personnel (MMP) is a specialist recruitment consultancy dedicated exclusively to providing locum civilian medical, dental and healthcare professionals to the Ministry of Defence. We are a contracted supplier to the MOD and have locum vacancies on military bases throughout the UK and occasionally overseas locations.

Military Medical Personnel offer an attractive package for candidates which may include the following:

  • Attractive rates of pay with weekly payments and choice of payment model
  • A generous Refer a Friend bonus scheme
  • Flexibility of long- and short-term assignments to suit your availability
  • Free uniforms provided (if required)
  • A PVG membership (Disclosure Scotland) or an Access Northern Ireland certificate is required for this role.
  • Free mandatory training
  • Weekly payments
  • Assigned an experienced consultant who will support you throughout your application and will continue to look after you during your assignment

All job placements are subject to the receipt of satisfactory compliance requirements.

Please note that MMP is unable to sponsor work visas. Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK, such as a valid visa with no restrictions on hours.

Due to the volume of applications received, only candidates who meet the essential criteria will be contacted regarding their application.

employer: The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
title: Post-CCT Fellow in Oculoplastics
descriptionHtml:
We are delighted to be able to offer an opportunity for a highly motivated, ambitious individual to join our well integrated team within the Department of Ophthalmology, in the post of Post CCT Oculoplastic Fellow (Trust doctor in ophthalmology ST7+ Equivalent).

We aim to provide a high intensity surgical focussed fellowship with supervised oculoplastics lists with all 6 consultants, as well as quality clinical exposure and supervision in management across all subspecialty fields represented. We are extremely proud of our reputation in oculoplastics training, and are committed to ensuring our fellows receive experience of the highest standards.

This post is aimed at post CCST trainees (ST7+) who have already demonstrated a significant interest in oculoplastics and are looking to further their surgical and clinical management skills including subspecialty experience to the level of an NHS consultant, with the possibility of highly specialised orbital surgical training. This is specifically a fixed term post of 12 months duration for subspecialist training development with a high level of direct supervision specifically aimed at developing in clinical, surgical and managerial skills within a training role There is no on call commitment or banding with this post.

For an informal discussion and further information regarding the opportunity and Directorate, please contact: Lucy Clarke on 0191 2825404 (secretary), or via email at lucy.clarke16@nhs.net

title: Head of School (Foundation School Director) - Thames Valley
descriptionHtml:
NHSE is looking to appointment a Foundation School Director overseeing the Thames Valley Foundation School. The post would be an ideal opportunity for a Foundation Training Programme Director aiming to further develop their educational portfolio.

Please note: The post is offered on a contract for services basis and all candidates are reminded that if they are successful, they are responsible for securing written agreement from their Trust for release from clinical work for the specified number of PAs.

The Foundation School Director is professionally and managerially accountable to the Postgraduate Dean. The Foundation School Director will focus upon improvement of learner supervision, assessment and experience, engagement of faculty and ensuring effective educational outcomes, both now and in the future. The role is evolving and will also focus on whole workforce transformation and developing multi-professional links mas well as innovative ways of curriculum delivery and workforce well-being strategies.

The Foundation School Director will be expected to meet the challenges of leading the School and Education Providers to deliver the changing curricular in an evolving service landscape.

To support the Postgraduate Dean, Foundation School Director work across the spectrum of health and where relevant, social care, within the context of a team, so that the provision of education reflects changing service models. This will deliver an integrated workforce comprising individuals from a spectrum of professional and other backgrounds.

NHS England has a wide range of statutory functions, responsibilities and regulatory powers. These are focused on supporting the wider NHS to deliver high quality care, as well as doing those things that are best done once for the whole NHS.

Our staff bring expertise across clinical, operational, commissioning, technology, data science, cyber security, software engineering, education, and commercial specialisms -- enabling us to design and deliver high-quality NHS services.

In March 2025, the Government announced that NHS England and the Department of Health and Social Care will increasingly merge functions, ultimately leading to NHS England being fully integrated into the department.

title: Practice Nurse
descriptionHtml:
We are seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Practice Nurse to join our friendly and supportive GP practice in Sidmouth.

This is an exciting opportunity to work within a collaborative multidisciplinary team, delivering safe, effective, and patient-focused care to our local community. You will play a key role in managing long-term conditions, delivering preventative care, and supporting patients to achieve better health outcomes.

At Sid Valley Practice, we pride ourselves on our strong team culture, commitment to high-quality care, and dedication to staff wellbeing and professional development. We actively support ongoing training and career progression, making this an excellent opportunity for both experienced nurses and those looking to expand their skill set.

To be responsible for the implementation of processes for the effective management of patients with long-term conditions using evidence-based practice including care for elderly and housebound patients.

Working as a senior member of the practice multidisciplinary team, the post holder will ensure nursing services are delivered effectively to the patient population.

Working to agreed local and national protocols, the post holder will provide assessment, monitoring, review, and health education to patients with long-term conditions.

Additionally, the role involves providing screening and health education advice to the practice population, promoting and supporting healthy lifestyle choices.

Key objectives of the role include:

  • Providing high quality nursing care and support
  • Supporting patients with the long term health conditions using evidence-based practices
  • Ensuring effective delivery of clinical services
  • Contributing to the development and review of clinical policies and procedures

Sid Valley Practice is a well-established and forward-thinking GP practice based in Sidmouth, Devon, operating from the Beacon Medical Centre with an additional site at Sidmouth Hospital. We provide high-quality, patient-centred care to a coastal and semi-rural population, combining traditional general practice values with modern multidisciplinary working.

We have a registered list size of approximately 14,500 patients, delivering a broad range of primary care services including chronic disease management, minor surgery, immunisations, and nurse-led clinics.

Our Team

We are proud of our supportive, collaborative, and experienced multidisciplinary team. This includes GP partners, salaried and associate GPs, advanced nurse practitioners, practice nurses, healthcare assistants, and a skilled administrative and patient care navigation team.

Our nursing team plays a key role in delivering high-quality care through chronic disease management, treatment room services, and preventative health work, supported by nurse prescribers and advanced practitioners. We also work closely with community services such as district nurses, midwives, and specialist teams to ensure joined-up care for our patients.

We foster a positive working environment with a strong emphasis on teamwork, professional development, and delivering compassionate care to our local community.

title: Specialty Doctor in Palliative care
descriptionHtml:
This post is for a Specialty Doctor in Palliative Care.

It would be suitable for doctors who are fully registered with a license to practice, and who have at least 2 years clinical experience post-registration. Essential and desirable criteria are listed under 'person specifications' below.

This post is particularly suitable for doctors who have an interest in any of the following:

Pursuing a career in Palliative Medicine

Working across the interface between hospital and community care

Acquiring excellent advanced communication skills

Working in a dynamic environment

Working within a multi-disciplinary team

Working collaboratively with other members of the multidisciplinary team (MDT): MDT working is a key component of working in the department. The post holder will work closely with the Hospital Specialist Palliative Care Team and with any other members of the MDT.

Reviewing patients referred to the Specialist Palliative Care Team (SPCT) on any ward (including ED) within Bedford Hospital. This will include new patient assessments and reviews of patients on the team's caseload.

As needed, reviewing patients alone or with another member of the SPCT.

Electronic prescribing of medications for symptom management for patients on the SPCT caseload.

Leading and/or attending family meetings as required.

As one of the largest NHS Trusts in our region you will have access to a programme of high quality training and development to help you grow your career. The Trust continues to be committed to delivering the best patient care using the best clinical knowledge and technology.

Our Values

We not only recruit based on qualifications and experience - we recruit individuals who demonstrate the behaviours which underpin our Trusts core values. We achieve this by using values based recruitment. We are dedicated to making our recruitment practices as inclusive as possible for everyone, we are committed to promoting equality and diversity, and creating a culture that values differences.

Please note that vacancies may close prior to the advertised closing date when sufficient number of applications have been received. All new staff will be subject to a probationary period covering first 6 months in post. Travel between hospital sites may be required. Please review all documents attached to ensure you familiarize yourself with all requirements of the job.

title: Locum Consultant Radiologist with MSK special interest
descriptionHtml:
Applications are invited for a Locum Consultant Radiologist with MSK interest post at the Wye Valley NHS Trust (WVT).

A full time (10 PA) Consultant post is being advertised. This is an additional post, approved to meet additional demand. The post is intended to be whole-time, but applications would be considered from candidates wishing for personal or domestic reasons to work part-time.

The successful candidate will join the existing establishment of 18 Consultant Radiologists in providing a comprehensive Radiology service to the population of Herefordshire Health District plus a catchment population from mid Wales and referrals from parts of surrounding counties of Shropshire, Worcestershire and Gwent (total population 230,000).

The post holder should have broad radiology experience with the skills expected from a fully trained and experienced general Radiologist, as well as a more specialised interest with experience in MSK radiology.

The post holder will be expected to take part in departmental audit and clinical governance issues, provide training and education to medical and other departmental staff as required and participate in Multi-disciplinary team (MDT) Meetings.

For further details on our new CDC please click on this link:

Community Diagnostic Centre

Unused SPA time would be expected to be used for direct clinical care.

Wye Valley NHS Trust is a member of an NHS Foundation Group with South Warwickshire NHS FT , the George Eliot Hospital NHS Trust and Worcestershire Acute Hospitals NHS Trust.

Located on the border with Wales in the shadow of the Black Mountains, we provide acute and community services across Herefordshire and into parts of Powys and run Hereford County Hospital and the community hospitals in Bromyard, Leominster and Ross-on-Wye.

Worcestershire is our neighbouring county. The post holder will be required to travel between sites.

We are a progressive and forward looking trust with ambitious plans to improve quality and integrate patient pathways through close collaborative working with our partners to deliver the quality of care we'd want for our family and friends.

More than 3,500 people work for the Trust - they tell us it's a great place to work, blending the busyness of a DGH with the benefits of working in a beautiful rural and unspoilt county like Herefordshire.

We can offer a great work-life balance and have a fine tradition of working with staff to help them achieve their full potential.

Russell Hardy, Trust Chairman: "The strength of the Trust is its amazing staff; a great place to work, a great place to develop your career and a great place to reach your potential."

Our values -Care, Accountability, Respect and Excellence - are at the heart of all we do. We believe in providing the right care in the right place at the right time...all the time.

title: Consultant Obstetrician High Risk Pregnancy and Labour Ward Lead
descriptionHtml:
Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to appoint an enthusiastic, forward-thinking Consultant Obstetrician with a specialist interest in High-Risk Pregnancy and Intrapartum Care (10 PAs). We are committed to flexible working and welcome applications from candidates wishing to work less than full time or via job share, with individualised job planning arrangements agreed with the successful candidate. You will provide visible senior clinical leadership on the Labour Ward, working collaboratively with the multidisciplinary team to ensure the delivery of safe, personalised, and evidence-based maternity care. Playing a pivotal role in service development, you will drive improvements in maternity safety, clinical governance, workforce development, risk management, quality improvement, and patient experience across maternity services. Key responsibilities include promoting multidisciplinary working, supporting the development of medical and midwifery staff, and contributing to the implementation of local and national maternity safety initiatives. You will also share responsibility for the delivery and development of our multidisciplinary obstetric emergency training programme (PROMPT). By leading simulation training and promoting shared learning from incidents and audits, you will help improve teamwork, patient safety, and clinical outcomes to support our ambition of delivering outstanding maternity care.

Deliver high-quality, evidence-based, patient-centred obstetric care across GHNHSFT.o Participate in the Consultant Obstetric on-call rota, leading acute obstetric emergencies.o Provide Labour Ward leadership, promoting safe, personalised maternity care through multidisciplinary teamwork.o Deliver and develop care for complex, high-risk pregnancies, including maternal medicine and intrapartum care.o Develop specialist services, including fetal growth surveillance, obstetric ultrasound, preterm birth prevention, and perinatal mental health.o Co-lead and develop the Trust's multidisciplinary PROMPT emergency training programme.o Lead quality improvement, patient safety, clinical governance, and risk management initiatives.o Collaborate with obstetric, midwifery, anaesthetic, neonatal, and allied health colleagues to optimise outcomes.o Supervise trainees and students, supporting teaching, audit, research, and strategic Directorate objectives.

The Obstetrics and Gynaecology Directorate sits within the Women and Children's Division, led by Chief of Service Dr Clara Thompson, Director of Midwifery Zita Martinez, Divisional Operations Director Becky Hughes, and Divisional Nursing Director Karen Pudge. Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (GHFT) runs one of the largest maternity services in the South West, supporting 5,411 births in 2024/25. We offer specialist clinics in fetal medicine, maternal medicine, preterm birth, and diabetes in pregnancy, with strong links to the South West Maternal Medicine Network and tertiary fetal medicine in Bristol. Our services span three sites:o Gloucestershire Royal Hospital (Women's Centre): Consultant-led delivery suite with two obstetric theatres, alongside midwifery-led birth unit, Maternity Assessment Unit, antenatal clinics, ultrasound, and our Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.o Cheltenham General Hospital (St Paul's Wing): Antenatal clinics, fetal medicine, obstetric ultrasound, and a standalone midwifery-led birth unit.o Stroud Maternity Hospital: Antenatal clinics, obstetric ultrasound, and a standalone midwifery-led birth unit. Committed to delivering Best Care for Everyone, our success relies on compassionate, expert staff making a lasting difference to women, babies, and families across Gloucestershire.

title: Locum Consultant Gastroenterology and Hepatology
descriptionHtml:
Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals NHS Trust is seeking to appoint a Locum Consultant in Gastroenterology and Hepatology on a 12-month fixed-term contract, working across Queen's Hospital and King George Hospital.

The successful candidate will have experience in both Gastroenterology and Hepatology and will contribute to the delivery of specialist liver disease services alongside general Gastroenterology outpatient clinics, diagnostic and therapeutic endoscopy, inpatient care and emergency GI bleed on-call commitments.

The post is required to support the continuity and development of Gastroenterology and Hepatology services following changes to the existing consultant provision.

Applicants should demonstrate experience in managing complex liver disease, including decompensated cirrhosis and liver failure, alongside a broad range of gastrointestinal conditions.

The successful candidate will also contribute to multidisciplinary team working, clinical governance, teaching, supervision of junior medical staff and service improvement.

The post offers a 10 PA job plan, including direct clinical care and supporting professional activities, to be agreed with the successful candidate.

The successful candidate must demonstrate competence in general Gastroenterology, upper and lower GI endoscopy, management of GI bleeding and specialist Hepatology care, and will be expected to undertake the following responsibilities:

oEndoscopy (inpatient and outpatient) Service lists are at 12 points with training lists at 10.

oProvide consultant-led inpatient care on a rotating ward-week model (1:8)

oRun specialist Hepatology and General Gastroenterology outpatient clinics (minimum two per week).

oParticipate in and support the development of hepatology pathways for viral hepatitis, MASLD, autoimmune liver disease, and alcohol-related liver disease.

oContribute to emergency endoscopy services (1:14 GI bleed rota).

oSupport junior medical staff through supervision, mentorship, and teaching.

oParticipate in multidisciplinary team (MDT) meetings including benign liver disease and upper GI cancer.

oEngage in service development and improvement initiatives within the Gastroenterology and Hepatology departments.

oProvide specialist assessment, investigation, treatment and follow-up for patients with chronic liver disease, cirrhosis and its complications, including appropriate escalation and referral to regional specialist liver services.

oWork collaboratively with the Hepatology Clinical Lead and specialist nursing team to support coordinated inpatient and outpatient liver disease management.

We're an organisation that is getting better and better and our improvements are driven by a determination to deliver care we're proud of and our patients are happy with.

We operate from two main sites - KGH in Goodmayes and Queen's Hospital in Romford. We have two busy emergency departments with more than 346,000 people visiting them last year. We're campaigning to secure the £35m we need to transform the A&E at Queen's and get rid of corridor care.

We run a Women's Health Hub in Ilford; an Ageing Well Centre in Hornchurch; and Community Diagnostic Centres (CDC) at Barking Community Hospital and at St George's Health and Wellbeing Hub. These CDCs are open 12 hours a day, 7 days a week.

The majority of our 8,400 staff - who come from 146 different countries - live in the three diverse London boroughs we serve and are from black, Asian and minority ethnic groups. Many can work flexibly and more than 400 of them are on our Ofsted accredited apprenticeship programmes. We're proud to be a London Living Wage employer.

University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust strives to have an inclusive culture where everyone feels like they belong, can thrive, knows that they add value and feels valued. We do this by developing compassionate and culturally competent leaders, being values driven in all that we do and by creating a welcoming and inclusive workplace that thrives on the diversity of our people. As such we want to attract and recruit talented individuals from all backgrounds, and for each of you to feel supported for the diversity you bring, to achieve your full potential. For those staff with a disability, including physical disability, long term health condition, mental health or neurodiverse condition, this also means being committed to making reasonable adjustments needed for you to carry out your role.

title: Trust Doctor in Emergency Medicine (ST1-2)
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for enthusiastic doctors who have successfully completed Foundation Year 2 training to take up this post in Emergency Medicine.

It is an exciting time to join our team as we have recently redeveloped our Emergency Department and have implemented a wide range of new processes and pathways. We are now expanding our workforce to offer additional opportunities to motivated and engaged doctors who wish to develop themselves and the department.

We offer exceptional training opportunities in point of care ultrasound (POCUS) with two hours of dedicated teaching every week day! There is also considerable scope for successful candidates to be involved in service re-design, simulation and quality improvement projects.

We have recently received awards and recognition for two projects at trust level. In the past year, a number of our trust grade doctors have been promoted to the next tier and three of our middle grades have been promoted to consultant level. Engaged and motivated candidates will find themselves at home in a culture of aspiration and excellence!

  • To review and appropriately manage undifferentiated medical patients presenting to the Emergency Department, with senior support as required.
  • To complete clinical notes contemporaneously, and to adequately record decision making on the computerised records system, including the x-ray reporting system.
  • To react positively to changes in planned workload when unforeseen interruptions occur and to plan tasks and activities accordingly.
  • To prioritise own workload demonstrating a methodical and well organised approach.
  • To ensure patient confidentiality is adhered to at all times and escalate any barriers leading to delays in patient management or referral.

Royal Surrey is a compassionate and collaborative acute and community Trust. Recognising that our 5,000 colleagues are our greatest strength, we offer a comprehensive health and wellbeing programme alongside a strong commitment to developing your career. Our diverse and welcoming Royal Surrey family ensures you feel valued from your initial interview and throughout your time with us.

We are clinically led and provide joined-up care by bridging hospital and community services, alongside delivering regional specialist cancer care. Our main acute hospital site is in Guildford, with community sites at Milford, Haslemere and Cranleigh, and services delivered in patients' homes across Guildford and Waverley.

We work in partnership with Ashford & St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust through a collaborative Group Model, supporting joined-up services, workforce flexibility and development opportunities.

The Care Quality Commission (CQC) has rated us as Outstanding. We are proud of our achievements and continue to invest in our people and infrastructure.

To learn more about life at Royal Surrey, please watch our short video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R96pMboIYdo

Adverts may close early, so you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

employer: Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust
title: Consultant ACM
descriptionHtml:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an enthusiastic, dynamic, and motivated consultant to join our Care of the Elderly team working as an integral part of our multidisciplinary team. Our team comprises of consultants, junior doctors, nurses and the full complement of allied health professionals providing a wide range of general and subspecialist geriatric treatment and support to the local population, providing seamless care through multidisciplinary team (MDT) working.

With a sound knowledge of Care of the Elderly, as well as an interest in general medicine or the motivation to learn and professionally develop these areas while working in a supportive environment, the successful applicant will provide a high standard of clinical care whilst supporting new ways of delivering quality services. As an organisation we have been proactive in developing systems for shared decision making and supporting self-management along with social prescribing and would expect the appointee to actively work supporting this aim.

An ability to work independently, and more importantly, as part of a team, whilst working calmly under pressure is essential. If you would like to work in a dynamic, caring, inclusive and forward-thinking environment where innovation is welcomed, then we would welcome your application

Across the Northern Care Alliance NHS Trust, we have a fully established a successful Frailty Same Day Emergency Care (SDEC) Service whose purpose is to ensure that frail older people in a crisis situation receive expert, responsive, and safe care in a place closest to home, that best meets their needs.

The Care of the Elderly team works collaboratively with community services and primary care to support healthcare provided at home and early discharge from hospital wherever appropriate, via the Hospital at Home model. The successful candidate will be expected to identify, onboard, and provide senior review for patients suitable for assessment within the Frailty SDEC service as well as those suitable for admission to the frailty Hospital at Home service - providing hospital care at home. Working collaboratively with the local community services, the service, through rapid identification and assessment of frailty would support admission avoidance and minimal inpatient stay to deliver the most appropriate outcomes for this patient cohort.

Continual professional development is encouraged, and while not a formal requirement for appointment, this post is highly suitable for consultants who may be working towards, or wish to work towards, a higher qualification in Frailty or Elderly Medicine.

The Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust (NCA) provides hospital and integrated health and social care services to over one million people living across Greater Manchester. Our 20,000 colleagues care for people in hospital and in the community, working across Bury, Rochdale, Oldham, and Salford, to save and improve lives.As a large NHS trust we are committed to enhancing the health of our local population by delivering consistently high standards of care and collaborating closely with local authorities and key partners. We believe in our power and potential to make a difference and we are always looking for people who demonstrate our three core values - care, appreciate and inspire - to join our team.In return, we can offer you a job role with purpose and flexibility. The size and scale of the NCA means we can provide more challenge and opportunities so your career can always be moving in the right direction. By joining us you can also access a competitive benefits package, including, a fantastic annual leave allowance, flexible working opportunities and protected hours for health and wellbeing activities, helping you to achieve more personal downtime and a better work-life balance.

title: Salaried GP
descriptionHtml:
Alnwick Medical Group is looking to recruit a Salaried GP.

Temporary Maternity cover from January 2027 - September 2027 (with the possibility of progressing to a permanent post) Part Time, 6 sessions / 3 days per week (Tues, Wed, Fri) salary will be up to £11,000-£11,900 per session depending on experience.

If you are interested in applying for this exciting vacancy (or wish to find out more information) application is by CV and covering letter to:

Paula Breen, Strategic Practice Manager, paula.breen1@nhs.net Telephone: 01665 650270 / 07908272573

We would encourage you to visit our website to learn more about Alnwick Medical Group: https://www.alnwickmedicalgroup.nhs.uk/

Your day will consist of:

  • The delivery of highly effective medical care to our patient population consistent with the GMS contract via face to face, telephone consultations and home visits.
  • Generic prescribing adhering to guidance.
  • Processing of administration promptly to include: referrals, correspondence, repeat prescriptions and test results.
  • As a total triage Practice, you will on a rotational basis triage alongside another GP allocating patients to appropriate practitioners in an appropriate timescale, whilst also dealing with some urgent patient appointments

We are a forward thinking SystmOne (with eConsult & Ardens), Training Practice with a list size of almost 20,000 patients, operating across four sites in rural Northumberland located in Alnwick, Embleton & Seahouses. With an excellent diverse clinical team providing a good mix of male and female Partners, Salaried GP's, Physicians Associate, ANP's (Prescribing), Frailty Nurses, Practice Nurses, Nurse Associates and HCA's. We have named Practice Leads covering a number of clinical and operational specialisms.

As a dispensing practice we also have a large pharmacy team consisting of: Prescribing and Dispensing Manager, Pharmacists, Pharmacy Technicians, Pharmacy Admin and Dispensers. Our PCN ARRS roles include: FCP's, Pharmacists, Pharmacy Technicians, GP Link Workers, Health & Wellbeing Coaches, Mental Health workers, Care Coordinators and a Clinical Research Team.

We hold daily MDT's with social care attendance, clinical education sessions and our team have access to Blue Stream training software
